CHAPTER 5
第五章
Writing Words of Comfort
写下安慰的话语
C OMPOSING A COMFORTING PIECE of writing can be a sensitive and thoughtful process but can also, at times, be easier than speaking directly. When we write a letter or e-mail to someone in pain, we can take our time and reflect on what words we are choosing. Introverted people especially may find the gentle and private act of writing more meaningful. And indeed, a simple note written on a lovely card, perhaps with a soothing image on it, can serve as a keepsake for the person in need, providing them with comfort in the thick of their sadness and for years to come.
写一封慰藉人心的信可能是一个细腻而深思熟虑的过程，但有时也比直接倾诉更容易。当我们给身处痛苦中的人写信或发邮件时，我们可以慢慢斟酌，斟酌用词。内向的人尤其会发现，这种温柔而私密的写作方式更有意义。的确，一张写在精美卡片上的简单便条，或许配上舒缓的图片，就能成为需要帮助的人珍藏的纪念品，在他们最悲伤的时候给予他们慰藉，并在未来的日子里长久陪伴他们。
I have listed below an easy step-by-step guide to composing a comforting note or letter, be it for snail mail or e-mail. Most of these steps listed below apply to all kinds of comforting, not just for offering condolence for bereavement situations, but for supporting others at difficult times in general.
下面我列出了一份简单的分步指南，教你如何撰写慰问信或便条，无论是邮寄还是电子邮件。以下步骤大多适用于各种慰问场合，不仅适用于表达丧亲之痛，也适用于在他人遭遇困境时给予支持。
1. First, let the person know you have them on your mind.
“Since I heard the news, I’ve been thinking about you every day.”
1. 首先，让对方知道你一直惦记着他/她。“自从听到这个消息后，我每天都在想你。”
2. Next, let them know how you feel.
“It really took me by surprise at first, and now I feel so sad about your loss.”
2. 接下来，让他们知道你的感受。“一开始我真的非常震惊，现在我对你的遭遇感到非常难过。”
3. Then, ask how they are doing.
“I’ve been wondering how you were doing this past week especially.”
3. 然后，问问他们过得怎么样。“我一直很想知道你过去一周过得如何，尤其是这周。”
4. Let them know what you notice about any positive ways they are coping.
It’s often empowering for people in distress to have someone spot a strength or skill they are currently using, even at difficult times. As a friend, coworker, or family member, we might point out a particular quality to let them know we believe in them (though we would not want to dismiss their current level of pain and distress). “Carla, this might be the hardest time you have ever gone through, but I can’t help noticing how good you are about returning all those phone calls. I don’t know how you do it.”
4. 让他们知道你注意到他们有哪些积极的应对方式。对于身处困境的人来说，有人注意到他们正在发挥的优势或技能，即使是在艰难时刻，也会让他们感到鼓舞。作为朋友、同事或家人，我们可以指出他们身上的某个特质，让他们知道我们相信他们（当然，我们不会忽视他们当前的痛苦和困境）。“卡拉，这可能是你经历过的最艰难的时期，但我注意到你每次都能及时回复电话，做得非常好。我不知道你是怎么做到的。”
5. (For bereavement situations) If you knew the deceased, you can offer to share a memory about that person, or make a statement about what that person meant to you. Sharing briefly a significant moment of being with the deceased can help the griever feel a sense of continuity and connection with the people the deceased cared about. “Keith was one of the kindest people I ever met. Once he offered to call his former employer to help us locate a doctor for our daughter.”
5.（在丧亲的情况下）如果您认识逝者，您可以分享一段关于他的回忆，或者说说他/她对您意味着什么。简要地分享与逝者共度的重要时刻，可以帮助悲伤的人感受到与逝者所爱之人的联系和延续感。“基思是我见过的最善良的人之一。他曾经主动提出打电话给他以前的雇主，帮我们找一位能照顾我们女儿的医生。”
6. Express your desire to stay in touch and follow it up with a concrete offer of your time. Suggest a phone call, a visit, an invitation to an activity, or an e-mail to check in later.
“I would really like to be there for you in any way I can. Would you like to join me next week for lunch at Joe’s?”
6. 表达你想保持联系的意愿，并提出具体的行动方案。你可以建议打电话、拜访、邀请对方参加活动，或者之后发邮件问候一下。“我真的很想尽我所能帮助你。你下周想不想来乔家吃午饭？”
7. Stay in touch.
Your letter is only the first letter, the start of a comforting process. Keep writing and checking in, for many months or longer. Especially pay attention to anniversaries, holidays, and birthdays, as these are times when people need extra support. In my work facilitating grief support groups for sixteen years, a common lament I’ve heard from grieving people is the silence that ensues after the first few weeks of their loss. After getting dozens of sympathy cards, flowers, gifts, food, and letters of condolence, there is little follow-up by many well-wishers some months later. They seem to drop away and move on. Some bereaved people are particularly sensitive to the lack of inclusion in other people’s daily lives. This is why, when it comes to writing letters of condolence, we need to offer ways to stay connected and to keep sharing ourselves.
7. 保持联系。你的信只是第一封，是抚慰过程的开始。请持续写信、关心，持续数月甚至更久。尤其要关注周年纪念日、节假日和生日，因为这些时候人们最需要额外的支持。在我十六年来组织哀伤互助小组的工作中，我经常听到哀悼者抱怨，在失去亲人的最初几周之后，随之而来的是一片沉寂。在收到几十张慰问卡、鲜花、礼物、食物和唁电之后，几个月后，许多好心人却鲜少再来关心。他们似乎就此消失，继续过自己的生活。有些丧亲者对被他人冷落尤为敏感。因此，在写唁电时，我们需要提供一些保持联系、彼此倾诉的方式。
A Word of Caution
一句忠告
In writing a letter, as opposed to speaking with someone directly, we are given the opportunity to carefully review our words. Read and reread your letter or note to be sure that you have not inadvertently included any platitudes. In the previous chapter, I provided lists of commonly used platitudes and alternative things to say that will perhaps be more helpful to the person you wish to comfort. Many of these hold true for the written word as well, so you might want to review them on pages 111 to 113. Following are some platitudes that people tend to revert to in written communication in particular. Be careful to avoid:
与直接交谈不同，写信时我们有机会仔细斟酌用词。反复阅读你的信件或便条，确保没有无意中使用任何陈词滥调。在前一章中，我列举了一些常用的陈词滥调，以及一些可能更有助于安慰对方的替代说法。其中许多也适用于书面交流，因此你可能需要回顾一下第111页至113页的内容。以下是一些人们在书面交流中尤其容易脱口而出的陈词滥调。务必避免使用：

Including cheery upbeat news from your own life.
包括分享你生活中令人振奋的好消息。
It can be tempting to, in a “look on the bright side” vein, pad your letter with “positive” news from your life. Better to just focus on the person you’re writing to and the pain that they are going through.
出于“往好处想”的心态，你可能会忍不住在信里添油加醋地写一些自己生活中的“积极”消息。但最好还是把重点放在收信人身上，以及他们正在经历的痛苦上。
Instead, you might write: “It sounds like this might take a long time to get through.”
相反，你可以这样写：“听起来这件事可能需要很长时间才能解决。”

Assurance that you “understand” what he or she is going through.
向他/她保证你“理解”他或她正在经历的事情。
Instead, you might write: “Please feel free to write or call if you want to, because I honestly would like to know about your experiences.”
相反，你可以这样写：“如果你愿意，请随时来信或打电话，因为我真的很想了解你的经历。”

Writing “We all go through it” comments.
写下“我们都会经历这个阶段”的评论。
Instead, you might write: “With all you’ve gone through this year, your loss seems to come at a terrible time.”
相反，你可以这样写：“经历了今年这么多的苦难，你的损失似乎来得非常不是时候。”

Writing pages and pages of “helpful” thoughts and reflections about loss and grief.
写了好几页关于失去和悲伤的“有益”想法和反思。
Instead, it’s better to keep your letter one to two pages, with simple, personal, and genuine words. Usually grieving and distressed people are not able to focus on reading a lot of text at one time. Though soothing words of wisdom from a self-help book or from religious scripture may have helped you, these words might not be helpful in the raw stages of grief someone is enduring.
相反，最好将信件控制在一两页，用简洁、真诚、个人化的语言表达。通常，悲痛欲绝的人无法一次性集中精力阅读大量文字。虽然自助书籍或宗教经文中的一些抚慰人心的话语或许对你有所帮助，但这些话语在别人经历极度悲痛的阶段可能并无助益。
# ↩

Sharing Photos, Keepsakes, and Memories

分享照片、纪念品和回忆

Added to your letter, it can be heartening to send a photograph of a treasured moment, a card, an image, or a keepsake /souvenir from a favorite activity. A short poem, lines from a favorite song or book that the grieving person has shared with you in the past can be included, because what you have in common can be a comfort to that person.
在信中附上一张珍贵瞬间的照片、一张卡片、一张图片，或一件来自挚爱活动的纪念品，都会令人感到温暖。你还可以附上一首短诗、一首挚爱歌曲或一本书中的几句歌词，这些内容都是逝者生前与你分享过的，因为你们的共同经历或许能给逝者带来慰藉。
A Sample Letter, Sent Inside a Card—Supporting a Bereaved Friend
一封寄给丧亲朋友的信件范例（附在卡片内）
Dear Lynne,
亲爱的琳恩，
You have been on my mind a lot these days. How are you doing? It must be so hard living without Jamie. I wish I didn’t live 900 miles away, as I’d really like to see you. But for now, I was wondering if I could give you a call next Sunday afternoon, June 12th.
这些天我一直很想念你。你过得怎么样？没有杰米的日子一定很难熬。真希望我离你近一点，有900英里远，我真的很想见你。不过现在，我想问问你能不能下周日下午，也就是6月12日，给你打个电话。
Yesterday on the radio I heard a song by Cat Stevens, “Moonshadow,” and remembered how much Jamie loved that song back in 1972, when we all went to hockey camp. I remember how we sang “Moonshadow” together on one bright moonlit night, in that huge Buick station wagon when we drove back from camp. I was inspired, after hearing the song, to go through my albums in the attic, and thank goodness, I found this GREAT PIC of all of us at camp! I wanted to share this with you, and I hope this can be a keepsake for you.
昨天在广播里听到卡特·史蒂文斯的《月影》（Moonshadow），让我想起了1972年我们一起去参加冰球训练营时，杰米有多么喜欢这首歌。我记得在一个月光皎洁的夜晚，我们坐在那辆巨大的别克旅行车里，从训练营回来的路上，一起唱着《月影》。听完这首歌后，我受到启发，翻出了阁楼里的唱片，谢天谢地，我找到了这张我们所有人在训练营的合影！我想和你们分享，希望这张照片也能成为你们的珍贵回忆。
I have you in my prayers every night.
我每晚都会为你祈祷。
Love,
Annette
爱你的，安妮特
A Sample Short Note, Sent with Pink Roses—From a Husband to His Wife (during a painful wait for their child’s heart valve surgery and recovery)
一封丈夫写给妻子的简短便条，附赠粉红玫瑰——在他们痛苦等待孩子心脏瓣膜手术和康复期间
My Dear Emily,
我亲爱的艾米丽，
It’s strange using words to express what I feel sitting with you all these hours in this sterile hospital environment. I haven’t been able to find any decent words to comfort you. With these lovely roses, I want you to know what has been hard for me to say in the hospital—but here’s what my heart wants to say:
在这冰冷的医院里陪了你这么久，用语言来表达我的感受，感觉很奇怪。我找不到任何合适的词语来安慰你。我想用这些美丽的玫瑰花，让你知道我在医院里一直难以启齿的话——但我的心声是这样的：
You have been so patient with Julie, with the nurses, with the docs—and, mostly, with me. I know Julie feels your patience.
你对朱莉、护士、医生，尤其是对我，都非常有耐心。我知道朱莉感受到了你的耐心。
You have been so loving to Julie, to everyone, and me. I know Julie feels your love.
你一直对朱莉、对所有人，也对我，都非常关爱。我知道朱莉能感受到你的爱。
You have been so brave with Julie, with everyone, and especially with me. I know Julie feels your courage.
你对朱莉、对所有人，尤其是对我，都非常勇敢。我知道朱莉能感受到你的勇气。
I never cease to marvel at how beautiful you are.
我总是惊叹于你的美貌。
Let me hold your hand a little longer for this afternoon, until we get the final news.
今天下午，让我再多握一会儿你的手，直到我们得到最终消息。
Your adoring husband,
Matt
你深爱的丈夫，马特
# ↩

Electronic Comforting

电子舒适

These days, many of us send our comfort electronically. We e-mail our comfort to loved ones, friends, and colleagues. The exact words chosen are extremely important in our cyberworld of comforting, as we don’t have the facial expressions, voice intonations, eye contact, human touch, or even the tactile feel of our personal stationery or a beautiful card to express our comfort or condolence. On the other hand, electronic comforting allows those we wish to comfort to feel the immediate benefits of our act of reaching out to them.
如今，我们许多人选择通过电子方式传递慰问。我们会给亲人、朋友和同事发送电子邮件，表达慰问。在网络世界里，措辞的选择至关重要，因为我们无法像面对面交流那样，通过面部表情、语调、眼神交流、肢体接触，甚至无法触摸到手写的信纸或精美的卡片来表达慰问或哀悼。另一方面，电子慰问也能让那些我们想要安慰的人立刻感受到我们伸出援手的诚意。
Another benefit of electronic comforting is that we can follow and “stay close” to someone more easily—day by day or hour by hour—without intruding on their privacy (they can either chose to read our message or not, depending on how open they are feeling to our comfort). With a quick e-mail or text message we can:
• Check in with someone to let them know we have that person on our mind. “Been wondering about you . . .”
• Let them know we care about them. “As your friend (sister, nephew, fellow band member), I’ve stopped to think about what you’re going through this week, and what might be helpful.”
• Let them know we are feeling with them (empathy). “I’m sad to hear you have just gotten such rotten news. I’m home tonight, so I can call you if you like.”
• Gently follow their progress and offering our support. “I’m checking in again about how the meeting went with your brother . . . hope you landed on your feet.”
• Offer an “appointment” for more direct contact. “Would you like me to call you next weekend? If not, that’s fine—just letting you know I’m here.”
电子慰藉的另一个好处是，我们可以更轻松地关注并“陪伴”他人——无论一天还是一小时——而不会侵犯他们的隐私（他们可以选择是否阅读我们的信息，这取决于他们是否愿意接受我们的安慰）。只需一封电子邮件或短信，我们就可以：• 问候对方，让他们知道我们惦记着他们。“我一直在想你……”• 让他们知道我们关心他们。“作为你的朋友（姐妹、侄子、乐队成员），我一直在想你这周的经历，以及什么可能会对你有所帮助。”• 让他们知道我们感同身受（同理心）。“听到你刚刚得到这么糟糕的消息，我很难过。我今晚在家，如果你愿意，我可以给你打电话。”• 温和地关注他们的进展并提供支持。“我再次问候一下你和你哥哥的会面……希望你一切顺利。” • 提供一个“预约”以便更直接地联系。“您希望我下周末给您打电话吗？如果您不想，也没关系——只是想让您知道我一直都在。”
A Sample E-mail Letter—A Brother’s Support for a Bereaved Brother
一封电子邮件范例——兄弟对丧亲兄弟的支持
Lee,
李，
Last night, I had you on my mind. I was thinking about our meeting last month in Orlando, and wondered how things were going. From what you told me, it sounded like you had some rough weeks. I’m really glad to hear how the support group has helped you. I think it took a lot of guts to start going to that group. Considering you didn’t know anyone in the group, it seems you fit in pretty well. I imagine that being with people going through the same thing is empowering. But also, I guess, it could be a drag, too.
昨晚我一直在想你。我想起了上个月我们在奥兰多的会面，想知道你最近过得怎么样。听你这么说，感觉你那几周过得挺艰难的。很高兴听到互助小组对你有帮助。我觉得你鼓起勇气去参加那个小组需要很大的勇气。考虑到你之前一个都不认识，你现在融入得这么好，真是令人欣慰。我想，和经历相似的人在一起肯定能给人力量。不过，我想，有时候也可能挺累人的。
I was talking with my friend in Orlando, Martin, last week, and he invited you and me to come down this winter, on January 30, for some R and R while his friends are in town for a 20-year high school reunion.
上周我和我在奥兰多的朋友马丁聊天，他邀请你我今年冬天，也就是 1 月 30 日，去他那里放松一下，因为他的朋友们要来城里参加 20 周年高中同学聚会。
I’ll give you a call this coming Saturday morning and see if you can make this trip.
我会在下周六早上给你打电话，看看你能不能来这次旅行。
By the way, I found this amazing picture you took of a hawk a long time ago. You are pretty good with bird shots.
对了，我找到了你很久以前拍的一张很棒的鹰的照片。你拍鸟类照片真的很厉害。
Take care,
保重，
Tim
蒂姆
It’s important to emphasize that in our role as comforters, it’s better not to pressure the person in distress for a response. We might ask them a question, but also let them know they don’t have to answer it if it doesn’t feel right at the time. For example, we could say, “I’m concerned, but I realize you may not be able to get back to me yet. Just letting you know I’m standing by. Hope you take all the time you need.”
需要强调的是，作为安慰者，最好不要强迫处于困境中的人做出回应。我们可以问他们一些问题，但也要让他们知道，如果当时觉得不合适，他们不必回答。例如，我们可以说：“我很关心你，但我知道你可能暂时无法回复我。我随时都在。希望你慢慢来，别着急。”
It’s also good to show appreciation and humility if they share personal information about their progress (medically, emotionally, spiritually), and if they respond to our gentle offers of more contact (a phone call, a face-to-face visit).
如果他们分享有关他们病情进展（医疗、情感、精神方面）的个人信息，并且回应我们温和地提出的更多联系（电话、面对面拜访）的提议，我们也应该表示感谢和谦逊。
Here is a close friend reaching out to another after hearing she had a uterine biopsy in the past week.
这是一位好友在得知另一位好友上周做了子宫活检后，主动联系她的消息。

First e-mail, October 18, 10:05 a.m.:
Checking in to see how you’re doing since the biopsy. Sounds like it’ll take more days to get the results. Darn—what a wait! I’m there for you with all my heart!
第一封邮件，10月18日上午10:05：问候一下你活检后的情况。听起来还要过几天才能拿到结果。哎——真是煎熬！我会一直支持你的！
Second e-mail, October 18, noon:
I’m free tomorrow night after 7 p.m. if you want me to call you. Really would like to talk with you soon, if it’s okay with you. Always good to hear your voice.
第二封邮件，10月18日中午：如果你想让我给你打电话，我明天晚上7点以后有空。如果方便的话，我很想尽快和你聊聊。很高兴听到你的声音。
Third e-mail October 18, 1:15 p.m.:
Sorry we can’t talk tomorrow on phone—you’ve got a lot on your plate. I’ve got you in my prayers in the meantime.
第三封邮件，10月18日下午1:15：抱歉我们明天不能打电话——你有很多事要忙。这段时间我会为你祈祷。
Fourth e-mail, October 22, 6:32 p.m.:
Heard the biopsy results yet? I’ve got you on my mind and in my prayers.
第四封邮件，10月22日下午6:32：活检结果出来了吗？我一直惦记着你，为你祈祷。
Fifth e-mail, October 22, 8:02 p.m.:
Thanks for getting back tonight. So they want more tests? Sounds like more waiting—really sucks. If you feel up to it, we can talk tonight—up to 11.
第五封邮件，10月22日晚上8:02：谢谢你今晚回复。他们还要做更多检测？听起来又要等了——真糟糕。如果你觉得可以的话，我们今晚可以聊聊——最晚到11点。
Sixth e-mail (upon hearing the unfortunate news that the biopsy and tests revealed cancer), October 24, 5:12 p.m.:
What bad news. I know there is a lot to sink in. I am sending you a big hug with all my love. I’m standing by.
第六封邮件（得知活检和检查结果显示患有癌症的不幸消息后），10月24日下午5:12：真是个坏消息。我知道你需要时间消化。给你一个大大的拥抱，我爱你。我会一直陪着你。
Seventh e-mail, October 24, 6:00 p.m.:
Yes, love to talk with you tonight. 8 p.m.—great. Honored to be your friend at this awful time. Thanks for reaching out to me.
第七封邮件，10月24日下午6点：好的，今晚很乐意和你聊聊。晚上8点——太好了。在这个艰难的时刻能成为你的朋友，我感到非常荣幸。谢谢你联系我。
The friend is now willing to engage in a phone call with this comforter. Yes, the e-mailing has been softly persistent, and certainly not pushy. The e-mails have shown caring and affection, but not with expectations or demands for any news or personal information. We need to be balanced in our e-mails, as we “follow” people in a caring way, without hounding them for updates when they are already swamped in demanding or overwhelming circumstances.
这位朋友现在愿意和这位安慰者通电话了。是的，邮件沟通一直温和而坚持，绝非咄咄逼人。邮件中流露出关心和爱意，但并未期待或索要任何消息或个人信息。我们在发送邮件时需要保持平衡，以关心的方式“关注”他人，而不是在他们已经身处繁重或压力巨大的境地时，纠缠不休地追问近况。


T HOUGH IN OUR SOCIETY today we resort more frequently to electronic communication, we need to remember the written word is only one, very limited, way of offering our comfort. Best of all, a face-to-face encounter brings forth all of our communication abilities, and greatly enriches our comforting messages and heartfelt reassurance of being there for that person. People in distress dearly need our direct contact, sometimes our loving touch and affection. In short, texting our comfort, though helpful, cannot be a substitute for our more sensitive, gentle, and finely attuned nonverbal language of comforting. Humans are, after all, “hardwired” for softness from each other.
尽管如今我们越来越频繁地使用电子通讯，但我们必须记住，文字只是表达安慰的一种非常有限的方式。面对面的交流能充分发挥我们的沟通能力，极大地丰富我们安慰的信息，并让我们真切地感受到陪伴和支持。身处困境的人们迫切需要我们的直接联系，有时甚至需要我们充满爱意的抚触和关怀。简而言之，虽然发送短信表达安慰有所帮助，但它无法取代我们更敏感、更温柔、更细致入微的非语言安慰方式。毕竟，人类天生渴望彼此的温柔。
# ↩

PART THREE
第三部分
The Comfort of Art
艺术的慰藉
Inspiration from Healing in the Arts
从艺术疗愈中汲取灵感
# ↩

CHAPTER 6
第六章
Art as a Source of Comfort
艺术作为一种慰藉之源
# ↩

Introduction: When We Run Out of Comforting Words

引言：当我们无话可说时

W E’VE ALL HEARD THE SAYING “A picture is worth a thousand words.” When it comes to comforting, I’d say that art of any kind is worth a million words. Sometimes a beautiful photograph, the soft tones of a guitar, a joyous painting, or a tender scene in a movie can speak far more powerfully than any comforting words we might offer someone in need of our support.
我们都听过“一图胜千言”这句谚语。说到安慰，我认为任何形式的艺术都胜过百万言辞。有时，一张美丽的照片、一段柔和的吉他旋律、一幅欢快的画作，或是电影中一个温馨的场景，其力量远胜于我们能给予需要帮助的人的任何安慰之词。
One night, exhausted after a twelve-hour day of intense social work with clients, I plopped myself down on my sofa to watch the television reality show So You Think You Can Dance . That night, to my surprise, a couple brilliantly danced an emotional, poignant story about a woman with breast cancer and her loving partner. Having worked closely with cancer survivors over the years, and having recently lost a friend to this dreadful disease, I was deeply touched. And I was not alone in my feelings—the whole panel was in tears, as were many people in the audience and, I suspect, millions of viewers around the country. In just minutes, the dance had expressed all the raw and conflicted emotions, as well as the delicate, loving gestures between loved ones facing life-threatening illness. In the days following the broadcast, I was heartened to stumble across several articles and blogs—many of them written by cancer survivors and their loved ones—indicating just how many people had been touched, comforted, and amazed by this gift from the dancers and the choreographer. And this is what art can do—it can help us to both express for ourselves and share with others our thoughts and emotions around a difficult life experience.
一天晚上，在为客户进行了十二个小时紧张的社工工作后，我筋疲力尽地瘫倒在沙发上，准备观看电视真人秀节目《舞林争霸》。那天晚上，令我惊喜的是，一对舞伴精彩地演绎了一个感人至深的故事：一位身患乳腺癌的女士和她深爱的伴侣。多年来，我一直与癌症幸存者密切接触，最近又有一位朋友因这种可怕的疾病去世，我深受触动。我的感受并非孤例——评委们都热泪盈眶，现场观众也一样，我想，全国数百万的电视观众也同样如此。短短几分钟，这段舞蹈就淋漓尽致地展现了所有复杂而矛盾的情感，以及面对危及生命的疾病时，爱人之间那些细腻而充满爱意的举动。节目播出后的几天里，我偶然看到许多文章和博客——其中很多都是癌症幸存者及其亲友所写——这些都让我深受鼓舞，也让我看到了有多少人被舞者和编舞的这份礼物所感动、安慰和震撼。这就是艺术的作用——它可以帮助我们在经历艰难的人生经历时，表达自己的想法和情感，也可以与他人分享这些想法和情感。
When we witness an artistic creation that contains the agony as well as the joys of being human, it shows us that we are not alone. For example, a cancer survivor told me how blasting Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony into his bedroom had gotten him through the dark nights of his soul, as he joined with Beethoven’s soul through the eternal language of his music. I also know an injured veteran of the Iraq War who pulled through grueling physical therapy while listening to the gritty rap of Missy Elliott’s “Get Ur Freak On.” And I’ve heard three different depressed, suicidal men share with me how Andy’s “get busy living” determination in The Shawshank Redemption changed their lives.
当我们欣赏到一部既饱含人性苦乐又饱含人性喜悦的艺术作品时，它让我们意识到自己并不孤单。例如，一位癌症幸存者告诉我，贝多芬第九交响曲在他生命中最黑暗的夜晚陪伴他度过了难关，他通过音乐永恒的语言与贝多芬的灵魂相连。我还认识一位在伊拉克战争中受伤的老兵，他一边听着米西·艾莉特充满力量的说唱歌曲《Get Ur Freak On》，一边坚持完成了艰苦的康复治疗。此外，我还听过三位曾患有抑郁症甚至有自杀倾向的男士讲述，《肖申克的救赎》中安迪“努力生活”的决心如何改变了他们的人生。
# ↩

The Comfort of Being in an Audience

身处观众席的舒适感

One frigid day in January 2009, I sat in the warmth of my home reviewing my checking account balance, which seemed to be plummeting as fast as the temperature outside. It was -1 degree F and falling and the wind was rattling my window as the arctic air slapped hard across the rocky Maine landscape. Clients were late in their payments again , so I was late in paying my bills again , but I found myself sighing with a strangely comforting sense of connection with all the other people on the planet in the same boat. The nearly bankrupt country of Iceland had much in common with me this evening, as did the General Motors workers, the workers from England to Russia to Singapore, all feeling the pain. Alas, I quipped to myself, what doesn’t come around doesn’t go around—money, that is, for most of us. My trusty little heat monitor, half filled with propane, hummed steadfastly, noisily, keeping my studio apartment warm enough, as long as I wore my fleece top over my turtle-neck and jeans. At least I could pay my heating bill, but not much else.
2009年1月一个寒冷的冬日，我坐在温暖的家中查看银行账户余额，余额似乎正随着室外气温的骤降而飞速下降。气温是零下1华氏度，而且还在持续下降，凛冽的寒风拍打着窗户，仿佛北极的空气狠狠地拍打着缅因州嶙峋的岩石地貌。客户又一次拖欠了款项，所以我又一次逾期支付了账单。然而，我却不由自主地叹了口气，心中涌起一种奇特的慰藉，仿佛与地球上所有身处同样困境的人们产生了某种共鸣。今晚，濒临破产的冰岛与我有着诸多共同之处，通用汽车的工人们，以及从英国到俄罗斯再到新加坡的工人们，都感同身受，共同承受着这份痛苦。唉，我自嘲道，报应不爽——对我们大多数人来说，金钱就是如此。我那可靠的小型温度监测器，里面装着半罐丙烷，嗡嗡作响，稳稳地维持着我单身公寓的温暖——只要我穿着抓绒衫套在套头衫外面，再套上牛仔裤。至少我能付得起暖气费，但除此之外就没什么了。
Meanwhile, it was Golden Globe and Oscar season, and one of my great comforts, no matter how gloomy the weather, the economy, or my mood, was watching all the nominated films. Even with only twenty bucks to get me through a couple more days, and the matinee ticket meant living on rice and freezer-burned Lean Cuisines, movies were my soul food. I pulled on my boots, bundled up in winter wraps, heated up the car, scraped the ice off the windows, and headed down the interstate against the snow squall to the theater to lose myself in New Orleans, India, Germany, or San Francisco. For all the Oscar nominees, the lines were long and the theaters were packed.
与此同时，正值金球奖和奥斯卡颁奖季，无论天气多么糟糕，经济多么低迷，心情多么低落，观看所有提名影片都是我最大的慰藉之一。即便只剩下二十美元勉强撑过几天，即使买一张午场电影票意味着只能靠米饭和冻得发白的速食食品度日，电影依然是我的精神食粮。我穿上靴子，裹上厚厚的冬衣，打开暖气，刮掉车窗上的冰，顶着暴风雪沿着州际公路驶向影院，沉浸在新奥尔良、印度、德国或旧金山的奇幻世界中。所有奥斯卡提名影片的放映厅都人山人海，排起了长队。
As our economy grinded to a halt in the fall of 2008, going out to see movies quickly became a comforting activity for Americans, with box-office numbers increasing by 16 percent. In his article “Riveting Tales for Dark Days,” David Carr of The New York Times noted, “When people fear for their futures, they like to gather in a dark room and stare at a screen, holding hands against the gloom.”
2008年秋季，随着美国经济陷入停滞，看电影迅速成为美国人的慰藉，票房收入增长了16%。《纽约时报》的戴维·卡尔在其文章《黑暗日子里的引人入胜的故事》中指出：“当人们对未来感到恐惧时，他们喜欢聚集在黑暗的房间里，盯着屏幕，手牵着手驱散阴霾。”
Indeed, what else could drive people to leave their cozy homes on a dark winter’s evening to wait in line, huddling in the cold, to buy a movie ticket and then to sit humbly in the darkness with a bunch of strangers to witness someone else’s plight on-screen? There is something deeply familiar and comforting about being in a live audience as a story unfolds in a film, a play, or an opera. Being part of a chorus of laughs, sighs, gasps, and tears is a unifying event that brings us together in so many ways. We may never know who sat in the darkness with us, but for two hours, we rooted for our characters to triumph over their adversities, while putting our own adversities on hold.
的确，还有什么能驱使人们在寒冷的冬夜离开温暖的家，挤在寒风中排队买票，然后与一群陌生人一起，默默地坐在黑暗中，观看银幕上别人的遭遇呢？当电影、戏剧或歌剧的故事在现场展开时，身处观众席中，会有一种深深的熟悉感和慰藉感。加入到欢笑、叹息、惊叹和泪水的合唱中，这种体验将我们紧紧联系在一起，以各种方式将我们凝聚在一起。我们或许永远不会知道谁与我们一起坐在黑暗中，但在那两个小时里，我们为剧中人物战胜逆境而欢呼，同时也暂时搁置了自己的烦恼。
# ↩

Identifying with the Underdog

认同弱者

Of all the audiences I joined that winter, the one watching Slumdog Millionaire was the most animated and audibly responsive (both positively and negatively) of any I witnessed. A sea of curious New Englanders, we drifted together through the darkness into a balmy, colorful Mumbai. Along with the gasps, laughs, and hushed tension of a riveted audience, I harbored a hundred conflicting emotions and sensations running with the kids along train tracks, sewers, trash heaps, more trains, tunnels, the steps of the Taj Mahal, glitzy hotels, brothels, and humongous skyscrapers towering over ever more trains and bustling crowds. My circuits fast overloading, I could hardly breathe or think. Some scenes forced me to avert my eyes. Several audience members walked out. For those of us who hung on for the inspirational ending, we were treated to a joyous Bollywood dance, among even more trains. The audience broke into applause and cheers, and some hooted and gyrated in their seats. I marveled that these sensible, stoic New Englanders, more reserved than most Americans, had been so moved. People looked dazed, some exhausted, some smiling as they streamed out into the lobby. It had been an intense, rough ride, but most hardworking, hearty Mainers could identify with this gritty tale of a terribly deprived but extremely determined underdog.
那年冬天我参加过的所有电影放映会中，观看《贫民窟的百万富翁》的那场最为热闹，观众的反应也最为热烈（既有积极的，也有消极的）。一群好奇的新英格兰人，我们一起穿过黑暗，进入了温暖多彩的孟买。伴随着观众们屏息凝神时的惊叹、笑声和压抑的紧张，我内心也涌动着百种矛盾的情绪。我和孩子们一起奔跑在铁轨、下水道、垃圾堆、更多的火车、隧道、泰姬陵的台阶、金碧辉煌的酒店、妓院和高耸入云的摩天大楼之间，这些摩天大楼俯瞰着更多的火车和熙熙攘攘的人群。我的大脑迅速超负荷运转，几乎无法呼吸和思考。有些场景让我不得不移开视线。一些观众中途离场。而我们这些坚持到最后，看到励志结局的人，则欣赏到了一段欢快的宝莱坞舞蹈，周围依然是更多的火车。观众席爆发出热烈的掌声和欢呼声，有些人甚至在座位上欢呼雀跃，扭动身躯。我惊叹于这些理智、坚忍的新英格兰人，他们比大多数美国人都要内敛，竟然如此动容。人们神情恍惚，有些人疲惫不堪，有些人则面带微笑地涌出大厅。这真是一段紧张而艰辛的旅程，但大多数勤劳坚韧的缅因州人都能感同身受这个关于一个生活极其困苦却意志无比坚定的弱者的励志故事。
No matter where we live, who we pray to, or who we work for, it is extremely comforting to root for the underdog. We did it for Seabiscuit, the racehorse, winning for us during the Depression in the 1930s. We listened to Rin Tin Tin , the wonder-dog war hero, on the radio. We did it for Rocky in the late ’70s. We rooted for Erin Brockovich , Antwone Fisher , Billy Elliot, Andy in The Shawshank Redemption , the Whale Rider girl, and Johnny Cash in Walk the Line . Even our latest, coolest Star Trek featured an underdog Captain Kirk. Fiction or true story, they gave us hope, telling us, “Get busy living or get busy dying” ( The Shawshank Redemption ), “Jai Ho” ( Slumdog Millionaire ), to “boldly go where no man has gone before” ( Star Trek ). And of course, “No man is a failure who has friends” ( It’s a Wonderful Life ).
无论我们身在何处，信仰何人，为何人工作，支持弱者总能带来莫大的慰藉。我们曾为赛马“海饼干”（Seabiscuit）加油，它在20世纪30年代的大萧条时期为我们赢得了胜利。我们曾在广播里聆听过神奇的战犬“灵犬莱西”（Rin Tin Tin）的故事。我们曾在70年代末期为电影《洛奇》（Rocky）加油。我们曾为艾琳·布罗科维奇（Erin Brockovich）、安东尼·费舍尔（Antwone Fisher）、比利·艾略特（Billy Elliot）、《肖申克的救赎》中的安迪（Andy）、《鲸骑士》中的女孩以及《与歌同行》中的约翰尼·卡什（Johnny Cash）加油。就连我们最新、最酷炫的《星际迷航》也塑造了一个不屈不挠的柯克船长形象。无论是虚构的故事还是真实的历史，他们都给予我们希望，告诉我们“要么忙着活，要么忙着死”（《肖申克的救赎》），“Jai Ho”（《贫民窟的百万富翁》），以及“勇敢地去往前人未至之境”（《星际迷航》）。当然还有那句经典名言：“有朋友的人不算失败者”（《生活多美好》）。
When groups of us root and hoot together with hope, whether in a darkly lit theater, in front of a football game in a friend’s living room, or on Facebook, we give and exchange comfort with each other in enjoying the given art form, opening our hearts all the more in our sharing of the experience. This communal spirit of sharing our feelings and soulful expressions can carry us through bleak and frightening times, when stock markets plunge, when we lose jobs and homes, when we feel disconnected from our family members or from our own courage. No matter what is happening in our lives, the arts wait for us—a living spirit of hope and connection.
当我们一群人一起欢呼雀跃，满怀希望地呐喊助威时，无论是在灯光昏暗的剧院里，还是在朋友家的客厅里观看足球比赛，亦或是在网上，我们都在欣赏艺术的过程中彼此给予和交流慰藉，并在分享体验的过程中更加敞开心扉。这种分享感受和真情流露的社群精神，能够陪伴我们度过阴霾和恐惧的时刻，无论是股市暴跌，还是失去工作和家园，亦或是感到与家人或自身勇气脱节。无论生活如何变幻，艺术始终在等待着我们——它是希望和联结的鲜活力量。
# ↩

The Arts Teach Us How to Be Comforting

艺术教会我们如何给予安慰

Art calls us to stop, to pause and step out of our own personal dramas, and experience someone else’s life—vicariously. According to the Oxford Dictionary , the word vicarious means “experienced in the imagination through the feelings or actions of another person.” Art takes us through the ups and downs on someone else’s journey and, as such, invites us to feel the empathy that is so vital to good comforting. Well-told stories—be they told in a book, a movie, or a beautifully drawn landscape as seen through the eyes of the artist—teach us how to walk in someone else’s shoes, to identify with someone else’s challenges. When we allow ourselves to be moved by art, we are opening ourselves to being inspired and nurtured by a greater sense of humanity.
艺术召唤我们停下脚步，暂时放下自身的个人烦恼，去体验他人的生活——感同身受。牛津词典对“感同身受”（vicarious）一词的解释是“通过想象，感受他人的感受或行为”。艺术带领我们经历他人人生旅程中的起伏跌宕，从而激发我们去体会那种对抚慰人心至关重要的同理心。无论是书籍、电影，还是艺术家笔下描绘的美丽风景，精彩的故事都能教会我们如何设身处地，如何理解他人的困境。当我们允许自己被艺术所感动时，我们也敞开心扉，去感受更广阔的人性，并从中获得启发和滋养。
Another way that art can teach us comforting skills is through the scenes it so often depicts of human connection—be it a random act of caring, a merciful gesture, or a heartfelt, honest confession. One simple yet brilliant example of someone offering comfort to another is in the movie Little Miss Sunshine , when the little sister, Olive, goes to comfort her distraught teenage brother who has run off from the family and is sitting alone in an empty field. Little Olive walks softly toward him, then quietly sits down next to him and reaches her arm around his shoulders. She just holds him in silence, without trying to convince him to join the family. Quite soon, touched by her kindness and love, her brother feels better.
艺术教会我们抚慰人心的另一种方式，是通过它经常描绘的人际联结——无论是偶然的关怀、仁慈的举动，还是发自肺腑的坦诚告白。电影《阳光小美女》中就有一个简单却精妙的例子：妹妹奥利芙去安慰离家出走、独自坐在空旷田野里的哥哥。奥利芙轻柔地走向他，在他身边静静地坐下，伸出手臂环住他的肩膀。她只是默默地抱着他，没有试图劝他回到家人身边。很快，哥哥被她的善良和爱所感动，心情也好了很多。
One of my favorite lessons about the art of comforting was learned from the movie Leaving Normal . In this movie we witness a bold, honest friendship between two women radically different from each other. I was struck by their peculiar bonding when they each ranted about how hard life had been for them. They angrily brought up the “make lemonade out of lemons” platitude, then quickly tore it to shreds with “What happens when life only gives you shit ?” They pondered bitterly over what anyone could make out of shit, sans lemons, yet in all their bitterness, a sweet, soulful moment of connection suddenly occurs. Their mutual, fiery rage at the world actually burns away their fear of trusting and connecting with each other.
我最喜欢的关于安慰的艺术的教训之一，来自电影《离开正常生活》。在这部电影中，我们见证了两个性格迥异的女人之间一段勇敢而真诚的友谊。当她们各自抱怨生活有多么艰难时，她们之间那种奇特的联结深深打动了我。她们愤怒地提起“把柠檬榨成柠檬汁”这句老生常谈，然后又迅速地用一句“如果生活只给你一堆烂摊子怎么办？”将其撕得粉碎。她们苦涩地思考着，如果没有柠檬，人们还能从烂摊子里创造出什么，然而就在她们的苦涩之中，一个甜蜜而深刻的心灵联结突然出现。她们对这个世界共同的、炽热的愤怒，反而烧尽了彼此信任和建立联系的恐惧。
In short, art doesn’t only touch us and comfort us, it teaches us how to be comforting, as our softer skills are shaped by the finer languages of music, images, dreams, reflections, and stories.
简而言之，艺术不仅能触动我们、安慰我们，还能教会我们如何去安慰别人，因为我们更柔和的技能是由音乐、图像、梦境、反思和故事这些更精妙的语言塑造的。
# ↩

The Comfort of Sharing Art

分享艺术的慰藉

As comforters, there are times when we run out of words to say or activities to propose, to help lift someone we care about out of their pain. At these times it can be especially beneficial to instead sit back with the person we wish to comfort and take refuge in the wide world of art and entertainment. Here are a few ways we can share works of art together.
作为安慰者，有时我们会词穷，不知如何安慰或提议活动，才能帮助我们关心的人走出痛苦。此时，不妨静静地陪伴他们，沉浸在艺术和娱乐的世界中。以下是一些我们可以一起欣赏艺术作品的方式。
# ↩

JUST SITTING TOGETHER, SHARING ART AND ENTERTAINMENT

只是坐在一起，分享艺术和娱乐

Simply sitting together and watching a beloved television show or movie or listening to a favorite piece of music with someone can be a highly comforting activity. Our companionship, as long as we are focused and honestly engaged in what they choose to share, is a simple and powerful way to connect heart to heart with someone in pain. I’ve heard beautiful stories of comforters spending their last weeks with loved ones at the end of their lives, sitting at their bedside, just sharing art and entertainment together on DVDs, TV, and radio.
仅仅是和某人一起坐着，观看他们喜爱的电视节目或电影，或者聆听他们喜欢的音乐，就能带来极大的安慰。只要我们全神贯注，真诚地投入到他们选择分享的内容中，我们的陪伴就能成为一种简单而有力的方式，与正在经历痛苦的人进行心灵的交流。我曾听过许多感人的故事，一些陪伴者在亲人生命的最后几周里，坐在床边，一起通过DVD、电视和广播分享艺术和娱乐。
One well-known and moving true story involves a ten-year-old girl, Colby Curtin, who was dying of cancer and dearly wanted to see the movie Up before her time ran out on earth. The producers of the Pixar movie, when contacted at the last minute, quickly provided a DVD of Up for her to view from her bed, as she was too weak to see it in a theater. The child enjoyed the video, smiled while it played, and died soon afterward. Though she could not open her eyes, and could only listen to the movie, her family was able to share this last wish coming true for her in the nick of time. Her mother was deeply touched by the story of Up, and was glad to share it with her daughter. The images in the film of people going up into the sky with their balloons meant to her that Colby was going up to heaven, too.
一个广为人知且感人至深的真实故事讲述了十岁的科尔比·柯廷（Colby Curtin）的故事。她身患癌症，生命垂危，生前最大的愿望就是在生命终结前观看电影《飞屋环游记》（Up）。皮克斯动画工作室的制片方在最后一刻接到通知后，迅速提供了一张《飞屋环游记》的DVD，让她可以在病床上观看，因为她当时身体虚弱，无法去电影院。科尔比很喜欢这部电影，在观看过程中脸上露出了笑容，不久后便离开了人世。虽然她已经无法睁开双眼，只能听到电影的声音，但她的家人还是在最后一刻实现了她最后的愿望。科尔比的母亲被《飞屋环游记》的故事深深打动，很高兴能与女儿分享这部电影。影片中人们乘坐热气球升空的画面，在她看来，意味着科尔比也将升入天堂。
# ↩

RECORD A COMPILATION OF YOUR LOVED ONE’S FAVORITE TUNES

录制一张你爱人最喜欢的歌曲合辑

Many people have told me in support groups their best comforts have been gifts made by loved ones of thoughtful compilations of their favorite music. A survivor of lung cancer who was often exhausted dearly enjoyed a CD her son burned for her, with uplifting songs he selected for her “that reminded him of my journey.”
许多人在互助小组中告诉我，他们收到的最好的慰藉是亲人精心挑选的、包含他们最喜欢的音乐的合辑。一位肺癌幸存者经常感到疲惫不堪，她非常喜欢儿子为她刻录的一张CD，里面收录着儿子为她挑选的振奋人心的歌曲，“这些歌曲让他想起我的抗癌历程”。
She continues, “I play it when I need a boost of energy. But mostly it’s a great comfort to me, because I am still touched by how sweet he was to pick out my favorite singers and tunes. He remembered my old-timers like the Beatles, Stevie Nicks, and Randy Newman. I mean, the kid is only twenty, but he recorded music from The Point ! I still can’t believe how well he ‘gets’ me. It’s like he knew my soul well enough to find the music that makes me smile.”
她接着说：“我需要提神的时候就会听。但对我来说，它更多的是一种莫大的安慰，因为他能如此贴心地挑选出我最喜欢的歌手和歌曲，这让我至今仍然很感动。他还记得我喜欢的那些老歌，比如披头士乐队、史蒂薇·尼克斯和兰迪·纽曼。我的意思是，这孩子才二十岁，但他竟然录下了The Point的音乐！我到现在都难以置信他竟然这么了解我。他好像很懂我的灵魂，能找到那些让我微笑的音乐。”
# ↩

SCRAPBOOKING TOGETHER

一起做剪贴簿

Scrapbooking has quickly become a popular pastime recently. It is fun to collect old photos, memorabilia, little souvenirs (letters), and other images, and make beautiful pages to tell the stories of our loved one’s life. This can be done with our loved one or not, but it certainly is a gift that celebrates our loved one’s journey.
近年来，剪贴簿制作迅速成为一种流行的消遣方式。收集旧照片、纪念品、小物件（例如信件）和其他图片，制作精美的页面来讲述我们所爱之人的生平故事，是一件非常有趣的事情。制作剪贴簿可以和我们所爱之人一起完成，也可以独自完成，但这无疑是一份纪念他们人生旅程的礼物。
# ↩

READING AND RECITING POETRY, SONNETS, FAVORITE WRITINGS TOGETHER

一起阅读和朗诵诗歌、十四行诗和喜爱的作品

One of my colleagues, Pam Blunt, an arts therapist (later profiled in this section) shared a story with me about her mother’s last days of life that beautifully illustrates how art can bring people together:
“My mother loved the arts, and turned to them a great deal during the last year of her life. She found solace in poetry, literature, and music, a source of comfort and guidance for facing her grief after my father died, and her own illness and imminent death. During that time, she often spoke to me about how a poem or piece of music moved her and helped her understand some aspect of her experience. On one of the last nights we spent with her, my sister and I recorded her telling family stories from her life. We recited her favorite poems together, and we listened to Mozart. It was a sweet, intimate night spent with two women who are the most beloved to me in the world. Her last request to me was to recite Shakespeare’s Sonnet 116, as she lay dying: ‘Let me not to the marriage of true minds admit impediments. . . .’ I hope it was as powerful and comforting for her as it was for me.”
我的同事帕姆·布朗特是一位艺术治疗师（本节稍后会介绍她），她跟我分享了她母亲生命最后几天的故事，这个故事生动地展现了艺术如何将人们联系在一起：“我母亲热爱艺术，在她生命的最后一年里，她经常沉浸其中。诗歌、文学和音乐给了她慰藉，在父亲去世后，这些艺术为她提供了安慰和指引，帮助她面对自己的疾病和即将到来的死亡。在那段时间里，她经常跟我说，一首诗或一首乐曲如何触动了她，帮助她理解了自己经历的某些方面。在我们陪伴她的最后几个晚上之一，我和妹妹录下了她讲述的家庭故事。我们一起朗诵了她最喜欢的诗歌，还一起听了莫扎特的音乐。那是一个温馨而亲密的夜晚，我和两位我生命中最挚爱的女性共度时光。她临终前最后的请求是让我朗诵莎士比亚十四行诗第116首：‘愿我不要承认真爱结合的结合。’障碍……我希望它对她来说也像对我一样，充满力量和安慰。
# ↩

The Comfort of Creating Art for Others and with Others

为他人和与他人一起创作艺术的慰藉

Equally as comforting to the comforter and the one being comforted as appreciating art is the whole experience of creating art. And we don’t need to be artistically talented or gifted to enjoy the comfort of making things for or with our loved ones. The hands-on satisfaction of knitting, wood-working, photography, or home decorating are activities that naturally bring forth our unique creativity and innovation.
对于安慰者和被安慰者而言，欣赏艺术带来的慰藉与创作艺术的整个过程同样重要。我们无需具备艺术天赋或才能，也能享受为所爱之人或与他们一起制作物品的乐趣。编织、木工、摄影或家居装饰等亲手制作的乐趣，都能自然而然地激发我们独特的创造力和创新精神。
Channeling our human drive to express ourselves is comforting in itself. Singing (or ranting, as the case may be!) in the shower, ingeniously creating space in our closets, or doodling with our highlighters while our computer boots up—all of these simple creative acts can be satisfying outlets. In addition, our creations—be it our home-baked lasagna, herb sachets from our gardens, or a photo of ducks on a pond—can communicate our comfort in simple yet profound ways. Here are a few of the ways that we can use the creation of art to comfort others and ourselves:
• Grounds us, centers us
Whether we are sewing pillows, playing a flute, carving wood, or acting in a play, we step into the present moment, out of our heads and egos, uniting ourselves with what we are creating. We touch the fabric, or reach for the notes of the flute. We shape the wood, or play with our voice, all requiring our full attention, our step-by-step process, our time. Even when we are overwhelmed with problems, immersing ourselves in these activities takes us into a healing, grounding space, perhaps into the creative force of life itself.
• Connects us, tethers us
When we share our stories, our crafts, our music, our photos, or even our cooking, people are drawn out of themselves in the act of enjoyment, or by their sheer curiosity. The gift we have created, no matter how simple, brings us together, in many different ways—over the dinner table, over the pages, over the blogs, over the radio, over the audience. Even if people don’t always “get it” right away, most of them appreciate the action taken, the thoughtfulness, the effort.
• When we make things for others, we think “outside the box”
Something magical happens when our creation designed for another person has taken shape. It takes on a life of its own. It speaks to us, in its own way. Suddenly, our piece of art, what we thought was finished, morphs into something more, or something else. It asks for more from us. The pillows we made for our grandmother suddenly seem to look better on her bed than on her living room chairs, and before we know it, she asks us to make some more pillows for her chairs. She loves them so much, she wants your signature pillows in every room! We can make new pillows for her over the years for memorable occasions, such as her birthday, Christmas, her wedding anniversary, and many more opportunities. Pillow-making becomes a ritual of love, and we are challenged in a fun way to keep creating new designs. We step outside our box and become more creative than we think we really can be when people enjoy our comforting creations.
Art, any creation made for someone else, has a way of growing on them and on us, expanding beyond its original boundaries, asking us to stretch our imaginations. And when we reach with our minds and hearts to make art to comfort someone we care about, we are thinking outside the box of our own self-imposed limits and fears, and stepping into new areas and perspectives.
• Teaches us empathy, respect for others, comforting skills
Before I became a counselor, I taught drama and dance to children and teens for fifteen years, through the 1980s and into the mid-1990s. With the excitement of music, costume, props, and masks, the kids had a blast performing as Egyptians, Native Americans, Greek gods, Russians, runaway slaves, princesses, astronauts, explorers, cowboys, blind people, elderly people, homeless people.
Years later, I was delighted to hear from my students how the oral skills, movement skills, and teamwork skills were vital to their later success in communicating effectively as adults. But the most heartening news was that drama and dance had taught them the skills of empathy and respect for others, having walked in the shoes/sandals/ moccasins/boots of people in different cultures and backgrounds, as well as different eras. Becoming the people they were reading about or hearing about on TV had not only helped them understand other people better, it had made their world less scary and foreign. Acting and dance gave them the opportunity to portray through their characters the universal comforting traits of humor, kindness, wisdom, patience, empathy—timelessly comforting virtues in all cultures and classes.
• Helps us release emotions and heal
Sometimes the best way to zap a bad mood is to pound a drum, strike the right chords on a piano, or get embroiled in your character’s feisty dialogues in the novel you’re writing. You could even dance till you drop. Certainly, these are all more productive channels for raw emotions than starting arguments, joining in nasty snarkiness and gossip on a blog, punching holes in our cubicles, or yelling at our pets.
All the better to share the experience with someone who also needs a release—to paint a mural together or compose a short story together.
引导我们表达自我的本能本身就是一种慰藉。在淋浴时唱歌（或者咆哮，视情况而定！），巧妙地整理衣橱空间，或者在电脑启动时用荧光笔涂鸦——所有这些简单的创作行为都能成为令人满足的宣泄途径。此外，我们的作品——无论是自制的千层面、花园里的香草香囊，还是池塘里鸭子的照片——都能以简单而深刻的方式传递我们的慰藉。以下是一些我们可以利用艺术创作来慰藉他人和自己的方式：• 让我们脚踏实地，找到内心的平静。无论是缝制枕头、吹奏长笛、雕刻木头，还是表演戏剧，我们都会进入当下，放下思绪和自我，与我们正在创造的东西融为一体。我们触摸布料，或拨动长笛的音符。我们塑造木头，或吟唱，所有这些都需要我们全神贯注，一步一步地完成，投入时间。即使我们被各种问题压得喘不过气来，沉浸于这些活动中也能让我们进入一个疗愈、踏实的空间，或许还能让我们感受到生命本身的创造力。• 连接我们，凝聚我们 当我们分享我们的故事、手工艺品、音乐、照片，甚至是烹饪时，人们会在享受的过程中，或仅仅出于好奇，而放下自我。我们创造的礼物，无论多么简单，都能以各种方式将我们联系在一起——在餐桌旁、在书页间、在博客上、在广播里、在听众面前。即使人们并非总能立刻“理解”，他们中的大多数人也会欣赏我们的行动、我们的用心和我们的努力。• 当我们为他人创作时，我们会跳出思维定式 当我们为他人设计的作品成形时，奇妙的事情就会发生。它仿佛拥有了自己的生命。它以自己的方式与我们对话。突然间，我们原本以为已经完成的艺术作品，变成了某种更丰富的、或者别的东西。它向我们发出了更多的呼唤。我们为奶奶做的枕头，突然间似乎放在她的床上比放在客厅的椅子上更合适。没过多久，她就让我们再做一些枕头放在她的椅子上。她太喜欢这些枕头了，恨不得每个房间都摆上我们亲手制作的枕头！这些年来，我们可以为她制作新的枕头，作为她生日、圣诞节、结婚纪念日等各种值得纪念的日子的礼物。制作枕头成了一种充满爱意的仪式，我们也在以一种有趣的方式挑战自己，不断创造新的设计。当人们喜欢我们制作的这些温暖舒适的枕头时，我们便突破了思维定式，展现出远超我们想象的创造力。艺术，任何为他人创作的作品，都会在他们和我们身上生根发芽，超越最初的界限，激发我们无限的想象力。当我们用心创作，用艺术来慰藉我们所爱的人时，我们便突破了自我设限和恐惧的束缚，踏入了新的领域，获得了新的视角。 • 教会我们同理心、尊重他人和安慰他人的技巧。在我成为一名咨询师之前，我曾教授儿童和青少年戏剧和舞蹈长达十五年，从上世纪八十年代一直到九十年代中期。伴随着音乐、服装、道具和面具的兴奋，孩子们尽情地扮演着埃及人、美洲原住民、希腊诸神、俄罗斯人、逃亡奴隶、公主、宇航员、探险家、牛仔、盲人、老人和无家可归者。多年后，我很高兴地听到我的学生们说，口语表达能力、肢体动作能力和团队合作能力对他们日后作为成年人有效沟通至关重要。但最令人欣慰的是，戏剧和舞蹈教会了他们同理心和尊重他人的技巧，让他们有机会体验不同文化背景、不同时代人们的感受。成为他们从书本或电视上看到的人物，不仅帮助他们更好地理解他人，也让他们的世界不再那么可怕和陌生。表演和舞蹈让他们有机会通过角色展现幽默、善良、智慧、耐心和同理心这些普世的、令人感到慰藉的品质——这些美德在所有文化和阶层中都经久不衰。• 帮助我们释放情绪，疗愈身心。有时候，驱散坏心情的最好方法就是敲敲鼓，弹奏一曲动听的钢琴曲，或者沉浸在你正在创作的小说中，与笔下人物进行激烈的对话。你甚至可以跳舞跳到筋疲力尽。当然，这些都比挑起争端、在博客上参与恶毒的讽刺和八卦、在办公隔间上打洞或对宠物大吼大叫更能有效地释放真实的情绪。最好还能与同样需要释放情绪的人分享这种体验——一起画一幅壁画或共同创作一个短篇故事。

CHAPTER 7
第七章
The Healing Power of Art in Action
艺术的疗愈力量

Introducing Our Guides to the Arts of Comforting

隆重推出我们的《抚慰艺术指南》

F ROM MY EARLIER YEARS of teaching in the performing arts through my later career as a counselor, I’ve met dozens of inspirational colleagues and mentors applying the arts in the fields of education, psychotherapy, nursing, and community development. Their passion, energy, and vision for what they do year after year never ceases to amaze me. In the following pages I will introduce you to three of these master comforters, a storyteller, a ceramic artist, and an expressive-arts therapist.
从我早年从事表演艺术教学，到后来成为一名咨询师，我结识了数十位鼓舞人心的同事和导师，他们将艺术应用于教育、心理治疗、护理和社区发展等领域。他们年复一年对工作的热情、活力和远见卓识总是令我惊叹不已。在接下来的篇幅中，我将向您介绍其中三位艺术大师：一位故事讲述者、一位陶艺家和一位表达性艺术治疗师。
Our guides to the arts of comforting are vibrant, resourceful people with a reverence for the spark of creativity that dwells in all of us, and they use this energy to help people heal. These aren’t just talented artists and experts, well known and vital to their communities; they are genuinely comforting people at heart.
我们这些引领人们领略慰藉艺术的导师们充满活力、足智多谋，他们敬畏每个人心中都蕴藏的创造力火花，并运用这份能量帮助人们疗愈身心。他们不仅是才华横溢的艺术家和专家，在各自的社区中享有盛名，更是社区中不可或缺的人物；他们内心深处也真正充满着抚慰他人的热情。
