FINDING COMMON GROUND WITH STORIES

寻找故事中的共同点

Les Schaffer
莱斯·谢弗
Storyteller
故事讲述者
Cofounder and Director, Tell Tale Hearts Storytellers Theater, Richmond, Virginia
弗吉尼亚州里士满市“Tell Tale Hearts Storytellers Theater”联合创始人兼导演
No matter what we’ve been through, or what we’ve lost, we always have a story left to tell.
无论我们经历过什么，或者失去了什么，我们总会有故事可讲。
Core Comforting Qualities: Wisdom and Humility
核心的安慰品质：智慧与谦逊
A natural-born storyteller, and cofounder of the Tell Tale Hearts Storytellers Theater in Richmond, Les Schaffer takes his audiences through the twists and turns of his adventures and misadventures with humor, intrigue, and tenderness. Les travels throughout Virginia with his troupe, performing for a wide range of audiences at festivals, retreat centers, addiction treatment programs, nursing homes, schools, colleges, community centers, and libraries, and everywhere he goes his audiences hoot with laughter. Les always lives up to his signature quote, “All my stories are true, even the ones I make up.”
莱斯·沙弗是一位天生的讲故事高手，也是里士满“倾诉衷肠”故事剧团的联合创始人。他以幽默、引人入胜又饱含温情的方式，带领观众体验他跌宕起伏的冒险经历。莱斯带着他的剧团在弗吉尼亚州各地巡回演出，为各种各样的观众献上精彩表演，演出地点包括节日庆典、静修中心、戒瘾治疗中心、养老院、学校、大学、社区中心和图书馆。无论走到哪里，他的表演都能引得观众捧腹大笑。莱斯始终践行着他的名言：“我所有的故事都是真的，即使是我编造的。”
Les derives his wisdom and passion for storytelling from his long, rich career as a family and children’s counselor. For more than twenty years in a community mental health center, Les used storytelling as a therapeutic tool to resolve family conflict. Les encouraged children and parents to pick their favorite characters with whom they most identified and to act as if they were that character being confronted with a situation or situations similar to that of their own. Using this creative play therapy, Les’s clients were able to explore the consequences of their character’s choices and behaviors and, ultimately, search for solutions to their real-life problems.
莱斯对讲故事的热情和智慧源于他多年丰富的家庭和儿童咨询师经验。在社区心理健康中心工作的二十多年里，莱斯一直运用讲故事这种治疗手段来解决家庭冲突。他鼓励孩子和家长选择自己最认同的角色，并扮演角色，面对与自身经历相似的情境。通过这种富有创意的游戏疗法，莱斯的来访者能够探索角色选择和行为的后果，并最终找到解决现实生活问题的方案。
Les was so convinced and inspired by the healing power of storytelling that he cofounded the Tell Tale Hearts Storytellers Theater in 1999. Drawing on his extensive experience utilizing storytelling within a therapeutic environment, Les now carefully chooses and adapts the best stories to meet the specialized needs of his audience. He improvises easily with them, inviting them to participate out loud, as he flexes his lines and gestures to respond to their impromptu requests. More than a performer and theater director, Les facilitates healing events, drawing forth the creativity, courage, and compassion of his audiences as they observe and join in his stories.
莱斯深信故事的疗愈力量，并深受启发，于1999年与人共同创立了“倾诉心声”故事剧团。凭借在治疗环境中运用故事的丰富经验，莱斯如今精心挑选并改编最能满足观众特定需求的故事。他能轻松地与观众互动，邀请他们大声参与，并灵活调整台词和肢体语言来回应他们的即兴要求。莱斯不仅是一位表演者和戏剧导演，更是一位疗愈活动的推动者，他引导观众在聆听和参与故事的过程中，激发他们的创造力、勇气和同情心。


I ’VE SAT DOWN WITH LES many times over the past few years to talk about the healing power of storytelling, and about how being a storyteller has helped him heal from his own battle with prostate cancer.
在过去的几年里，我曾多次与莱斯坐下来谈论讲故事的治愈力量，以及讲故事如何帮助他从与前列腺癌的斗争中恢复过来。
According to Les, we can derive a great deal of comfort from telling our stories about the most difficult and challenging aspects of our lives. This is because when we tell a story about a painful experience it forces us to reach for some kind of narrative, to offer a sequence of events—beginning, middle, and end. We might stutter, or repeat ourselves, grasp awkwardly for the right words, meander, and pause, but good listeners, good comforters, don’t mind that at all. They follow us quietly as we find the words to describe how our journey unfolded and, ultimately, what meaning we take from it by way of a conclusion. And suddenly, our story told—our pain shared—some of the weight of the world is lifted off our shoulders.
莱斯认为，讲述我们生活中最艰难、最具挑战性的经历，能让我们获得极大的慰藉。这是因为，当我们讲述一段痛苦的经历时，它会迫使我们去构建某种叙事，呈现事件的顺序——开头、中间和结尾。我们可能会结结巴巴，重复自己，笨拙地寻找合适的词语，语无伦次，停顿片刻，但好的倾听者，好的安慰者，完全不会介意这些。他们会静静地陪伴我们，直到我们找到合适的词语来描述我们的人生旅程是如何展开的，以及最终我们从中领悟到的意义。突然间，我们的故事讲完了——我们的痛苦被分担了——肩上的重担也随之卸了下来。
Les says, “Every day I witness the ways stories connect us. Even with just a few sentences, storytelling is an antidote to isolation. I’ve seen the most devastated people find connection and a sense of belonging by joining with others to tell their stories.”
莱斯说：“我每天都能亲眼见证故事如何将我们联系在一起。即使只是寥寥数语，讲故事也能成为对抗孤独的良药。我见过许多最痛苦的人，通过与他人分享故事，找到了彼此的联系和归属感。”
Les shares his own account of the power of storytelling in facing his diagnosis of moderately advanced prostate cancer in 2005. “I was scared and felt terribly isolated. Nothing comforted me until I was able to hear another older man tell me his cancer survival story. I could have searched the Internet for advice, seen a hundred doctors, gotten the best treatment in the world, but having a regular guy tell me his story of how he faced his illness was the most comforting thing I encountered.”
莱斯分享了他自己在2005年被诊断出患有中晚期前列腺癌时，通过讲故事所获得的力量。“我当时很害怕，感觉非常孤立无援。直到我听到另一位老人讲述他战胜癌症的故事，我才感到一丝安慰。我本可以上网搜索建议，看上百位医生，接受世界上最好的治疗，但一个普通人讲述他如何面对疾病的故事，却是我遇到的最令人感到安慰的事情。”
Les marveled at how this ordinary man’s story about battling cancer changed his life.
莱斯惊叹于这个普通人与癌症抗争的故事如何改变了他的人生。
“The chord he struck in me was that it was okay to be scared, downright petrified—scared to the point of paralysis. This guy’s fear totally shut him down. In agonizing detail, he told me how it took him all day to get up the guts to phone the doctor for an appointment, after not sleeping the night before. Just hearing about these minute-by-minute and day-to-day dilemmas of dealing with gripping fear unlocked me from feeling so isolated and ashamed of my own fear. Facing cancer as a man, afraid of my own cowardice as much as the cancer itself, I was so relieved to find how much I had in common with another man I admired. His story gave me common ground to stand on for braving this strange new world of life-threatening illness.”
“他触动了我内心最深的一点：害怕是正常的，哪怕是吓得魂飞魄散——害怕到几乎瘫痪。这个人被恐惧彻底击垮了。他痛苦地告诉我，前一天晚上彻夜未眠，第二天却鼓起勇气打电话给医生预约，整个过程耗费了整整一天的时间。仅仅是听到他讲述这些与恐惧抗争的每一分每一秒、每一天的困境，就让我不再感到孤立无援，也不再为自己的恐惧感到羞愧。作为一个男人，面对癌症，我既害怕癌症本身，也害怕自己的懦弱。当我发现自己与一位我敬佩的男人如此相似时，我感到无比欣慰。他的故事给了我一个共同的立足点，让我能够勇敢地面对这个充满致命疾病的陌生世界。”
Les outlines this man’s story to demonstrate four ways in which stories comfort us:
1. Stories connect us. After the frightening news of having cancer, an older man telling me about how he first reacted to his diagnosis reassured me I was not alone in feeling so afraid. Stories alleviate our isolation.
2. Stories teach us survival skills, especially how to face adversity. When I talked with this cancer survivor about how he handled his chemo sessions, I was better informed and more prepared to face my treatment. Stories teach survival skills on many levels, socially, financially, physically, spiritually, morally.
3. Stories inspire us. This kind man shared his spiritual journey with me, and how facing his own mortality made him more compassionate and grateful for his life. Stories spark what moves and motivates us.
4. Stories reveal and clarify issues for us. When I heard this man describe how he procrastinated making phone calls for his medical appointments, it opened my eyes to what fear was doing to me. This alerted me to how much more support I needed to get for myself. Whenever we tell a story, we weave together the fragments and pieces of our lives into patterns, themes, directions. Stories give our experiences structure, meaning, and closure, even those experiences that had once seemed insignificant or obstructive. More than just venting, we can usually recognize a message in our narrative that rings true for us. The message of a story will keep us going. And better still, we can share the wisdom of our stories with others.
莱斯讲述了这个人的故事，以此说明故事如何以四种方式安慰我们：1. 故事将我们联系在一起。得知自己患癌的噩耗后，一位老人向我讲述了他最初得知诊断结果时的反应，这让我感到安心，因为我并不孤单，很多人都和我一样感到恐惧。故事减轻了我们的孤独感。2. 故事教会我们生存技能，尤其是如何面对逆境。当我与这位癌症幸存者交谈，了解他如何应对化疗时，我得到了更多信息，也为自己的治疗做好了更充分的准备。故事在社交、经济、身体、精神和道德等多个层面教会我们生存技能。3. 故事激励我们。这位善良的老人与我分享了他的精神之旅，以及直面死亡如何让他变得更加富有同情心，并对生命充满感恩。故事激发了我们内心深处的情感和动力。4. 故事揭示并澄清我们的问题。当我听到这位老人讲述他如何拖延预约就诊的电话时，我意识到恐惧对我的影响有多大。这让我意识到我需要为自己争取更多的支持。每当我们讲述故事时，我们都会将生活中的碎片编织成模式、主题和方向。故事赋予我们的经历以结构、意义和圆满，即使是那些曾经看似无关紧要或阻碍我们前行的经历。故事不仅仅是发泄情绪，我们通常还能从中找到与自身产生共鸣的信息。故事的信息会激励我们继续前行。更重要的是，我们还可以与他人分享故事中的智慧。
Les wonders how he would have fared in his recovery from cancer without Tell Tale Hearts and all that his experiences with his troupe and his audiences have taught him. “I bet that doing what I love doing, and loving the people I love has kept me going this strong for so long.”
莱斯不禁思考，如果没有《泄密的心》这部剧，如果没有与剧团成员和观众们相处的点点滴滴，他的癌症康复之路会是怎样一番景象。“我敢肯定，正是做着我热爱的事，爱着我爱的人，才让我能够如此坚强地走下去。”

Les’s Suggestions for Families or Other Groups to Inspire Storytelling
莱斯给家庭或其他团体提出的激发讲故事灵感的建议
One evening, while enjoying a Mediterranean meal with hummus, tapas, falafel, and colorful veggies spread across our table, Les and I brainstormed on the ways that families could use storytelling to create simple, comforting moments together.
一天晚上，我和莱斯一边享用着地中海美食——桌上摆满了鹰嘴豆泥、西班牙小吃、沙拉三明治和五彩缤纷的蔬菜——一边集思广益，探讨家庭如何利用讲故事来创造简单、温馨的团聚时光。
• Create movie theme nights
Most people need props, “conversation pieces,” or ice-breakers before the stories they might like to share start percolating. Movies, TV shows, games, sports, party food, music, holiday cooking, and craft activities are highly popular ways to get people in the mood for telling stories about their lives. Once the group has enjoyed the entertainment, elect a “moderator” to then steer the conversation toward storytelling. Following are some ideas for how this might be done using television show and movies:
Star Trek episodes can serve as a launching point for stories about adventures in strange new worlds—how we navigated environments or situations that were new to us.
Old classics with Buster Keaton, Charlie Chaplin, Laurel and Hardy, and the Three Stooges might inspire us to talk about the humor in painful experiences.
Diva nights with movies celebrating strong women will naturally inspire groups of women to talk about difficult moments in their lives when they discovered that they were much stronger than they thought. Superhero movies like Spider-Man or Batman can have a similar effect on young boys in terms of bringing forth stories of discovering untapped “special powers.”
• 举办电影主题之夜 大多数人在开始分享故事之前，都需要一些道具、“话题”或破冰活动。电影、电视节目、游戏、体育运动、派对美食、音乐、节日烹饪和手工活动都是非常受欢迎的方式，可以激发人们讲述自己生活故事的热情。在大家享受完娱乐活动后，可以选出一位“主持人”来引导谈话，让大家聊聊故事。以下是一些利用电视节目和电影进行此类活动的建议：《星际迷航》剧集可以作为讲述在陌生新世界冒险故事的起点——讲述我们如何应对全新的环境或情况。巴斯特·基顿、查理·卓别林、劳雷尔与哈迪以及三傻的经典老电影或许能启发我们谈论痛苦经历中的幽默。以歌颂坚强女性的电影为主题的“女主角之夜”自然会激发女性群体谈论她们人生中的艰难时刻，以及她们如何发现自己比想象中更加坚强。像蜘蛛侠或蝙蝠侠这样的超级英雄电影，对年轻男孩来说，在讲述发现自身未开发的“特殊能力”的故事方面，可能会产生类似的影响。
• Read stories to children.
Stories teach children how to deal with adversity in all areas of life. Kids are comforted when another kid or animal protagonist in a story figures out how to resolve a big problem.
In “Hansel and Gretel,” the children learn the rewards of resourcefulness in leaving bread crumbs along their path.
In Alexander and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Very Bad Day , we learn the world doesn’t fall apart when things are going badly.
In “The Three Little Pigs,” we learn how the pigs outsmart the big bad wolf. We can solve problems, even at scary times, with a bit of ingenuity and drive.
In “The Frog Prince,” we learn not to base decisions on appearances, or we might miss a wonderful surprise.
• 给孩子们讲故事。故事能教会孩子们如何应对生活中各个方面的逆境。当故事中的其他孩子或动物主角想办法解决大问题时，孩子们会感到安慰。在《汉塞尔与格蕾特》中，孩子们学会了在路上留下面包屑的机智带来的回报。在《亚历山大和他糟糕透顶的一天》中，我们明白即使事情进展不顺，世界也不会崩溃。在《三只小猪》中，我们学会了小猪们如何智胜大灰狼。即使在可怕的时刻，只要有点智慧和动力，我们也能解决问题。在《青蛙王子》中，我们学会了不要以貌取人，否则可能会错过美好的惊喜。
• Get together to listen to elder family members tell their stories of how they survived. For example, when we listen to our grandparents tell us how they survived during the Depression of the 1930s, we might learn ways to cope with our struggling economy in 2009.
Do special things at dinnertime like lighting a candle to signal that tonight you will linger longer at the table and honor your time together more. At the end of a long day, a family or group dinner can be a wonderful way to connect and tell stories about our days or our lives in general.
• 聚在一起，聆听长辈讲述他们如何度过难关的故事。例如，当我们聆听祖父母讲述他们在20世纪30年代大萧条时期是如何生存下来的，或许能从中汲取应对2009年经济困境的方法。晚餐时可以做一些特别的事情，比如点燃一支蜡烛，象征着今晚你们会在餐桌旁多待一会儿，更加珍惜彼此相聚的时光。漫长的一天结束后，与家人或朋友共进晚餐，是增进感情、分享彼此一天经历或人生故事的绝佳方式。
• Create special celebrations. Why wait for official holidays to sit down and reconnect with your loved ones? Instead, create occasions to celebrate accomplishments (getting A’s on a report card or passing a tough exam; Mom’s new look with a bold haircut; a friend’s graduation). Bake cookies, make garlands, make banners, blow up balloons, hand out wacky little party favors or souvenirs, read riddles out loud. Create special new spaces in which you can exchange stories about proud moments in your lives.
• 创造特别的庆祝活动。为什么非要等到法定假日才和亲朋好友坐下来好好聚聚呢？不如创造一些机会来庆祝成就（比如成绩单上得了A，或者通过了一场艰难的考试；妈妈剪了个新发型，焕然一新；朋友毕业）。烤饼干、做花环、制作横幅、吹气球、分发一些有趣的小礼物或纪念品、大声朗读谜语。创造一些特别的空间，让你们可以分享彼此生活中值得骄傲的时刻。
• Start a book club or a discussion group (salon).
Is there anything better than a good book to elicit stories from each other in a group? After general discussion of the given book, make time for the group to tell stories connected to the themes the book introduced.
• 成立读书俱乐部或讨论小组（沙龙）。还有什么比一本好书更能激发小组成员分享彼此的故事呢？在对指定书籍进行一般性讨论之后，留出时间让小组成员讲述与书中主题相关的个人故事。
# ↩

GRACIOUSNESS UNDER PRESSURE

压力下的优雅

Amy Handy
艾米·汉迪
Artist, Writer, Editor
艺术家、作家、编辑
Owner, Clay Play, Yarmouth, Maine
缅因州雅茅斯 Clay Play 工作室老板
People are so afraid of doing things wrong when they try something new. I love telling people “There is no wrong way to do this” when they make pottery with us. Being gracious is essential for people to feel safe here.
人们尝试新事物时总是害怕出错。我喜欢告诉和我们一起做陶艺的人“做这件事没有对错之分”。待人友善是让人们在这里感到安全的重要因素。
Core Comforting Qualities: Warmth and Graciousness
核心舒适特质：温暖和优雅
What’s comforting on a restless Saturday afternoon in snowy Yarmouth, Maine, when the kids are running high cabin fevers and you’ve run out of things to do? Head to Clay Play, where owner Amy Handy beckons people to explore their own curiosity and wonder while their clay creations take shape.
在缅因州雅茅斯一个百无聊赖的周六下午，孩子们在屋里待得焦躁不安，而你又无事可做，这时什么能让你感到慰藉呢？那就去“黏土乐园”（Clay Play）吧，店主艾米·汉迪（Amy Handy）热情地邀请人们在黏土作品成型的过程中，探索自己的好奇心和想象力。
One cold December day I visited Clay Play and found Amy rotating between the many tables, periodically running to the back of the store to grab fresh supplies or to check on the kiln. Radiating graciousness under pressure, she smiles the whole time, chatting easily with staff and customers.
十二月一个寒冷的冬日，我拜访了陶艺工作室Clay Play，发现艾米在众多桌子间穿梭，不时跑到店后去取新的材料或查看窑炉的情况。尽管压力重重，她依然保持着优雅的风度，始终面带微笑，轻松地与店员和顾客交谈。
I listen to a delightful cacophony of voices across the busy tables, as people of all ages converse while working on their pieces. Grown-ups catch up on who’s doing what in their lives. An eight-year-old boy talks excitedly about the gift he is making. “This is for my Grandma’s birthday. She loves apples, so I’m painting bright red apples all over this cup.” Family members visiting from out of town catch up with their host relatives as they all paint mugs together. Children share stories about favorite characters from books, movies, and TV, as the grown-ups listen and comment. Wizards, fairies, cartoon characters are painted on plates and trays. Elders share recollections about favorite objects and keepsakes, triggered by the pieces they are creating.
我聆听着熙熙攘攘的餐桌间此起彼伏的嘈杂声，各个年龄段的人们一边创作一边交谈。大人们互相问候近况。一个八岁的小男孩兴奋地谈论着他正在制作的礼物：“这是送给我奶奶的生日礼物。她喜欢苹果，所以我要在杯子上画满鲜红的苹果。” 外地来的亲友们一边和接待他们的亲戚聊天，一边一起绘制马克杯。孩子们分享着他们最喜欢的书本、电影和电视角色，大人们则在一旁聆听和评论。盘子和托盘上绘满了巫师、仙女和卡通人物。老人们在创作的过程中，回忆起自己珍藏的物品和纪念品。
I met Amy at a “newcomers club” when I first moved to Maine ten years ago. Amy quickly put me at ease by introducing me to the smiling women sitting next to her, as well as her daughter, Veronica, a toddler who was enjoying the chatter and attention around her. Over the years, she invited me to speak for the club’s monthly events, and after the event we’d relax over a late dinner, absorbed in fascinating conversations about the healing power of art.
十年前我刚搬到缅因州时，在一个“新移民俱乐部”认识了艾米。她很快就让我放松下来，把我介绍给了坐在她旁边笑容满面的女士们，还有她蹒跚学步的女儿维罗妮卡。维罗妮卡当时还是个蹒跚学步的孩子，正享受着周围的谈笑风生和大家的关注。这些年来，她邀请我到俱乐部的月度活动上发言。活动结束后，我们会一起享用一顿丰盛的晚餐，沉浸在关于艺术疗愈力量的精彩对话中。
Amy, her husband, and her older daughter, Julia, moved from New York to Maine just a few years before I arrived. We both loved Yarmouth and the greater Portland area, finding plenty of artistic and enterprising people in small, vibrant communities along the coast.
艾米和她的丈夫以及大女儿朱莉娅在我到达缅因州前几年从纽约搬到了这里。我们都很喜欢雅茅斯和波特兰周边地区，在沿海那些充满活力的小社区里，我们发现了很多富有艺术气息和进取心的人。
For more than twenty years, Amy has been an editor of art, craft, and design books, and has worked with Amazon.com and Abbeville Press. She is the author of several books, including American Castles: A Pictorial History . Before becoming a book editor, she was a production manager for the costume house Eaves-Brooks in New York City. In addition to her editing work, she has designed and produced costumes for Ogunquit Playhouse and served as props coordinator for the Portland Stage Company in Maine.
二十多年来，艾米一直从事艺术、工艺和设计类书籍的编辑工作，曾与亚马逊和阿贝维尔出版社合作。她著有多部书籍，其中包括《美国城堡：图文历史》。在成为图书编辑之前，她曾担任纽约市伊夫斯-布鲁克斯服装公司的制作经理。除了编辑工作之外，她还曾为奥甘奎特剧院设计和制作服装，并担任缅因州波特兰舞台剧团的道具协调员。
Amy goes with the flow better than anyone I’ve ever met. Extremely imaginative and resourceful, she can improvise with anything tossed her way: too many customers, too few customers, pushy customers, crying toddlers, paint spills across the floor, pottery dropped on the floor, fighting siblings, lost wallets, tired and complaining moms. If necessity is the mother of invention, then, for Amy, necessity is the mother of creative genius.
艾米是我见过最能随机应变的人。她极富想象力，足智多谋，无论遇到什么情况都能随机应变：顾客太多、顾客太少、咄咄逼人的顾客、哭闹的幼儿、洒在地上的颜料、掉在地上的陶器、打架的兄弟姐妹、丢失的钱包、疲惫不堪又抱怨连连的妈妈们。如果说需要是发明之母，那么对艾米来说，需要就是创造力的源泉。
Amy’s passion and joy bursts forth when she speaks about the comfort of making crafts. According to Amy, “Making things with our hands is comforting— period . It’s truly comforting to feel different textures and shape things with our hands, whether we’re quilting, sewing, weaving baskets, decorating wreaths, baking, playing with clay, planting seeds, scrapbooking, or knitting.”
艾米谈起手工制作带来的慰藉时，她的热情和喜悦溢于言表。艾米说：“用双手做东西会让人感到慰藉——就这么简单。无论是做拼布、缝纫、编织篮子、装饰花环、烘焙、玩泥巴、播种、制作剪贴簿还是编织，用双手感受不同的质地、塑造形状，都真的让人感到无比舒适。”
Amy has been particularly impressed with how teenagers interact with one another while doing hands-on art activities—when they can get away from texting for a while! “I love watching how relaxed and friendly teenagers can be with each other when they are painting pottery at a table together. Girls seem to enjoy making gifts for each other, particularly when they are first getting to know each other. This helps develop their relationships and push past the peer pressure to fit in.”
艾米对青少年们在进行动手艺术活动时的互动印象尤为深刻——当他们能暂时放下手机时，这种互动就显得尤为珍贵！“我喜欢看青少年们一起在桌边画陶器时那种轻松友好的氛围。女孩们似乎很喜欢互赠礼物，尤其是在刚认识的时候。这有助于她们发展彼此的关系，并克服同辈压力，更好地融入群体。”
It is Amy’s hope that through her work at Clay Play she can help to restore a highly comforting time in our past when the creation of crafts grounded and connected us.
艾米希望通过她在 Clay Play 的工作，能够帮助人们重拾过去那段令人倍感慰藉的时光，那时手工艺品的创作让我们脚踏实地，彼此相连。
“People are hungry for hands-on activities, especially group activities, many of which have been lost in our contemporary society. But these lost arts are being restored. As an editor of craft books for the past twenty years, I’ve observed that user-friendly craft books, for practical and decorative uses, as well as good old-fashioned home economics, are making a comeback, especially as our world economy weakens. People with less money to spend are rediscovering the comfort and practical uses of crafts. With some of our repeat customers at Clay Play, I’ve often heard people remark that making pottery inspired them to do more crafts at home, and to be creative in finding new ways to use their old stuff. It heartens me to learn how people have pulled their old curtains out of boxes and cleverly hung them up again, made new pillows to brighten up their living room sofas, or mended old quilts to hang on hallway walls. Creating fresh new uses for old things is one of life’s greatest comforts.”
人们渴望动手实践的活动，尤其是团体活动，而这些活动在当今社会中大多已经消失。但这些失落的技艺正在复兴。过去二十年来，我一直担任工艺书籍的编辑，我观察到，实用且美观的工艺书籍，以及传统的家政书籍，正在卷土重来，尤其是在全球经济疲软的当下。人们的消费能力下降，他们重新发现了工艺带来的慰藉和实用价值。在“陶艺乐园”（Clay Play），我经常听到一些老顾客说，制作陶器激发了他们在家里进行更多手工创作，并创造性地寻找旧物新用途。看到人们把旧窗帘从箱子里翻出来，巧妙地重新挂起来；制作新枕头来点亮客厅的沙发；或者修补旧被子挂在走廊的墙上，我感到非常欣慰。为旧物创造新的用途，是生活中最美好的事情之一。
Amy’s Comforting Practices at Clay Play
艾米在黏土游戏中的安慰练习
Amy is a master at calmly reassuring people that it’s okay for them to experiment with clay. She explains how she provides comfort to help first-time artists get past their fears and awkwardness:
“First, I say to my guests, There is no wrong way to do this.
“Accommodating them is the key to their success. I adapt the project to the customer’s skill level and background. I show them samples that fit their skill level, and offer stamps, stencils, and idea files full of pictures. I watch how they react to the samples, and tune in to what might be obstacles for them. I help them think of ways to get around obstacles and show them materials that excite and inspire them.
“Next, I ask them questions to help them make choices and decisions about their piece.
“I ask if they are making something for someone else or themselves. If they are making the piece for someone else, I find out more about the person they are making it for, as this often gets them motivated and more interested in their project. I ask gentle questions to help guide their process: ‘Do you want to make something practical or more decorative?’ ‘Is this just for fun?’ ‘Is this going in your kitchen, or what room in your home?’ ‘What colors are your favorite?’
“Because people can be intimidated by staring at a blank piece of paper or a blank piece of pottery, I offer easy tools such as stencils or rubber stamps, so no one needs to create ‘from scratch.’ People are often more comfortable using images and designs they can play with, rather than making their own drawings to paint.
“As they progress to the final phases of their piece, I share in their joy and surprise as they watch their work take shape. Talking about the uses for the piece or where it will be displayed brings out smiles and fresh ideas. It’s usually quite evident, by the way people hold the finished product in their hands, that they are truly comforted by their creation.”
艾米非常擅长用平静的语气安抚人们，让他们相信尝试陶艺是完全没问题的。她解释了自己如何帮助初学者克服恐惧和尴尬：“首先，我会告诉我的客人，做陶艺没有对错之分。“帮助他们是成功的关键。我会根据顾客的技能水平和背景调整项目。我会展示适合他们技能水平的样品，并提供印章、模板和包含图片的创意素材。我会观察他们对样品的反应，并留意他们可能遇到的障碍。我会帮助他们思考如何克服这些障碍，并向他们展示一些能激发他们灵感和兴趣的材料。“接下来，我会问他们一些问题，帮助他们做出关于作品的选择和决定。“我会问他们是为别人还是为自己制作。如果是为别人制作，我会更多地了解收礼人，因为这通常能激发他们的动力，让他们对自己的作品更感兴趣。我会温和地询问一些问题来引导他们的创作过程：“你想做实用的东西还是装饰性的东西？”“只是为了好玩吗？”“这件作品是要放在厨房里，还是家里的哪个房间？”“你最喜欢的颜色是什么？”“因为人们面对一张白纸或一块空白的陶器可能会感到不知所措，所以我提供一些简单的工具，比如模板或橡皮图章，这样就不用从零开始创作了。人们通常更喜欢使用现成的图片和图案，而不是自己绘制草图。”“当他们的作品接近完成时，我会和他们一起分享喜悦和惊喜，看着作品逐渐成型。讨论作品的用途或摆放位置，总能让他们露出笑容，迸发出新的想法。通常，从人们捧着成品时的表情就能看出，他们真的为自己的创作感到欣慰。”
Amy’s Comforting Art-Making Activities for Families
艾米为家庭准备的温馨艺术创作活动
• Go to a pottery studio and paint your own ceramic art.
• 去陶艺工作室，亲手绘制属于你自己的陶瓷艺术品。
Amy encourages families to discover local paint-your-own pottery studios (like Clay Play) in their own communities. Over the past decade or so, studios of this type have sprung up throughout America, providing a very affordable and fun creative activity (for nationwide listings, visit www.paintyourownpottery.net ).
艾米鼓励家庭在自己所在的社区寻找当地的DIY陶艺工作室（例如Clay Play）。在过去的十年左右，这类工作室在美国各地如雨后春笋般涌现，提供了一种非常经济实惠且充满乐趣的创意活动（如需查看全国范围内的工作室列表，请访问www.paintyourownpottery.net）。
• Make a family tree or a family collage of your relatives and ancestors.
• 制作一张家谱或家族拼贴画，展示你的亲戚和祖先。
Research family genealogy. Use a computer program to assemble a family tree, or draw one out on a big sheet of paper. Photocopy or scan old family photos and pictures of ancestors to incorporate into the tree.
研究家族谱系。可以使用电脑程序制作家谱，也可以在一张大纸上绘制。复印或扫描老照片和祖先的照片，添加到家谱中。
• Make and decorate cookies.
• 制作并装饰饼干。
Since you’ll be eating your work and not leaving any permanent record, some people may be less afraid to be creative.
因为你的作品会被吃掉，而且不会留下任何永久记录，所以有些人可能不太害怕发挥创造力。
• Make gifts for any occasion. Some easy and inexpensive things:
• 为各种场合准备礼物。一些简单又便宜的选择：
A box of handmade cards (stamped, sponged, or painted).
一盒手工卡片（印章、海绵印制或手绘）。
A framed page of collaged images or photos with a special message for someone.
一幅装裱好的拼贴画或照片，附有写给某人的特别留言。
Beading—for simple bracelets, necklaces, ornaments, and other decorative art.
串珠——用于制作简单的手链、项链、饰品和其他装饰艺术品。
• Make decorations for any occasion. It’s always comforting to make thoughtful decorations, not just for holidays, but also to simply add a personal touch to our surroundings. Textures, favorite colors, touches of humor, keepsakes, and little pockets of beauty can soften the edges of our rooms, corners, and furniture.
• 为任何场合制作装饰品。精心制作装饰品总能让人感到舒适，不仅适用于节日，也适用于为我们的周围环境增添个人风格。纹理、喜爱的颜色、幽默的元素、纪念品和精致的小物件都能柔化房间、角落和家具的棱角。
Decorate windows, walls, large potted plants, or shelves with things such as a string of tiny lights, garlands, ribbons, silk or dried flowers, scarves, ornaments, fabrics, quilts and throws, wreaths, stones, baskets, driftwood.
用小彩灯、花环、丝带、丝绸或干花、围巾、装饰品、布料、被子和毯子、花环、石头、篮子、浮木等物品装饰窗户、墙壁、大型盆栽植物或架子。
Make fun mobiles to hang from the ceiling, such as stars, comets, suns, angels, rainbows, origami pieces, flying fairies, flying birds, flying planes . . . flying anything.
制作有趣的悬挂装饰品，例如星星、彗星、太阳、天使、彩虹、折纸片、飞翔的仙女、飞翔的鸟、飞翔的飞机……任何会飞的东西。
Check clearance sections of craft stores and stock up on odds and ends that can be incorporated into other projects. For example, red Christmas items can be turned into Valentine’s Day decor.
去工艺品商店的清仓区逛逛，买些零碎的小东西，可以用在其他手工项目里。比如，红色的圣诞装饰品可以改造成情人节装饰品。
• Make little fairy houses.
• 制作一些小仙女屋。
Get a group of children together outdoors to make a little village of fairy houses, using bits of natural objects (pebbles, shells, twigs, feathers, moss, dried flowers, or leaves glued to cardboard) for a magical time together. These houses can later be brought indoors and saved on a special shelf or viewing place.
组织一群孩子到户外，用一些天然材料（鹅卵石、贝壳、树枝、羽毛、苔藓、干花或树叶粘在硬纸板上）制作一个迷你仙女小屋村，一起享受一段奇妙的时光。这些小屋之后可以带回家，放在专门的架子或观赏处保存起来。

Veronica’s Tips
维罗妮卡的建议
Amy’s creative daughter, Veronica (age twelve), suggests these comforting art activities, using a wall in a bedroom, kitchen, or hallway:
• Make a section of your wall into a display area for sticky notes, and then collect fun messages from your friends or relatives when they come to visit you. Or use a large bulletin board to tack on their friendly messages, photos, and cards.
• Use chalkboard paint or magnetic paint to turn a section of your wall into a special viewing spot. You can put magnetic letters and images on the magnetic paint, and draw with colored chalk on the chalkboard paint.
• Make maps on poster board of places where you would like to go, or of fantasy places, and hang them on your wall.
• Make welcome signs for your guests on posters or banners. It’s fun to use different languages for signs too.
• And, of course, refrigerators are perfect places for magnetic letters, images and pictures, funny comics, and photos.
艾米富有创意的女儿维罗妮卡（12岁）建议，可以利用卧室、厨房或走廊的墙壁进行以下这些温馨的艺术活动：• 将墙面的一部分改造成便签展示区，收集朋友或亲戚来访时留下的有趣留言。或者使用一块大的公告板，把他们的留言、照片和卡片贴上去。• 使用黑板漆或磁性漆，将墙面的一部分变成一个特别的观赏点。你可以在磁性漆上贴上磁性字母和图片，也可以用彩色粉笔在黑板漆上画画。• 在海报纸上绘制你想去的地方或幻想中的世界的地图，然后把它们挂在墙上。• 用海报或横幅制作欢迎标语，迎接你的客人。使用不同的语言也很有趣。• 当然，冰箱也是贴磁性字母、图片、趣味漫画和照片的理想场所。
Veronica also suggests using tracing paper to copy images and shapes, and also stencils for designs to paint decorations for cards, collages, boxes, and pottery.
维罗妮卡还建议使用描图纸来复制图像和形状，以及使用模板来绘制图案，用于装饰卡片、拼贴画、盒子和陶器。
# ↩

SHINING A LIGHT ON ONE ANOTHER

彼此照亮

Pamela Blunt, LCSW
帕梅拉·布朗特，LCSW（临床社会工作者）
Expressive Arts Therapist, Artist, Social Worker
表达艺术治疗师、艺术家、社会工作者
Bisbee, Arizona
亚利桑那州比斯比
We need to be seen one another. We can’t recognize ourselves all by ourselves.
我们需要彼此看见。我们无法独自认清自己。
Core Comforting Qualities: Validation and Hopefulness
核心安慰特质：认可和希望
Pamela Blunt has a lovely voice, warm and resonant with soft, low tones. I could just sit back, close my eyes, and listen to her talk about anything. I can understand why her clients keep coming back. She simply sounds comforting.
帕梅拉·布朗特的声音甜美动人，温暖而富有磁性，音调低沉柔和。我可以放松地靠在椅背上，闭上眼睛，静静地听她讲述任何事情。我能理解为什么她的客户会一次又一次地光顾。她的声音听起来就让人感到无比舒适。
Pam’s generous spirit makes her the perfect companion for creative acts of all kinds, be it singing out loud or drawing a picture. Pam works a great deal with elderly people, many of whom have never made art before, and she has a gift for making them feel safe to explore their creative selves for the first time in their lives.
帕姆慷慨大方，是各种创意活动的完美伙伴，无论是放声歌唱还是绘画，她都能给予支持。帕姆经常与老年人一起工作，其中许多人从未接触过艺术，而她有一种天赋，能让他们感到安全，从而生平第一次探索自己的创造力。
I have worked with Pam as a colleague, and have first-hand experience with her co-creative spirit. She possesses an uncanny ability to shine a light on our creative abilities, often hidden inside us and unrecognized. She sees strengths we might not have seen in ourselves, spots a talent or a gift we might have undermined or overlooked. She heartens us to take our creative abilities seriously, whether we choose to develop them for our own personal growth or cultivate them professionally. To Pam, we are all creative at heart, but we usually do not recognize our creativity all by ourselves in a vacuum. Says Pam, “Without being witnessed by others, we don’t see our potential, our talents, our callings.” Pam laments how the excesses of rugged individualism in our culture have perpetuated myths about “finding ourselves” all by ourselves, just by looking within. “But we are relational beings and our talents and gifts usually show up when we are interacting in some way with others, when we get ourselves out of the way to express something important to others.”
我曾与帕姆共事，亲身感受到她富有创造力的精神。她拥有敏锐的洞察力，能够发现我们内心深处那些常常被我们忽略的创造力。她能看到我们自己可能都没意识到的优势，发现我们可能低估或忽视的才能或天赋。她鼓励我们认真对待自己的创造力，无论我们选择将其用于个人成长还是职业发展。在帕姆看来，我们每个人内心都蕴藏着创造力，但我们通常无法在孤立无援的情况下意识到这一点。帕姆说：“如果没有他人的见证，我们就看不到自己的潜能、才能和使命。”帕姆感叹，我们文化中过度强调个人主义的做法，助长了“通过内省就能找到自我”的迷思。 “但我们是关系型动物，我们的才能和天赋通常会在我们以某种方式与他人互动时展现出来，当我们放下自我，向他人表达一些重要的东西时才会显现出来。”
Pam once shined a light on me when I was confused and discouraged in my mid-twenties, juggling between finishing my BFA in theater, teaching drama and dance, and doing many part-time jobs to support myself as an artist and arts teacher. I had little encouragement for all the energy I was putting into trying to be an artist while keeping a roof over my head.
在我二十五六岁，迷茫沮丧的时候，帕姆曾给予我指引。那时我一边努力完成戏剧专业的艺术学士学位，一边教戏剧和舞蹈，还要兼职很多工作来维持自己作为艺术家和艺术教师的生活。我投入了大量精力想成为一名艺术家，同时还要维持生计，却几乎得不到任何鼓励。
I first met Pam in 1980 in our hometown of Richmond, Virginia, in a hip little vegetarian restaurant called the Grace Place. I was her waitress, and she was a friend of a friend. She kindly overlooked how bad a waitress I was, as I continued to forget her side order of falafel with each chatty visit I made to her table, but we hit it off quite well. By the time her falafel was finally delivered, we found ourselves in the midst of a passionate discussion about The Power of Myth by Joseph Campbell and the meanings of our dreams.
我第一次见到帕姆是在1980年，在我们家乡弗吉尼亚州里士满，一家名叫“恩典之地”的时髦素食餐厅。我是她的服务员，她是朋友的朋友。我每次去她桌边聊天，都会忘记给她点沙拉三明治，她虽然觉得我服务很差劲，但还是很宽容地忽略了我的不足。不过我们相处得还不错。等到沙拉三明治终于上来的时候，我们已经热烈地讨论起了约瑟夫·坎贝尔的《神话的力量》以及梦的意义。
Pam frequented the Grace Place, and after my shifts, we often shared our journals of our dreams and visions. She was well ahead of her time in exploring the connections between dance, myth, anthropology, and body work, while finishing her bachelor’s degree in anthropology at the University of Arizona and studying with healers and dancers. She captivated me with her thoughts on our creative processes, and how our body’s wisdom honestly tells us what our souls are calling us to. She indeed validated my inner wisdom about myself, inspiring my early calling as an artist.
帕姆经常光顾格蕾丝之家，我下班后，我们常常分享彼此的梦境和幻象日记。她在探索舞蹈、神话、人类学和身体疗愈之间的联系方面，远超同龄人。当时她正在亚利桑那大学攻读人类学学士学位，并跟随治疗师和舞者学习。她对我们创作过程的思考深深吸引了我，她认为我们身体的智慧能够真诚地告诉我们灵魂的召唤。她确实印证了我内心深处的智慧，也启发了我早期的艺术追求。
After settling permanently in Arizona, Pam worked as a massage therapist in private practice and at Canyon Ranch for ten years, then went for her graduate degree in social work. Initially she worked with children under the care of Child Protective Services, her natural passion for the arts leading her to integrate music, painting, movement, and drama into her work with them. She later shared these same expressive activities in a rural home-based hospice with adults who were dying and their loved ones.
在亚利桑那州定居后，帕姆在私人诊所和峡谷牧场担任按摩治疗师十年，之后攻读了社会工作研究生学位。起初，她为儿童保护服务机构照管的儿童提供服务，她对艺术的天然热爱促使她将音乐、绘画、肢体动作和戏剧融入到与孩子们的互动中。后来，她又在一家乡村家庭临终关怀中心，与临终的成年人及其亲人分享这些表达性活动。
In 2000, Pam began a five-year postgraduate course of study in intermodal expressive arts therapies at the International School for Interdisciplinary Studies in Tucson, Arizona, and later at the European Graduate School in Saas Fee, Switzerland. Currently Pam works with elders with disabilities, bringing arts therapies to their homes and to nursing homes. She also meets clients for sessions in her spacious art studio in Bisbee, Arizona, where she creates her own paintings and ceramics.
2000年，帕姆在亚利桑那州图森市的国际跨学科研究学院开始了为期五年的跨模式表达艺术疗法研究生课程学习，之后又在瑞士萨斯费的欧洲研究生院继续深造。目前，帕姆致力于为残疾老年人提供艺术疗法服务，将艺术疗法带到他们的家中和养老院。她还在位于亚利桑那州比斯比的宽敞艺术工作室为客户提供服务，并在那里创作自己的绘画和陶瓷作品。
She and her husband, Monte Surratt, an artist on the faculty of Cochise College, are highly involved with two artist cooperatives in Bisbee, collaborating with other artists on events throughout the year.
她和她的丈夫蒙特·苏拉特（Monte Surratt）是科奇斯学院的一名艺术家，他们积极参与比斯比的两个艺术家合作社，全年与其他艺术家合作举办各种活动。


T O MY SURPRISE AND DELIGHT, when Pam and I sit down to discuss the healing power of art, she’d rather explore the questions I ask her by asking me questions, engaging me in a fluid dialogue. It’s no surprise, as an expressive arts therapist, that she brings out the playful side of me while sharing her own joy along the way. Quite frankly, she is the easiest brain I have ever picked, bursting with great tips for both professional and personal applications of comfort.
令我惊喜的是，当我和帕姆坐下来讨论艺术的疗愈力量时，她更倾向于通过反问来探索我提出的问题，与我展开流畅的对话。作为一名表达性艺术治疗师，她能激发我活泼的一面，并在过程中分享她自己的喜悦，这并不奇怪。坦白说，她是我遇到过的最容易取悦的人，她总能提供许多关于如何在专业和个人生活中运用安慰技巧的绝妙建议。
What strikes me is Pam’s reverence for the power of expression, artistic or otherwise, our vital, human need to create and give life to what arrives through our imagination; to shape it with sound, movement, words, story, and/or imagery.
让我印象深刻的是帕姆对表达的力量的敬畏，无论是艺术的还是其他的，我们人类创造和赋予想象力以生命的重要需求；用声音、动作、文字、故事和/或图像来塑造它。
“There are no ‘uncreative’ people. Everyone has a well-spring of experiences, longings, fantasies, stories, ways of moving, tones of voice, which can be shared, played with, enlarged upon. What I find comforting about facilitating these experiences with people is how natural and simple it is. There is joy in the surprises that happen when we are immersed in an activity that we are really making up as we go along. I love witnessing people discovering their creative power. I can see the wonderment and delight on their faces at their very spontaneous and unique creations. Often an experience can be sacred, deep, and hilarious all at the same time. Many times people return to tell me that they were inspired to continue to create on their own, or with friends and family, based on something they created during a session.”
“世上没有‘缺乏创造力’的人。每个人都拥有丰富的经验、渴望、幻想、故事、肢体语言和语调，这些都可以分享、玩味和拓展。我发现，引导人们体验这些活动最令人欣慰的地方在于它的自然和简单。当我们沉浸在一个完全即兴创作的活动中时，惊喜的出现会带来快乐。我喜欢见证人们发现自己的创造力。我能看到他们脸上流露出的惊奇和喜悦，因为他们创作出了如此自发而独特的作品。很多时候，一次体验可以同时兼具神圣、深刻和欢笑的特质。很多时候，人们回来告诉我，他们在体验过程中创作的作品激发了他们继续创作的灵感，无论是独自创作，还是与朋友和家人一起创作。”
Pam says she never tires of being midwife to the imaginations of her clients, as she is often awed by what people create spontaneously with the simplest of tools: our hands, feet, voices, words, and most of all, our hearts. She might coax the dancer out of a woman with advanced multiple sclerosis, doing “hand dances” to the music of her favorite CD. She might laugh with an elder as he records his life story on a tape recorder. With someone else, it may be an original song that emerges, created out of a poem, in turn created out of the simple spoken words from a session. Or she might assist a family in creating an impromptu shrine for a loved one out of materials gathered in the desert around their home or from their kitchen drawers. All these activities require heartfelt interaction, spontaneity, and tender attention, fostered by Pam’s presence. But she laments how people censor themselves, and as a therapist she tries to free people from their inner critics.
帕姆说，她从不厌倦引导客户的想象力，因为她常常惊叹于人们用最简单的工具——双手、双脚、声音、语言，尤其是我们的内心——自发创造出的美好。她或许能激发一位患有晚期多发性硬化症的女性舞动起来，伴着她最喜欢的CD音乐跳起“手舞”。她或许会和一位老人一起欢笑，看着他用录音机记录自己的人生故事。对另一些人来说，或许会诞生一首原创歌曲，这首歌源于一首诗，而这首诗又源于咨询过程中简单的言语表达。或者，她会帮助一个家庭用从家附近沙漠或厨房抽屉里收集的材料，为逝去的亲人搭建一个临时的纪念亭。所有这些活动都需要真挚的互动、自发性和温柔的关注，而帕姆的存在恰恰促进了这一切。但她也感叹人们常常自我审查，作为一名治疗师，她努力帮助人们摆脱内心的批判声音。
“Most of us suffer from the societal habit of having to explain things all the time, to justify things we create for others and to ourselves, instead of experiencing an activity honestly and deeply. People can be so hard on themselves, censoring themselves from the full experience of making art, fearing they are not qualified to be artistic. This is so sad. I’ve worked with people late in their lives in their sixties, seventies, and eighties, who had never allowed themselves to leisurely and joyously do the artistic things they had always wanted to do.”
我们大多数人都深受社会习惯的困扰，总是需要解释一切，为自己和他人创作的作品辩解，而不是真诚而深刻地体验创作过程。人们常常对自己过于苛刻，压抑自己，不敢充分体验艺术创作的乐趣，害怕自己没有资格从事艺术。这真是令人遗憾。我曾与一些六七十岁甚至八十岁的老人共事，他们从未允许自己悠闲而快乐地去做那些他们一直想做的艺术创作。
She deeply believes we yearn to be witnessed and heard, and, most of all, moved. When we are moved, our creative response can surprise us, flowing beyond what we first had in mind—beckoning more from us. This yearning to be moved and to express what is in our hearts is the fiery source of our soul.
她深信我们渴望被见证、被倾听，尤其渴望被感动。当我们被感动时，我们的创造力会出乎意料地迸发，超越最初的设想，激发我们内心深处更多的可能性。这种渴望被感动、渴望表达内心感受的愿望，正是我们灵魂炽热的源泉。

Pam’s Tips for Helping People Find Healing Through Art
帕姆关于如何通过艺术帮助人们获得疗愈的建议
• First and foremost, offering my full attention.
This requires a slowed-down pace, and being comfortable with stillness and silence.
Asking simple, open-ended questions, not to probe, not to examine, but just to gently explore. I might simply ask, “What’s going on for you this week?” I often recapitulate what they have said, to show I am following them, and caring about what they are saying.
首先，也是最重要的，是全神贯注地倾听。这需要放慢节奏，并适应安静的环境。我会问一些简单、开放式的问题，不是为了探究或审视，而是为了温和地了解对方。我可能会简单地问：“你这周过得怎么样？”我经常会复述他们说过的话，以表明我在认真倾听，并且关心他们所说的话。
• Being willing to play.
It’s important to have a willingness to be involved in the art-making, too, to play together, not just to observe. I lead the activity just enough for someone to feel safe, but hang back enough for them to take a risk—it’s a responsive dance based on paying attention. But it’s really not that different from the way that children engage in dramatic play—making offers, going with what the other child makes up.
• 乐于参与。参与艺术创作、共同玩耍，而不仅仅是旁观，这一点也很重要。我会引导活动，让参与者感到安全，但又不会过度干预，鼓励他们尝试——这是一种基于专注的互动。其实，这与孩子们玩角色扮演游戏的方式并无太大区别——提出建议，并配合其他孩子的想法。
• Listening closely, and tuning in to their body language. I notice how people warm up or cool down about the topics they bring up, what energizes them or drains them. What makes them smile or squirm or grimace. I offer feedback. It’s important to know what energizes us and what drains us—gives us conscious choices to make that can improve the daily quality of our lives. Just having choices about formerly unquestioned behaviors can be comforting.
• 我会仔细聆听，并留意他们的肢体语言。我会观察人们对所谈论话题的热情或冷淡程度，以及什么会让他们充满活力或感到疲惫。什么会让他们微笑、局促不安或皱眉。我会提供反馈。了解什么能让我们充满活力、什么会让我们感到疲惫至关重要——这能让我们做出有意识的选择，从而改善日常生活质量。仅仅是能够对以前从未质疑过的行为做出选择，就能让人感到安心。
• Bringing them into awareness of the present moment through the senses. I often ask them to close their eyes and tell me what their senses are telling them, what they are perceiving in their surroundings and in their bodies. They might say, “I hear birds singing outside . . . I feel my lower back is a little tight . . . I smell a nice scent of pine in the air . . . I notice my breathing.” While they are relating this stream of consciousness, this awareness of their senses, I am writing down what they say. Later, I share with them what they said, and we might put this into a poem, or into a dance, or into a painting. Just allowing them to pay attention to the moment can reveal how rich our world around us and inside of us really is. By just being present in this way, people are comforted, no matter how limited their physical condition. Children love to do this exercise as well.
Paradoxically, of course, this experiment always brings people into a deeper sense of connection with other people and with the earth. I remember a woman who was blind and very depressed due to advanced diabetes. She was moved to tears when she realized that for a long time, she had not taken the time to listen to the many sounds in her environment, to touch the many textures. She said she felt the whole world was open to her again through this simple exercise. Another client severely crippled by rheumatoid arthritis now regularly writes poetry based on this exercise. The wonderful thing is that no matter how many times we engage in this awareness focus, it is always different and new.
• 通过感官引导他们觉察当下。我经常让他们闭上眼睛，告诉我他们的感官在告诉他们什么，他们在周围环境和自身身体中感知到了什么。他们可能会说：“我听到外面有鸟儿在歌唱……我感觉我的腰有点紧……我闻到空气中弥漫着松树的清香……我注意到我的呼吸。”当他们讲述这段意识流，这段对感官的觉察时，我会把他们的话记录下来。之后，我会和他们分享这些内容，我们可能会把它创作成一首诗、一支舞或一幅画。仅仅是让他们关注当下，就能揭示我们周围和内心世界是多么丰富多彩。仅仅通过这种方式保持临在，人们就能获得慰藉，无论他们的身体状况如何。孩子们也很喜欢做这个练习。当然，看似矛盾的是，这个实验总是能让人们与他人以及与地球建立更深层次的联系。我记得一位失明且因晚期糖尿病而极度抑郁的女士。当她意识到自己很久以来都没有花时间去聆听周围环境中的各种声音，触摸各种不同的质感时，她感动得热泪盈眶。她说，通过这个简单的练习，她感觉整个世界又重新向她敞开了。另一位患有严重类风湿性关节炎的客户现在经常根据这个练习创作诗歌。奇妙的是，无论我们进行多少次这种觉察练习，每次都会有不同的体验，都是全新的。
Pam’s Comforting Suggestions for Families
帕姆给家庭的贴心建议
• Touch
Even if no one is trained in massage or Healing Touch, just placing our hands gently but fully in contact over the ankles, knees, wrists can be very warming and relaxing. Foot baths and foot rubs using aromatherapy oils or mineral salts are delicious. Putting on lotion and rubbing it in is soothing, especially after a foot bath. Encourage the ones we are comforting to take long, full breaths.
• 触摸：即使没有人接受过按摩或疗愈触摸方面的训练，仅仅是将双手轻轻地、充分地接触到脚踝、膝盖和手腕，就能带来温暖和放松的感觉。用芳香精油或矿物盐进行足浴和足部按摩非常舒适。涂抹润肤露并轻轻按摩，尤其是在足浴之后，能起到舒缓作用。鼓励被我们安慰的人深呼吸。
• Playing music that they find comforting
It’s a thoughtful and comforting thing to put on music someone especially enjoys (even if we don’t like it that much). When we know it comforts our loved one in distress, it feels good to show we are thinking of them by saying, “I put on some music just for you this evening.”
• 播放他们觉得舒服的音乐。播放他们特别喜欢的音乐（即使我们自己不太喜欢）是一件体贴又令人感到安慰的事情。当我们知道这能安慰到我们爱的人，并且告诉他们“我今晚特意为你放了些音乐”时，我们会感到很温暖，因为这能表达我们对他们的关心。
• Playing board games and card games and doing puzzles
Games are convenient, comforting, and reliable ways to gather family members and/or friends together. Games provide structure and routine for families going through transition, crisis, or loss, and can be opportunities for people to come together in undemanding, lighthearted havens of good, old-fashioned fun.
Some all-time favorites (some come in junior versions) for most child and adult players (many are available online now):
Monopoly
• 玩棋盘游戏、卡牌游戏和拼图游戏。游戏是让家人和/或朋友聚在一起的便捷、舒适且可靠的方式。对于正在经历变故、危机或失去亲人的家庭来说，游戏能够提供结构和规律，也能让人们有机会在轻松愉快的氛围中享受纯粹的乐趣。以下是一些深受儿童和成人喜爱的经典游戏（部分游戏有儿童版），其中许多游戏现在都可以在网上找到：大富翁
Pictionary
你画我猜
Checkers
跳棋
Clue
妙探寻凶
Sorry
抱歉
Guess Who?
猜猜我是谁？
Yahtzee
骰子游戏（Yahtzee）
Scrabble
拼字游戏（Scrabble）
Twister
扭扭乐（Twister）
Battleship
战舰游戏（Battleship）
Cranium
脑力游戏（Cranium）
Chutes and Ladders

飞行棋（Chutes and Ladders）
• Watch game shows on TV like Jeopardy! or Wheel of Fortune .
• 观看电视上的游戏节目，例如《危险边缘》或《幸运之轮》。
• Play old-time favorite games such as Tag, Hide-and-Seek, Red Rover, Frozen Statues, Hot and Cold, Simon Says. On a rainy day, it can be really fun to play Hide-and-Seek throughout the house with friends and neighbors.
• 玩一些经典的老游戏，比如捉迷藏、捉人游戏、红灯绿灯、冰雕、冷热游戏、西蒙说。下雨天，和朋友邻居一起在屋子里玩捉迷藏会非常有趣。
Pam’s Activities for Bereaved Families
帕姆为丧亲家庭举办的活动
• Create a shrine.
A shrine could be arranged on a small table, a chest, a bookshelf, or in a quiet corner or nook. Some people create a collection of textures, pictures, and small objects and frame this gathering of things as a picture to hang on the wall.
We can include all of our senses in how we choose objects in honor of our loved ones for our shrine.
Visual: We can place pictures, photos, small objects, memorabilia, art, sculpture.
Sound: Place bells, music boxes, or musical cards.
Touch: Use textures, fabrics, nature objects (conch shells, stones, feathers, pine cones, driftwood).
Smell: Douse perfumes on fabrics, use aromatherapy oils or candles.
• 设立一个灵龛。灵龛可以摆放在小桌子、箱子、书架上，或者安静的角落或壁龛里。有些人会收集各种材质的物品、照片和小物件，然后将它们装裱起来，挂在墙上。在为纪念挚爱之人而选择灵龛物品时，我们可以调动所有感官。视觉：我们可以摆放照片、小物件、纪念品、艺术品和雕塑。听觉：摆放铃铛、音乐盒或音乐卡片。触觉：使用各种材质的织物和自然物品（例如海螺壳、石头、羽毛、松果和浮木）。嗅觉：在织物上喷洒香水，使用香薰精油或香薰蜡烛。
• Make a memory box or container.
This is also a kind of shrine, but it is portable and can be put away if needed.
Inside and outside the box, decorate it with paints or collage to express your thoughts, feelings, and memories about the deceased. Put special things inside the box, small keepsakes and memorabilia. One client enjoyed this so much that she ended up creating a large playful, movable sculpture with her children in their yard, as if the yard was their “box.” Truly, “thinking outside the box”!
• 制作一个记忆盒或容器。它也是一种纪念方式，但便于携带，需要时可以收起来。在盒子内外，用颜料或拼贴画装饰，表达你对逝者的思念、感受和回忆。在盒子里放一些特别的物品、小纪念品和纪念物。一位客户非常喜欢这种方式，她最终和孩子们一起在院子里创作了一个大型的、充满趣味的、可移动的雕塑，仿佛院子就是他们的“盒子”。真是“跳出思维定式”！
• Create a ritual.
Using favorite songs, poems, prayers, blessings, or sayings of our loved one, it can be as simple or as elaborate as we want to express. Decide as a family when and how often a ritual will be practiced. Lighting a candle and just saying out loud the words we have written in memory of our loved one is very healing. Often it helps to include each family member participating in the ritual to be responsible for a certain task. One person can light the candle and say an opening statement; the next person can read a prayer; then someone tells a short story or sings a song. Children and teens certainly benefit from participating.
• 创建一个仪式。可以使用逝者生前喜爱的歌曲、诗歌、祈祷文、祝福语或格言，仪式可以简单也可以复杂，完全取决于我们想要表达的情感。全家人可以一起决定何时以及多久举行一次仪式。点燃一支蜡烛，大声朗读我们为纪念逝者而写下的文字，本身就是一种疗愈。通常，让每位家庭成员参与仪式，并负责特定的任务，会更有帮助。例如，一个人可以点燃蜡烛并致开场白；下一个人可以朗读祈祷文；然后有人可以讲述一个小故事或唱一首歌。孩子们和青少年参与其中，尤其能从中受益。
• Make a memory wreath or decorate a memory tree.
To commemorate our loved ones, little pictures, ornaments, objects, origami shapes, and nature pieces can be placed on wreaths or small trees (often made with silk flowers, dried flowers, plastic, or papier-mâché). I once saw a beautiful white little plastic tree decorated with blue and gold origami (folded paper) shapes of Pegasus horses, stars, suns, and moons, in honor of a person who loved horses.
• 制作纪念花环或装饰纪念树。为了纪念我们挚爱的亲人，我们可以将小照片、饰品、物件、折纸作品和自然元素摆放在花环或小树上（通常用绢花、干花、塑料或纸浆制成）。我曾见过一棵漂亮的白色塑料小树，上面装饰着蓝色和金色的折纸作品，包括飞马、星星、太阳和月亮，以此纪念一位热爱马匹的人。
• Make a scrapbook.
Children and family members can write and draw around the photos of their loved one. Some children like to create a “cartoon” or “graphic” journal of memories.
• 制作剪贴簿。孩子们和家人可以在亲人的照片周围写字、画画。有些孩子喜欢创作“卡通”或“图画”风格的回忆录。

PART FOUR
第四部分
The Nature of Comforting
安慰的本质
What Animals and the Earth Teach Us
动物和地球教会我们什么
# ↩

CHAPTER 8
第八章
Comfort from the Heart of Nature
来自大自然的慰藉
# ↩

Chickadees

山雀

O NE JUNE MORNING, as I sat happily on a warm, mossy rock in Wolfe’s Neck Woods on the Casco Bay, a pair of chickadees swirled around me. One of them, a male, landed at the end of a branch in a spindly birch tree, right over my head. He seemed quite intrigued, as he fixed his gaze upon me, head tilted just so. I sat still, entranced by his intense, charming gaze. Suddenly, as if I were someone he knew well and trusted, he hopped onto my head. Amazed, I sat still, just feeling his warm little body, softly breathing and seeming in no hurry to leave. And then quietly he lowered his beak and lightly tapped me on my forehead—a tiny kiss. Afterward, he flew off, landing back on the branch above me. Smitten, I beamed a smile back at him as he continued to watch me. Everything in my world stopped as we lingered sweetly, staring into each other’s eyes, our souls joining together. In just a few minutes, this tiny bird made sacred all that I loved in creation.
六月的一个清晨，我惬意地坐在卡斯科湾沃尔夫颈森林里一块温暖、长满青苔的岩石上，两只山雀在我周围盘旋。其中一只雄鸟落在我头顶上方一棵纤细白桦树的枝头。它似乎很感兴趣，目光专注地注视着我，头微微倾斜。我静静地坐着，被它专注而迷人的目光深深吸引。突然，仿佛我是它熟悉且信任的人，它跳到了我的头上。我惊讶地坐在那里，感受着它温暖的小身体，它轻柔地呼吸着，似乎并不急于离开。然后，它悄悄地垂下喙，轻轻地啄了一下我的额头——一个小小的吻。之后，它飞走了，又落回了我头顶的树枝上。我被它迷住了，对着它露出灿烂的笑容，而它则继续注视着我。当我们依偎在一起，深情凝视彼此的双眼，灵魂交融的那一刻，我的世界仿佛静止了。短短几分钟，这只小鸟就让我心中所有挚爱的事物都变得神圣起来。
Ever since my chickadee initiation, I am especially attuned to their calls outside my window, even when I am fretting over bills, flu pandemics, the Taliban in Pakistan, or how loudly my neighbors like to play their music. They never cease to pull me out of my human drama du jour, drawing my racing imagination into their trees, hilltops, and skies.
自从与山雀结缘以来，我便对窗外的山雀鸣叫格外敏感，即便我正为账单、流感大流行、巴基斯坦塔利班的动向，或是邻居震耳欲聋的音乐声而烦恼不已。它们总能将我从每日的琐碎烦恼中抽离出来，引领我奔涌的思绪飘向它们的树梢、山丘和天空。
I am convinced the earth can give us great solace, wisdom, and hope, especially when our human-to-human experiences disappoint us or leave us lonely. After all, in nature, we are never really alone—the web of life, with all of its mysteries, surrounds and supports us. As comforters, one of the most powerful things we can do to help someone in pain is to bring them back to this great, unending source of peace. And as humans in need of comforting ourselves, it is important to remember that sometimes the greatest “medicine” is a quiet walk in the woods.
我深信，大地能给予我们莫大的慰藉、智慧和希望，尤其是在人与人之间的交往令我们失望或感到孤独之时。毕竟，在大自然中，我们从未真正孤单——生命之网及其所有的奥秘，环绕着我们，支撑着我们。作为安慰者，我们能做的最有力的事情之一，就是帮助那些身处痛苦中的人，将他们带回这伟大而永恒的宁静之源。而作为需要慰藉的人类，我们也应该记住，有时最好的“良药”就是在林间漫步。
# ↩

Beholding

凝视

I will never forget the pure connection I felt to that chickadee as he sat on that branch beholding me. The memory serves as a constant reminder that the way in which we behold someone in distress is as important as any comforting words we might say to them.
我永远不会忘记那只山雀栖息在树枝上凝视着我时，我与它之间那种纯粹的联结。这段记忆时刻提醒着我，我们如何看待身处困境的人，与我们对他们说的任何安慰话语都同样重要。
Over the years, I have watched comforting people in the act of beholding the ones they are tending to. There is a certain genuine, soft look in their eyes. According to the Oxford Dictionary , the Old English origin of behold is bi (thoroughly) halden (hold), to “thoroughly hold.” Stretching further, the definition of thoroughly : “performed with great care” and “regarded in every detail.”
多年来，我观察到，那些给予安慰的人，在照料他人时，总是带着一种真挚而温柔的神情。根据牛津词典，“behold”一词源于古英语，是“bi (thoroughly) halden (hold)”，意为“彻底地握住”。进一步解释，“thoroughly”则意味着“极其细致地执行”和“事无巨细地考虑”。
Don’t we all hunger to be beheld in this way? Sometimes more than being heard, or even held, what we need is to be beheld in a dignified, respectful, yet warm and welcoming way. We crave recognition and acceptance, one soul to another, an “unconditional positive regard,” as in Carl Rogers’s person-centered counseling approach. The Sanskrit greeting namaste says it all: “The light in me recognizes the light in you.”
我们难道不都渴望被这样看待吗？有时，我们需要的不仅仅是被倾听，甚至比被拥抱更重要的，是被以一种尊严、尊重、却又温暖而友好的方式看待。我们渴望被认可和接纳，灵魂与灵魂之间的交流，渴望一种“无条件的积极关注”，正如卡尔·罗杰斯以人为中心的咨询方法中所描述的那样。梵语问候语“合十礼”（Namaste）道尽一切：“我心中的光芒认出了你心中的光芒。”
For seventeen years my cat, Ivan, beheld me sweetly each day in his morning ritual of rolling on his back and staring at me with his gaga eyes as if I were his diva. Moments of comfort I remember best involve someone gazing upon me with love or tenderness or with kindness or respect. Just the look on these people’s or animals’ faces—some of whom had only briefly stepped into my life, like my chickadee, or a giggling toddler who once sat across the aisle from me on a train—linger in my memory as eternal sources of comfort.
十七年来，我的猫伊万每天早晨都会像往常一样，翻身仰躺，用它那双迷人的眼睛凝视着我，仿佛我是它的女神。我记忆中最温暖的时刻，莫过于有人用充满爱意、温柔、友善或尊重的目光注视着我。这些人或动物脸上的表情——其中一些人只是短暂地出现在我的生命中，比如我的小山雀，或者曾经坐在火车过道对面咯咯笑着的小孩——却永远留在我的记忆中，成为我永恒的慰藉。
Animals and nature remind us that we shortchange ourselves and those around us if we miss experiencing the great comfort of being both on and of this earth. They remind us that it is only when we observe thoroughly and listen deeply that we are truly “there” for ourselves and others.
动物和大自然提醒我们，如果我们错过了体验身处这片土地、与这片土地融为一体的巨大慰藉，我们就辜负了自己和身边的人。它们提醒我们，只有当我们用心观察、用心聆听时，才能真正地“陪伴”自己和他人。
Comforting Suggestions for Families or Other Groups to Connect with Animals and Nature
为家庭或其他团体与动物和自然建立联系提供的温馨建议

We can give back to our communities by volunteering with animals and nature as rewarding and meaningful work. Here are a few ideas:
• Pet therapy programs
• Humane societies
• Recycling projects
• Environmental projects—planting trees, cleaning up trails
• Nature centers, parks
• Going bird-watching or hiking on trails together
• Starting a garden in a private or community space or growing plants indoors
• Playing with our pets
我们可以通过参与动物和自然相关的志愿活动来回馈社区，这既有意义又令人满足。以下是一些建议：• 宠物治疗项目• 动物保护协会• 回收项目• 环保项目——植树、清理步道• 自然中心、公园• 一起观鸟或徒步旅行• 在私人或公共空间开辟花园或室内种植植物• 与宠物玩耍
# ↩

Introducing Our Guides to the Nature of Comforting

隆重推出我们的《舒适之道》指南

I am fortunate to know many healers who learned the nonverbal languages of comforting from the natural world around them. They have studied, partnered with, and applied this life-affirming wisdom with many groups of people, including those who are grieving, distressed, or chronically ill.
我很幸运认识许多疗愈师，他们从周围的自然界中学习了非语言的慰藉之道。他们研究、运用并结合了这种充满生命力的智慧，服务于许多群体，包括那些正在经历丧亲之痛、痛苦挣扎或身患慢性疾病的人。
Don and Brenda Weeks, a gentle and compassionate married couple, work with their therapy dogs, going to hospitals, nursing homes, and hospices. They present to us what they have learned from dogs about reaching out to people in distress who are often isolated, withdrawn, and afraid in their pain. Nancy Coyne, M.D., is a warm and wise psychiatrist working with horses as healers for trauma survivors, including those with severe PTSD, such as veterans of the Iraq War, victims of violent crime, and survivors of domestic abuse. Laura Hare has developed innovative and successful programs that show children how to be responsible caregivers and team players by directly caring for animals.
唐和布伦达·威克斯是一对温柔善良的夫妇，他们带着治疗犬前往医院、疗养院和临终关怀中心。他们向我们分享了他们从狗狗身上学到的经验，这些经验可以帮助那些身处困境、常常感到孤立、孤僻和恐惧的人们。南希·科因医生是一位热情睿智的精神科医生，她利用马匹作为疗愈工具，帮助创伤幸存者，包括患有严重创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）的患者，例如伊拉克战争老兵、暴力犯罪受害者和家庭暴力幸存者。劳拉·黑尔开发了一系列创新且成功的项目，通过让孩子们直接照顾动物，向他们展示如何成为负责任的照护者和团队成员。
Finally, Jen Deraspe, a wilderness retreat director and mindfulness instructor, shows us how to find stillness and quietude so we can behold the comfort of the earth—and the peace within ourselves.
最后，荒野静修指导员兼正念导师 Jen Deraspe 向我们展示了如何找到平静和安宁，以便我们能够感受到地球的舒适——以及我们内心的平静。
# ↩

DOG WISDOM: EVERYONE DESERVES COMFORTING

狗狗的智慧：每个人都值得被安慰

Don and Brenda Weeks
Providers of the Therapy Dog Program at
Central Maine Medical Center
Owners, Directors, and Trainers, Shangri-La Kennel,
Auburn, Maine
唐和布伦达·威克斯（Don and Brenda Weeks）是缅因州中部医疗中心治疗犬项目的提供者，同时也是香格里拉犬舍（Shangri-La Kennel）的所有者、负责人和训练员，该犬舍位于缅因州奥本市。
For people in distress during unpredictable times, dogs can be a predictable comfort. Dogs allow us the freedom to let our own walls down, so we can be present with each other.
在动荡不安的时期，对于身处困境的人们来说，狗狗能带来一丝慰藉。狗狗让我们卸下心防，彼此敞开心扉，坦诚相待。
Core Comforting Qualities: Acceptance and Compassion
核心安慰特质：接纳与同情
Don and Brenda Weeks smile modestly as I ask them what dogs teach us about comforting. They have poured me an icy Coke and seated me at a table in their huge country kitchen with two of their dogs, Savannah, a black Lab, and Onyx, a flat-coated retriever, lying politely beside my feet. Wearing sandals, I can feel Onyx’s wagging tail gently swooshing across my feet and shins, which is fine with me. The tail becomes a kind of barometer, responding to the level of excitement or intensity of our conversation. When we laugh, I feel her tail knocking against my feet, and when we settle back down, her tail slows back to its original leisurely pace.
当我问唐和布伦达·威克斯，狗狗教会了我们如何安慰他人时，他们谦逊地笑了笑。他们给我倒了一杯冰可乐，让我坐在他们宽敞的乡村厨房的一张桌子旁，他们的两只狗狗——黑色拉布拉多犬萨凡纳和扁平毛寻回犬奥尼克斯——乖乖地趴在我的脚边。我穿着凉鞋，能感觉到奥尼克斯摇摆的尾巴轻轻地拂过我的脚和小腿，我感觉很舒服。它的尾巴就像一个晴雨表，能反映出我们谈话的兴奋程度和激烈程度。当我们大笑时，我能感觉到它的尾巴轻轻地拍打着我的脚；当我们安静下来时，它的尾巴又恢复了原本悠闲的节奏。
I giggle as Onyx suddenly begins to lightly lick my hand. Don and Brenda chuckle softly at their dog’s uncanny ability to sense exactly what I need at this moment, relieving some of my shyness and pre-interview tension. Already, one thing is clear about what dogs can teach us about comforting—they remind us not to take ourselves so seriously.
奥尼克斯突然轻轻舔了舔我的手，我忍不住咯咯笑了起来。唐和布伦达轻声笑着，他们的狗狗似乎拥有不可思议的能力，能准确地感知到我此刻的需求，这让我稍稍缓解了羞涩和面试前的紧张。狗狗能教会我们安慰人的一点显而易见——它们提醒我们不要太把自己当回事。
Married for twenty-six years, Don and Brenda have quietly and humbly devoted themselves to running a kennel, training therapy dogs and volunteers, and collaborating with medical staff all over central Maine. Don and Brenda met while studying to be certified guide dog instructors at the Guiding Eyes School for the Blind in Yorktown Heights, New York, in the early 1980s. Earlier, they had both gone to the same school at Holliston Junior College in Massachusetts for their kennel management certificate. Since 1993, they have been visiting patients in local nursing homes and Central Maine Medical Center with several of their therapy dogs.
唐和布伦达结婚二十六年，一直默默无闻、谦逊低调地经营着一家犬舍，训练治疗犬和志愿者，并与缅因州中部各地的医务人员合作。上世纪八十年代初，唐和布伦达在纽约州约克镇高地的导盲犬学校学习导盲犬训练员资格认证时相识。此前，他们都曾在马萨诸塞州霍利斯顿专科学校就读，并获得了犬舍管理证书。自1993年以来，他们一直带着几只治疗犬去当地的养老院和缅因州中部医疗中心探望病人。
Brenda, who has coped with multiple sclerosis for sixteen years, uses a power chair and a vent but functions beautifully with the dogs when she goes on visits to nursing homes and hospices.
布伦达患有多发性硬化症已有十六年，她使用电动轮椅和呼吸机，但当她去探望养老院和临终关怀中心时，她和狗狗们相处得非常好。
Don and Brenda emphasize how important it is to sit back and let the dogs have the spotlight when they’re doing a therapy visit at a hospital. They gently guide the dogs so patients can focus their full attention on them. I soon learn what makes pet therapy professionals so good at what they do—they keep out of the way and stay in the background yet somehow direct their dogs remotely, invisibly. This is quite an art in itself.
唐和布伦达强调，在医院进行宠物治疗探访时，最重要的是要退居幕后，让狗狗们成为焦点。他们轻柔地引导狗狗，以便患者能够将全部注意力集中在它们身上。我很快就明白了宠物治疗专家们为何如此出色——他们不会喧宾夺主，而是默默地、隐蔽地引导狗狗。这本身就是一门艺术。
Brenda has a sweet, almost angelic face, and she positively beams when she talks about the work the dogs do. “When people don’t know what to say, a dog is someone everyone can relate to—can touch, can talk about, like a conversation piece. Everyone can connect with the dog in some way, to be playful and relax a little. The therapy dog changes the mood and the whole energy of the patient’s room. The patient, family members, and hospital staff will often laugh, slow down a little, and connect with each other in a way they hadn’t before.”
布伦达长着一张甜美、近乎天使般的脸庞，谈起狗狗们的工作时，她总是容光焕发。“当人们不知该如何表达时，狗狗就成了每个人都能产生共鸣的对象——可以触摸，可以谈论，就像一个话题。每个人都能以某种方式与狗狗建立联系，一起玩耍，放松身心。治疗犬能改变病房的气氛和整体氛围。病人、家属和医护人员常常会开怀大笑，放慢节奏，以一种前所未有的方式彼此交流。”
Don adds, smiling and nodding, “Dogs pull us out of our shells. People start to tell stories, even long stories, especially about dogs they’ve had, or other pet stories. Everyone has some kind of an animal story, and we often feel safer telling animal stories than other personal stories. The animal stories ultimately lead them on to relating personal stories about themselves, their fears, their worries, and what might lie ahead for them. We’re always humbled that they feel comfortable enough with us to share tales they haven’t told others before.”
唐笑着点点头，补充道：“狗狗能让我们敞开心扉。人们开始讲述故事，甚至是很长的故事，尤其是关于他们养过的狗狗或其他宠物的故事。每个人都有一段与动物有关的故事，而且我们通常觉得讲述动物故事比讲述其他个人故事更自在。这些动物故事最终会引导他们讲述自己的个人故事，他们的恐惧、担忧以及对未来的展望。他们愿意和我们分享那些从未对别人说过的故事，这总是让我们感到无比荣幸。”
“And these stories can be funny, too, a great icebreaker,” Brenda joins in. “A good dog story can unify everyone, bring a family or a group of friends together with memories of good times—summer vacations, or trips, or birthday parties or weddings. It’s interesting how many of these stories are about dogs in group events, not just private moments. Dog stories can take a family down memory lane together, and they certainly help the patient at the hospital or hospice find enjoyable things to talk about, connect with.”
“而且这些故事也很有趣，是很好的破冰方式，”布伦达补充道。“一个好的狗狗故事能让大家聚在一起，让家人或朋友回忆起美好的时光——暑假、旅行、生日派对或婚礼。有趣的是，很多故事都与狗狗在集体活动中的互动有关，而不仅仅是私人时刻。狗狗故事能带领家人一起重温美好回忆，也肯定能帮助医院或临终关怀中心的病人找到一些有趣的话题，建立联系。”
I was curious what Don and Brenda, as comforters, were learning personally from dogs.
我很好奇唐和布伦达作为抚慰者，能从狗身上学到什么。
Don turns his answer over in his mind for a few moments and then says, “I have been working toward becoming a chaplain at Central Maine Medical Center’s training program, and have also been volunteering as a Eucharist minister, bringing communion to patients at a hospice house and nursing homes. Working with our dog Christophe and meeting patients has convinced me that I need to develop more unconditional love and acceptance for people. I still struggle with some judgmental qualities in myself, and I know this interferes with my comforting abilities as a chaplain. Christophe shows me how being present and attuned to the patients’ needs can pull me out of my rush to judgment and cynicism about human nature.”
唐在心里琢磨了一会儿，然后说道：“我一直在中央缅因医疗中心的培训项目中努力成为一名牧师，同时也在临终关怀中心和养老院做义工，为病人送圣餐。和我们的狗克里斯托夫相处，以及与病人接触，让我意识到我需要培养更多无条件的爱和接纳。我仍然在与自己身上的一些评判性倾向作斗争，我知道这会影响我作为牧师的安慰能力。克里斯托夫让我明白，用心陪伴病人，关注他们的需求，可以让我摆脱急于评判和对人性的愤世嫉俗。”
He tells a moving story about a man who struggled with alcoholism most of his life, lying alone in a hospital, dying of cirrhosis. “No one came to visit this man in his last days of life, as he had alienated everyone in his family, his ex-wife, his kids, and his friends. Aside from the medical staff, Christophe and I came to visit him every day. This patient understood and accepted why no one came to see him. He told me how he thought only a dog would be able to love him unconditionally, after all the trouble he had caused others in his life. He invited Christophe to jump up on his bed and lie down beside him. Christophe allowed this man to hold and caress him, and he returned his affection. He told me he had missed his own dog from an earlier time in his life, and thanked us with tears for having this opportunity to hold a dog once more at the end of his life.”
他讲述了一个感人的故事：一个男人一生都在与酗酒作斗争，最终因肝硬化独自躺在医院里，走向生命的尽头。“在他生命的最后几天，没有人来看望他，因为他疏远了所有的家人、前妻、孩子和朋友。除了医护人员，我和克里斯托夫每天都去看望他。这位病人理解并接受了没有人来看望他的原因。他告诉我，在他给别人带来了那么多麻烦之后，他觉得只有狗才能无条件地爱他。他邀请克里斯托夫跳上他的床，躺在他身边。克里斯托夫允许他拥抱抚摸自己，他也回应了他的爱意。他告诉我，他很想念自己年轻时养的狗，并含着泪感谢我们，让他有机会在生命的最后时刻再次拥抱狗狗。”
Don pauses, gently noticing how moved Brenda and I are, as my eyes moisten a little with tears, then he tenderly continues, “I know this is really sad, but just imagine how much Christophe gave this man. It wasn’t just the love, it was the freedom of being completely accepted, just as you are, all the good, the bad, everything . . . so you might find some peace at the end of your life. That is what I want to give people as a chaplain when they are in pain, emotionally or physically. I’ll never be able to do this as well as Christophe. I don’t need to let patients hug me like Christophe, but mostly they need to feel accepted and free of judgment in my presence.”
唐停顿了一下，温柔地注意到我和布伦达的情绪，我的眼眶也微微湿润，然后他轻声说道：“我知道这很令人难过，但请想想克里斯托夫给了这个人多少。不仅仅是爱，还有被完全接纳的自由，接纳你本来的样子，好的、坏的，一切的一切……这样你或许能在生命的尽头找到一些平静。作为一名牧师，当人们遭受痛苦，无论是精神上的还是身体上的，我都想给予他们这样的帮助。我永远无法像克里斯托夫那样做得更好。我不需要像克里斯托夫那样让病人拥抱我，但他们最需要的是在我面前感受到被接纳，感受到没有评判。”
On this topic of unconditional love and acceptance, Brenda shares how dogs have helped stop her from imposing “shoulds” on herself, and to be more accepting of others unconditionally.
关于无条件的爱和接纳这个话题，布伦达分享了狗狗如何帮助她不再给自己强加“应该”，并更加无条件地接纳他人。
“Being able to love unconditionally and ending my judgmental habits comes with my journey of accepting my illness with MS, after being progressively more disabled in my physical capabilities. For a long time, being paralyzed, in my chair, on my vent, I had felt I should be doing more for people, at least carrying my own weight, and therefore I judged myself as deficient. But learning from dogs, working with them to visit patients, I realized my presence alone was enough. People needed my loving presence at least as much as anything else. If I had been more physically able to move around and busier, I would not have focused so much on offering my full acceptance and compassion to others. Now I finally believe there is a reason I have had MS—to make me a true comforter. It has focused me on what I have to give to others—my heart, my time, my ears, my empathy. And when I go into a room with my dogs and visit people at the end of their lives, I can just be free to love them.”
“能够无条件地去爱，并摒弃评判他人的习惯，源于我接受自己罹患多发性硬化症的经历，以及我身体机能逐渐衰退的过程。很长一段时间里，我瘫痪在床，只能依靠呼吸机维持生命，总觉得自己应该为别人做更多的事情，至少应该承担起自己的责任，因此我常常觉得自己很无能。但从狗狗身上，以及带着它们去探望病人的过程中，我意识到，我的陪伴本身就足够了。人们需要我的爱，其重要性不亚于其他任何东西。如果我的身体状况允许我四处走动，或者更忙碌一些，我就不会如此专注于给予他人完全的接纳和关怀。现在，我终于相信，我患上多发性硬化症是有原因的——它让我成为一个真正的安慰者。它让我专注于我能给予他人的东西——我的心、我的时间、我的倾听、我的同理心。当我带着我的狗狗走进病房，去探望那些生命垂危的人们时，我终于可以自由地去爱他们。”
Brenda and Don are highly involved with the local hospice. In their hospice visits, they practice their quiet, unconditional love along with their dogs, allowing the visit to provide a peaceful sanctuary for people in the last days of their lives. Don tenderly reflects on his experiences in hospices:
“We have witnessed powerful experiences of comforting when we bring our dogs to hospice care. For patients at the end of their lives, dogs can help a family say good-bye. Often the patient will invite the dog to come up on the bed with them. The dog lies comfortably next to the patient, so when a family member sits or stands by the bed, they can pat the dog and talk to the dog, especially when they are having difficulty speaking with their loved one who is dying. Dogs help the patient and family handle the long silences that can feel empty and awkward.
“Family members often feel a sense of relief when they see the dog resting against the patient, feeling the closeness and comfort of the dog. The dog serves as a kind of hub of love for family and friends, as they connect to the patient through the dog, telling stories, sharing news, or just quietly enjoying the dog, stroking the fur, getting their hands licked, and sitting together in a tender moment.”
布伦达和唐积极参与当地的临终关怀中心活动。在探访临终关怀中心时，他们带着爱犬，用无声无息的爱陪伴着人们，为生命最后阶段的人们提供一片宁静的庇护所。唐深情地回忆起他在临终关怀中心的经历：“我们亲眼见证了带狗狗去临终关怀中心所带来的巨大安慰。对于生命垂危的病人来说，狗狗可以帮助家人与他们告别。通常，病人会邀请狗狗上床陪伴自己。狗狗会舒适地依偎在病人身边，当家人坐在或站在床边时，可以轻抚狗狗，和它说话，尤其是在难以与即将离世的亲人交流的时候。狗狗帮助病人和家人度过漫长而尴尬的沉默时光。当家人看到狗狗依偎在病人身边，感受到狗狗的亲近和安慰时，往往会感到如释重负。”对于家人和朋友来说，狗狗就像一个爱的纽带，他们通过狗狗与病人建立联系，讲述故事，分享消息，或者只是安静地享受与狗狗相处的时光，抚摸它的毛发，让它舔自己的手，一起享受温馨的时刻。
What Dogs Teach Us About Comforting
狗狗教会我们如何安慰人

DON AND BRENDA SUMMARIZED THE KEY WAYS DOGS TEACH COMFORTERS:
• When we don’t know what to say at awkward times, dogs give us something in common to talk about—about themselves, about other dogs or other pets, or about where their owners have taken them.
• Dogs help us handle long silences together, especially when we are in a comforting role with someone in pain or distress. Dogs encourage us to allow more silence, to relax, to feel free from having to talk or entertain someone.
• The contagious energy of dogs can calm us on hectic days and perk us up on dreary days.
• Their empathy is powerful, as they feel strongly what we feel, reflecting back to us the truth and depth of our own feelings.
• They slow us down, keep us grounded, and invite us to be in the present moment.
• When we are in pain, they can distract and engage us and draw our attention away from our fears and our worries.
• Dogs remind us we are never really alone, no matter how lonely we feel.
• Dogs help us cut through social pretenses, our status, or the inflation of our egos, or “BS,” and to be humble and authentic. They are great levelers—equalizers for humans.
• Dogs help life feel normal in abnormal situations.
• When medical staff have to break bad news, dogs can be a comfort for the patient and for the family members in the room.
• Dogs can draw out affection and love from withdrawn, depressed, or disoriented people, especially patients in clinical settings.
• Dogs also help focus and orient elders with cognitive disabilities, with dementia or Alzheimer’s, or those who have had strokes.
唐和布伦达总结了狗狗教会我们安慰他人的关键方式：• 当我们在尴尬的时刻不知该说什么时，狗狗能给我们提供共同的话题——关于它们自己，关于其他狗狗或其他宠物，或者关于它们的主人带它们去过的地方。• 狗狗能帮助我们一起应对长时间的沉默，尤其是在我们安慰那些痛苦或悲伤的人时。狗狗鼓励我们享受更多安静，放松身心，摆脱说话或取悦他人的束缚。狗狗充满感染力的能量，能在忙碌的日子里安抚我们，也能在阴郁的日子里提振精神。它们的同理心非常强大，能够强烈地感受到我们的感受，并将我们内心深处的真实感受反映出来。它们让我们慢下来，脚踏实地，引导我们活在当下。当我们痛苦时，它们可以分散我们的注意力，让我们不再为恐惧和忧虑而烦恼。狗狗提醒我们，无论多么孤独，我们都并非真正孤单。狗狗帮助我们摒弃社交伪装、身份地位、自负或虚伪，让我们变得谦逊真诚。它们是绝佳的平衡器——人类的平衡器。• 狗狗帮助人们在异常情况下保持正常的生活状态。• 当医护人员不得不告知患者坏消息时，狗狗可以安慰患者及其家属。• 狗狗能够唤起那些孤僻、抑郁或迷失方向的人的情感和爱，尤其是在临床环境中的患者。• 狗狗还能帮助认知障碍、患有痴呆症或阿尔茨海默病的老年人，以及中风患者集中注意力并调整方向。
Comforting Suggestions for Families or Other Groups
给家庭或其他团体的安慰建议
With your own dog or a borrowed dog, Don and Brenda suggest the following comforting activities we can do with dogs:
• Enjoying some quiet time brushing and grooming them
• Playing with their toys, with balls, sticks and Frisbees, and getting down on the ground to play
• Watching pets playing together and laughing at their goofy stuff
• Observing pets comfort and nurture each other
• Holding your pets, loving them
• Taking walks and exploring with them
• Enjoying all their little routines; their predictability is comforting
• Reading stories and seeing movies and TV shows about animals and nature, which can be fun to share and talk about
唐和布伦达建议，无论你养的是自己的狗还是借来的狗，都可以和狗狗一起做以下这些温馨的活动：• 享受安静的梳毛和美容时光• 和狗狗一起玩玩具，比如球、树枝和飞盘，甚至可以趴在地上和它们玩耍• 观察宠物们一起玩耍，为它们的滑稽举动而开怀大笑• 观察宠物们互相安慰和照顾• 拥抱你的宠物，爱抚它们• 带它们散步和探索世界• 享受它们所有的日常小习惯；它们的规律性令人感到安心• 阅读关于动物和自然的故事，观看相关的电影和电视节目，这些都可以成为你们分享和讨论的乐趣
