HORSE WISDOM: CLARITY AND FIRMNESS FOR COMFORTERS

马的智慧：为舒适者带来清晰与坚定

Nancy Coyne, M.D.
南希·科因，医学博士
Staff Psychiatrist and Instructor
精神科医生兼讲师
Epona Center for Equine Experiential Learning Sonoita, Arizona
埃波纳马匹体验式学习中心，索诺伊塔，亚利桑那州
Thirty years in private practice as a psychiatrist specializing in treating trauma survivors
从事精神科医生私人执业三十年，专门治疗创伤幸存者
We don’t have to be mean to mean what we say. Horses teach us how to be clear and firm, balanced with gentleness and respect.
我们不必刻薄才能表达自己的真实想法。马教会我们如何做到清晰坚定，同时又不失温柔和尊重。
Core Comforting Qualities: Clarity and Strength
核心舒适特质：清晰与力量
Nancy Coyne has had thirty years’ experience in private practice with trauma survivors, working with victims of domestic violence as well as veterans with PTSD. Yet for all the grief and pain she has known in listening to the stories of her clients’ harsh lives, she is deeply hopeful, an old soul, with a wonderful smile and a generous heart.
南希·科因拥有三十年的私人执业经验，专门帮助创伤幸存者，包括家庭暴力受害者和患有创伤后应激障碍的退伍军人。尽管在倾听客户坎坷人生的故事时，她也经历了种种悲痛，但她内心深处依然充满希望，拥有一颗老成的灵魂，脸上总是挂着灿烂的笑容，心中充满慷慨。
About ten years ago, she began to focus her practice more on working with horses as healers after she had observed how people who were devastated by human violence naturally connected with animals. She believed many survivors needed other-than-human connections to heal from human-caused trauma. Several years ago, inspired by the brilliant work of Linda Kohanov, Nancy moved to Arizona to work at the Epona Center for Equine Experiential Learning, which Linda had founded. Now as one of Epona’s instructors and their staff psychiatrist, Nancy counsels different groups of survivors, including veterans returning from Iraq and Afghanistan, survivors of domestic abuse and child abuse, and other survivors of violent crime.
大约十年前，她观察到那些遭受人类暴力创伤的人会自然而然地与动物建立联系，于是开始将工作重心更多地放在利用马匹进行疗愈上。她相信，许多幸存者需要与人类以外的其他生物建立联系，才能从人为创伤中恢复过来。几年前，受到琳达·科哈诺夫（Linda Kohanov）卓越工作的启发，南希搬到了亚利桑那州，在琳达创办的埃波纳马匹体验式学习中心（Epona Center for Equine Experiential Learning）工作。如今，作为埃波纳的导师和驻场精神科医生，南希为不同群体的幸存者提供咨询服务，包括从伊拉克和阿富汗战场归来的退伍军人、家庭暴力和儿童虐待的幸存者，以及其他暴力犯罪的幸存者。
Nancy is full of life because she loves her life, dedicated to her soul’s calling of working with horses as healers. She lives most of the year on her seven-acre farm near Sonoita, Arizona, with her partner, four horses, one donkey, one mini horse, two llamas, two goats, two cats, and two dogs. She migrates to Maine every summer to work with her East Coast clients and teach workshops. She spends her leisure time riding her horse in the desert near her farm. She speaks exuberantly of this experience: “Exquisite comfort comes from being one with the horse I am riding, a sense of being synchronized, and knowing the horse picks up on what I want with my slightest movements, tuning in to me. The horse and I work in such tandem that we both feel a freedom of movement, as if we are the same organism, breathing together the essence of the same life force.”
南希热爱生活，充满活力，她全身心投入到与马匹一起疗愈的灵魂召唤中。一年中的大部分时间，她都和伴侣、四匹马、一头驴、一匹迷你马、两只羊驼、两只山羊、两只猫和两条狗一起生活在亚利桑那州索诺伊塔附近占地七英亩的农场里。每年夏天，她都会前往缅因州，为东海岸的客户提供服务并举办工作坊。闲暇时，她喜欢在农场附近的沙漠里骑马。她兴致勃勃地谈起这种体验：“与我骑乘的马融为一体，那种感觉无比舒适，一种同步感，以及马匹能够感知我最细微的动作，与我心意相通的感觉。我和马匹如此默契，我们都感到行动自由，仿佛我们是同一个生命体，共同呼吸着同一生命力的精华。”
Her love and reverence for horses began with one of her earliest experiences on a horse when she was at camp as a young girl. As the sun was about to rise, she had secretly taken off on a horse from the stable, leaving the camp to ride bareback alone through a nearby field. She had immersed herself in the freedom and wildness of her adventurous ride, but soon she fell off her horse. As she lay on the ground, her horse gently kept from crushing her, placing his foot carefully on her belly. Amazed, she looked up, eye to eye with her horse, who protectively gazed down at her. This moment of trust and soulful connection has stayed with her all her life.
她对马的热爱和敬畏始于她幼年时在夏令营的一次骑马经历。那天清晨，太阳即将升起，她偷偷地从马厩里骑上一匹马，离开营地，独自一人骑着马穿过附近的田野。她沉浸在自由奔放的冒险之旅中，但很快就从马上摔了下来。她躺在地上，马儿温柔地保护着她，小心翼翼地用蹄子轻轻地踩在她的肚子上。她惊讶地抬起头，与马儿四目相对，马儿也低头守护着她。那一刻的信任和心灵的联结，永远铭刻在她的记忆中。
She shared another more recent story about a horse named Samson, a great comforting friend of hers who appeared at Epona a few years ago.
她还分享了另一个关于一匹名叫参孙的马的故事，这匹马是她非常安慰的朋友，几年前出现在埃波纳。
“I was grieving deeply over issues in my family and feeling lonely and teary. One day at Epona ranch a big black draft horse named Samson arrived in Arizona all the way from Michigan. This was his first day in Arizona, and we expected him to be restless and agitated. As I approached the fence, he trotted up and reached his head over the fence to me. Before I knew it, my face was buried in his neck, and he let me hug him for quite a while. We were all surprised. It was as if he felt what was in my heart, and feeling displaced and nervous himself, he came to me. It was mutual comforting.”
“当时我正为家里的事悲痛欲绝，感到孤独无助，泪流满面。有一天，埃波纳牧场来了一匹名叫萨姆森的黑色高大挽马，它从密歇根州远道而来。这是它来到亚利桑那州的第一天，我们以为它会焦躁不安。我走到围栏边时，它小跑过来，把头伸过围栏向我招手。还没反应过来，我的脸就埋进了它的颈窝，它让我拥抱了它好一会儿。我们都感到很惊讶。仿佛它感受到了我的心境，它自己也感到不安和焦虑，于是来到我身边。我们彼此都得到了安慰。”
I wondered about the particular qualities of horses that were comforting for trauma survivors, as opposed to the comfort of dogs, for example. Nancy answered this easily.
我很好奇，与狗相比，马匹究竟有哪些特质能给创伤幸存者带来安慰。南希轻松地回答了我的问题。
“Horses are different than dogs in what they teach us about comforting. Dogs are quite forthcoming with their love and attention—they dish it out! Horses, unlike dogs, require certain qualities from us, especially our careful attunement, because they are so much bigger than dogs and bigger than us. They are also prey animals, used to running from predators, and have been mistreated by humans for millenniums, so horses are highly sensitive to our gentleness, patience, and respect. However, they need our clarity and firmness, too, in guiding them.”
“马和狗在安抚方面给我们带来的启示截然不同。狗会毫不吝啬地表达爱意和关注——它们会毫不吝啬地付出！而马则不同，它们需要我们具备某些特质，尤其是细致入微的关注，因为它们比狗和我们体型都大得多。它们也是猎物，习惯于躲避捕食者，并且数千年来一直遭受人类的虐待，因此马对我们的温柔、耐心和尊重非常敏感。然而，在引导它们时，它们也需要我们清晰而坚定的指示。”
“So horses need us to be very soft and careful with them, respectful, but also to be clear and firm.” I said this out loud, letting the words sink in.
“所以，马需要我们温柔小心地对待它们，尊重它们，但同时也要清晰坚定。”我大声说道，让这些话在心里沉淀下来。
Nancy was eager to explain this. “This softness, balanced with clarity and firmness, is so important for trauma survivors to learn. This is a soft kind of strength that means being powerful without being demanding. People who have been traumatized by violence mistakenly think they have to be mean to mean what they say. They have learned strength and power in destructive experiences of force and aggression. Horses show us ways to be powerful through our presence, our focus, our belief, our energetic conviction behind our words. We need to be clear with horses in what we want them to do and what we want ourselves to do. Horses need our boundaries and capacities made quite obvious. For people who have been abused or violated in some way, horses draw out of them an ability to say no or yes with solid conviction, strong boundaries, or else the horse will stray or pull away from the rider’s intentions.”
南希急切地解释道：“这种柔和与清晰坚定相平衡的特质，对于创伤幸存者来说至关重要。这是一种柔和的力量，意味着强大而不强势。遭受过暴力创伤的人常常误以为，只有刻薄才能表达自己的真实想法。他们从充满破坏性的暴力和攻击经历中习得了力量。马匹教会我们如何通过自身的存在、专注、信念以及言语背后饱含的能量来展现力量。我们需要清晰地告诉马匹我们想要它们做什么，以及我们自己想要做什么。马匹需要我们明确地表达自己的界限和能力。对于那些曾遭受虐待或侵犯的人来说，马匹能够激发他们坚定地说‘不’或‘是’的能力，让他们拥有清晰的界限，否则马匹就会偏离方向，或者背离骑手的意图。”
“Don’t these horses intimidate some of your clients?” I wondered.
“这些马不会吓到你的一些客户吗？”我心想。
“Many of the horses at Epona are abused animals themselves, some retired racehorses, who still want to be useful and active but need our support. The trauma survivors and abused horses bond well together because they sense each other’s wounds, each other’s sensitivity, shyness, and hesitancy to make connections. They both need lots of gentleness, softness, and slow gradual steps to trusting each other. Some of the most important work happens before the survivors ever get on the horses, by taking time getting to know each other through brushing, grooming, cleaning, and leading the horses on walks, or in feeding them. They grow attached and little signs of communication are developed.”
“Epona马场里的许多马匹本身也曾遭受虐待，其中一些是退役赛马，它们仍然渴望发挥作用，积极参与社会活动，但需要我们的帮助。这些创伤幸存者和受虐马匹能够建立良好的关系，因为它们能够感受到彼此的伤痛、敏感、羞怯以及建立联系时的犹豫。它们都需要大量的温柔、细心和循序渐进的信任过程。一些最重要的工作是在幸存者骑上马之前完成的，通过刷毛、梳理毛发、清洁马匹、牵着马散步或喂食等方式，让幸存者花时间了解彼此。它们逐渐建立起依恋，并发展出一些沟通的迹象。”
Though dogs will approach almost anyone with affection, horses, more discriminating, will choose the people they like, and clients soon realize they are special in some unique way for their horse. Nancy continues, “Every day I hear clients exclaim how good it feels when they are chosen by a certain horse. It boosts their spirits, not just their self-esteem, when they say, “Look, he walked right up to me. He nuzzled me. He really likes me!” Horses quickly show us what sensitive qualities they need from us, but they definitely must have our clear direction and boundaries. They will test our limits and our patience, and we must be steady, calm, and determined.”
虽然狗几乎会对任何人表现出亲昵，但马却更加挑剔，它们会选择自己喜欢的人。客户很快就会意识到，自己对马来说有着某种独特的特殊意义。南希继续说道：“我每天都能听到客户们惊叹，当他们被某匹马选中时，感觉有多么美好。当他们说‘你看，它径直走到我跟前，用鼻子蹭我，它真的很喜欢我！’时，这不仅提升了他们的自尊心，也让他们精神振奋。” 马很快就会向我们展示它们需要我们具备哪些敏感的品质，但它们也绝对需要我们明确的引导和界限。它们会考验我们的极限和耐心，而我们必须保持沉着、冷静和坚定。”
Nancy’s comments stirred some old, die-hard beliefs still inside me about how our softness, gentleness, and patience as comforters could be exploited by others. If we were empathic and generous with each other, without boundaries and clarity, we could get sucked into being too submissive, too available to others, or self-sacrificing. I and many highly empathic people I knew, especially when I was younger, had struggled with our softheartedness, as controlling people tried to take advantage of us. Boundaries, firmness, and clarity seemed to go against the ingrained images of comforters in our minds, as our softer, comforting qualities seemed opposed to the “real world” qualities of toughness, guile, and dominance. Softness was still equated with weakness, subservience, and gullibility in our culture, so we empathic types were forced to go against our true natures, to be wary of our softheartedness to protect ourselves. Trauma survivors, especially of abuse, were extremely guarded against their softer, compassionate attributes that previously may have misled them to forgiving and tolerating their perpetrators. Many trauma survivors couldn’t risk being soft in a world that was still hard to be soft in—where bullying, controlling people still thrived in many workplaces, schools, courts, or on the streets. And because their softness had gotten them in trouble with relationships, they hardened themselves, often to their own detriment, and missed out on opportunities to be comforting.
南希的话触动了我内心深处一些根深蒂固的旧观念，那就是我们作为安慰者的温柔、善良和耐心可能会被他人利用。如果我们彼此富有同情心和慷慨大方，却缺乏界限和清晰的沟通，我们就很容易变得过于顺从、过于随和或自我牺牲。我和我认识的许多同理心很强的人，尤其是在我年轻的时候，都曾与自己的心软作斗争，因为那些控制欲强的人总是试图利用我们。界限、坚定和清晰的沟通似乎与我们脑海中根深蒂固的安慰者形象相悖，因为我们温柔体贴的特质似乎与“现实世界”中强硬、狡猾和支配的特质格格不入。在我们的文化中，温柔仍然等同于软弱、顺从和轻信，所以我们这些富有同理心的人被迫违背自己的本性，警惕自己的心软以保护自己。创伤幸存者，尤其是遭受虐待的幸存者，会极力克制自己内心柔软、富有同情心的一面，因为这些特质过去可能会让他们原谅甚至容忍施虐者。许多创伤幸存者不敢冒险展现自己的柔软，因为在这个世界上，温柔依然难以维系——欺凌和控制在职场、学校、法庭乃至街头巷尾仍然盛行。由于他们的柔软曾让他们在人际关系中陷入困境，他们变得冷酷无情，这往往对他们自身有害，也让他们错失了安慰他人的机会。
Yet Nancy was saying we didn’t have to become hardened in order to be hard sometimes, and horses showed us the grace of this truth. Horses proved to us we did not have to completely let down our guard to be soft and comforting. We could sustain good boundaries and be clear and firm about our availability, and still be soft as comforters. She offered, by way of the wisdom of horses, a fresh perspective for comforters to reconcile our softness with our strength. Indeed, horses taught us the power of soft strength.
然而，南希的意思是，我们不必变得冷酷无情才能偶尔展现坚强，而马匹则向我们展现了这一真理的精髓。马匹向我们证明，我们不必完全放下戒备才能温柔体贴。我们可以保持良好的界限，清晰而坚定地表明自己的意愿，同时依然温柔地安慰他人。她借由马匹的智慧，为安慰者提供了一个全新的视角，帮助我们调和温柔与力量。的确，马匹教会了我们柔和的力量。

What Horses Teach Us as Comforters and Healers
马作为安慰者和治愈者教会我们的什么
Nancy shares the most important things horses can teach us:
• Horses don’t lie. We learn to be scrupulously honest with ourselves and others.
• Horses are mirrors of our emotions and behaviors. If we have been denying or neglecting to face truths about ourselves, horses will reveal what we need to observe. Horses teach comforters to be aware of their own vulnerabilities and limitations, before approaching someone in distress, or else they might get pulled into actions they would regret later.
• Horses lower our blood pressure and calm us down.
• Horses teach us to be keenly aware of our environment and our effects on our environment.
• Horses teach us to be clear and firm as comforters, but not at the expense of our gentler, softer qualities.
南希分享了马能教会我们最重要的几件事：• 马不会说谎。我们学会对自己和他人绝对诚实。• 马就像一面镜子，映照出我们的情绪和行为。如果我们一直否认或忽视自身的真相，马会揭示我们需要观察的东西。马教会那些安慰他人的人，在接近处于困境中的人之前，要意识到自身的脆弱和局限，否则他们可能会做出日后后悔的事情。• 马能降低我们的血压，让我们平静下来。• 马教会我们敏锐地觉察周围环境以及我们对环境的影响。• 马教会我们作为安慰者要清晰而坚定，但不能因此而失去我们温柔的一面。

THE COMFORT OF CONTINUITY: RITUALS, ROUTINES, AND SEASONS

延续带来的慰藉：仪式、惯例和季节

Laura Hare
劳拉·黑尔
Children’s center director for thirty years; creator of nature programs for children
担任儿童中心主任三十年；儿童自然教育项目的创建者
Former Director, The Growing Tree Richmond, Virginia
前任主任，弗吉尼亚州里士满市“成长之树”项目
Our pets especially teach us the comfort of continuity, as they are creatures of habit who find great joy in the most mundane daily routines with us.
我们的宠物尤其教会了我们持续生活的舒适感，因为它们是习惯性动物，能从与我们一起最平凡的日常活动中获得极大的快乐。
Core Comforting Qualities: Reliability and Patience
核心舒适品质：可靠性和耐心
Laura greets me at the front door of her little lavender bungalow bedecked with window boxes full of pansies. A swinging chair with yellow cushions hangs on her front porch in the cool shade. She quickly closes the door behind me so her cats don’t run out, then gives me a big hug. She eagerly leads me to her back lawn to the tiny pond she built by several old apple trees. She points to her amazingly hardy “Terminator” goldfish in the pond, who have survived predators, ice storms, droughts, and heat waves. Next she shows me her cozy patio with potted geraniums, and then takes me to her sunroom with wide arched windows, where the evening sun streams through her crystals and across her hanging baskets of ivy.
劳拉在她那间淡紫色小平房的门口迎接我，窗台上摆满了种满三色堇的花箱。凉爽的阴凉处，门廊上挂着一把铺着黄色软垫的秋千椅。她迅速关上身后的门，以免猫咪跑出去，然后给了我一个大大的拥抱。她热情地带我来到后院，来到她用几棵老苹果树建造的小池塘边。她指着池塘里那些生命力惊人的“终结者”金鱼，它们经历了掠食者的袭击、冰暴、干旱和热浪的考验。接着，她带我参观了摆放着盆栽天竺葵的舒适露台，然后又带我来到阳光房，那里有宽大的拱形窗户，傍晚的阳光透过水晶和悬挂的常春藤花篮洒进来。
She invites me to sit in a well-cushioned old wicker chair and hands me an iced tea. I sip it down quickly, under her wide ceiling fan on this balmy June evening in Richmond, Virginia.
她邀请我坐到一张舒适的旧藤椅上，递给我一杯冰茶。在这个温暖的六月夜晚，弗吉尼亚州里士满，我坐在她家宽大的吊扇下，快速地喝完了茶。
Laura sits back snugly on her blue gingham sofa with her two black cats, on either side of her lap, watching every move I make.
劳拉舒服地靠在蓝色格子沙发上，两只黑猫分别趴在她腿的两侧，注视着我的一举一动。
In her cat’s astute glare, I glance self-consciously around her room, admiring her handiwork, her country quilts and throws, painted floral cabinets, baskets of seashells, and then happily remember our plans for tomorrow.
在她的猫敏锐的目光注视下，我有些不自在地环顾她的房间，欣赏着她的手艺、乡村风格的被子和毯子、彩绘花卉橱柜、贝壳篮，然后愉快地想起我们明天的计划。
“Laura, we are definitely going to Charles City Tavern tomorrow?”
“劳拉，我们明天肯定要去查尔斯城酒馆吧？”
“It’s a go—I can’t wait.” She shakes her head in amazement. “Wow . . . I can’t believe it’s been a year since I’ve seen you.” She hoots out loud and reaches across the coffee table to give me a high five. “Charles City Tavern tomorrow!” Annoyed with all the attention I am getting, her cats jump off the couch in protest, but don’t get farther than the doorway, where they lie down, their backs toward us, feigning they aren’t listening.
“成行了——我等不及了。”她惊讶地摇摇头。“哇……真不敢相信已经一年没见你了。”她大声欢呼，越过咖啡桌和我击掌。“明天去查尔斯城酒馆！”她的猫咪们似乎被我受到的关注弄得有些不耐烦，从沙发上跳下来表示抗议，但还没跑出门口就趴了下来，背对着我们，装作没听见。
Throughout our twenty-five-year friendship, Laura and I have kept sacred our pilgrimage to Charles City on the lush, green banks of the James River east of Richmond. We adore this old, gracious tavern, and always sit on the screened porch next to an herb garden, enjoying our Saturday midafternoon lunch, finishing it with our usual bourbon-soaked pecan pie with vanilla ice cream for dessert. Afterward, happily dazed in a sugar rush, we stroll amid the willow trees, pink roses, and irises all swaying in the moist, salty breezes streaming from the flat fields of soy and peanuts for miles around us.
在长达二十五年的友谊中，我和劳拉始终珍视着前往查尔斯城的朝圣之旅。查尔斯城位于里士满以东，詹姆斯河畔绿树成荫，景色宜人。我们钟爱这家古老而优雅的小酒馆，总是坐在香草园旁的纱窗门廊上，享用周六下午的午餐，最后以我们常点的波旁威士忌浸山核桃派配香草冰淇淋作为甜点。之后，我们沉浸在甜蜜的幸福中，漫步在柳树、粉红玫瑰和鸢尾花之间，它们在潮湿咸涩的微风中摇曳生姿，微风从周围绵延数英里的平坦大豆和花生田吹来。
Our ritual at Charles City Tavern has become increasingly more meaningful over the past ten years, ever since I moved away to Maine. If Laura and I lived to our eighties, even if the tavern fell into ruins, we’d still be walking along the James River every June for our annual reunion. I’ve always been able to count on Laura, and more than most friends and colleagues, she values the role of rituals, the magic of keeping reunions going, even for decades. Laura has always been the one to rely on, to show up for the life passages, great or small, for the people she loves. She honors the continuity of events with everyone in her life, from her family members, to the children she teaches, to her friends and colleagues.
自从我十年前搬到缅因州后，我们在查尔斯城酒馆的聚会仪式变得越来越有意义。如果我和劳拉都能活到八十岁，即使酒馆最终沦为废墟，我们每年六月依然会沿着詹姆斯河漫步，举行我们的年度聚会。我一直都很信赖劳拉，她比大多数朋友和同事都更重视仪式，重视维系聚会的魔力，即使持续几十年也如此。劳拉总是值得信赖，无论人生大事小事，她都会陪伴在她所爱的人身边。她尊重生命中每个人的延续，从家人到她教的孩子，再到她的朋友和同事。
This Friday evening we talk for a long time, almost to midnight, about Laura’s understanding of the art of comforting. In a nutshell for her, it’s all about sustaining continuity in our relationships. We need our reunions, our rituals, our little routines and cycles, especially children. Nature teaches this always, through the tides, moons, migrations, seasons, and generations we share with all of creation.
这个周五晚上，我们聊了很久，几乎到午夜，探讨劳拉对安慰艺术的理解。对她来说，关键在于维系人际关系的连续性。我们需要重聚、仪式、日常习惯和循环，尤其是对孩子而言。大自然通过潮汐、月亮、迁徙、季节更迭以及我们与万物共享的世代更迭，无时无刻不在教导我们这一点。


L AURA HAS DIRECTED children’s programs for twenty-eight years, teaching life skills through a better understanding of the cycles and ways of nature. She’s always had a knack for creating routines and rituals that make kids look forward to activities and roles. Whether it’s getting kids psyched for a Halloween Spook Night, cleaning Muffy the turtle’s tank, awaiting the birth of more bunnies from Stewey and Petunia, navigating maps for camping trips, or planting a cherry tree, she brilliantly taps the power of their anticipation and suspense.
劳拉从事儿童节目指导工作已有二十八年，她通过让孩子们更好地理解自然循环和规律，来教授他们生活技能。她一直擅长创造各种日常活动和仪式，让孩子们对即将参与的活动和角色充满期待。无论是让孩子们兴奋地迎接万圣节惊魂夜，清理乌龟玛菲的鱼缸，等待斯图伊和佩图尼亚的兔子宝宝出生，为露营旅行绘制地图，还是种植樱桃树，她都能巧妙地利用孩子们的期待和兴奋。
Laura previously specialized in working with children with disabilities, launching one of the first community inclusion initiatives in Virginia for after-school and recreational programs that integrated children with disabilities into mainstream activities. Her highly successful program at the Growing Tree in Richmond became the actual model for the Everybuddy Program of the Chesterfield public school system.
劳拉此前专注于为残疾儿童提供服务，她在弗吉尼亚州率先发起了一项社区融合计划，旨在通过课后和娱乐项目将残疾儿童融入主流活动。她在里士满“成长之树”（Growing Tree）开展的这项卓有成效的项目，后来成为切斯特菲尔德公立学校系统“人人伙伴计划”（Everybuddy Program）的蓝本。
At the heart of her success in integrating children with disabilities with other children in the mainstream is her practice of bringing nature and animals into her learning places. Everyone plays an important role, as each child is responsible for caring for their chosen animal, their plant, or their garden. When they take on the role of caregivers, a leveling process is established for all children, no matter how academically successful or not, how popular or not, or how deprived or not a child’s background may be. No one is any better than anyone else, but everyone is equally accountable for what they do in nurturing the animals who depend on them.
她成功地将残疾儿童融入主流教育体系的核心在于，她将自然和动物引入学习场所。每个人都扮演着重要的角色，每个孩子都负责照料自己选择的动物、植物或花园。当他们承担起照料者的角色时，所有孩子之间便建立了一种平等的关系，无论他们的学业成绩如何、受欢迎程度如何、出身背景如何。没有人比其他人更优秀，每个人都对他们照料依赖他们的动物负有同等的责任。
Grounded by rituals and routines, kids learn by continuity, Laura attests. Things we learn certainly sink in better when we watch over time how life moves in cycles, how habits form, and how people commit to work together. Further, continuity is deeply reassuring, a foundation for facing loss and change in life. In the face of life transitions, it’s important to keep some things as continuous as possible, whether it’s having dinner together at the same time of evening, or walking the dogs, or doing laundry every Saturday. “But continuity requires our reliability and keeping commitments. We’ve got to be able to count on each other, or else we learn not to count on each other, and lose our faith in our promises, to each other as well as ourselves. Kids are so beautiful when they light up with anticipation for a big event, when they are counting on everyone to show up, but with too many no-shows, they lose their spirit, get discouraged, cynical. It’s easy to understand why some of them turn too much to technology, to computers, video games, TV, and virtual worlds for continuity in their lives,” Laura says with a sigh.
劳拉证实，孩子们在仪式和日常习惯的熏陶下，通过持续性来学习。随着时间的推移，当我们观察生活如何循环往复、习惯如何养成、人们如何携手合作时，我们所学到的东西无疑会更加深入人心。此外，持续性能给人带来深深的安心感，是面对人生中的失落和变迁的基础。面对人生的种种转变，尽可能地保持某些事情的连续性至关重要，例如每天晚上同一时间一起吃晚饭、遛狗，或者每周六一起洗衣服。 “但维系关系需要我们的可靠性和信守承诺。我们必须能够彼此信赖，否则我们就会学会不信任彼此，最终失去对彼此以及对自己的承诺的信心。孩子们在期待重要活动时，脸上洋溢着兴奋的光芒，他们盼望着每个人都能到场，那时的他们是多么可爱。但如果太多人缺席，他们就会失去热情，变得沮丧、愤世嫉俗。很容易理解为什么有些孩子会过度依赖科技，依赖电脑、电子游戏、电视和虚拟世界来寻求生活的延续性，”劳拉叹了口气说道。
Laura isn’t against technology, but she worries that we aren’t learning essential comforting skills if we get too caught up in the instant gratification of “following” people on cell phones, BlackBerry phones, and Twitter. Instant gratification in quick cell calls and social networking can’t teach us the slower, gentler, mostly nonverbal language of comforting. And virtual people can’t touch us, hold us.
劳拉并不反对科技，但她担心，如果我们过于沉迷于在手机、黑莓手机和推特上“关注”他人所带来的即时满足感，就会错过学习必要的安慰技巧。快速的通话和社交网络带来的即时满足感，无法教会我们那种更缓慢、更温柔、大多非语言的安慰方式。而且，虚拟世界里的人也无法触碰我们，拥抱我们。
Laura continues, “Technology is important and has its place, but I believe humans are starving for the same direct attention our pets crave. With animals, being their only virtual buddies doesn’t do the trick. Our pets will die of loneliness without our hands-on affection, smiles, voices, hugs, and play time. And by play time, I mean getting down on our hands and knees, being silly, making crazy sounds, roughhousing a bit. And, I dare say, too many of the kids I teach and their parents are lonely for these same comforts.”
劳拉继续说道：“科技固然重要，也自有其用武之地，但我相信人类渴望得到宠物所渴望的那种直接的关注。对动物来说，仅仅成为它们唯一的虚拟伙伴是远远不够的。如果没有我们亲身的抚摸、微笑、声音、拥抱和玩耍，我们的宠物会孤独地死去。而我说的玩耍，是指和它们一起蹲下来，做些傻事，发出各种奇奇怪怪的声音，玩闹一番。而且，我敢说，我教的很多孩子和他们的父母也同样渴望这些慰藉。”
Nurturing animals and the earth creates continuity in our lives, as others depend on us to grow and survive. We are hardwired to nurture other living beings, and we often don’t realize this until we discover the joys of taking care of even the smallest of creatures. Laura reminisced on her childhood farm experiences and how she tries to bring similar experiences to children in her work today.
呵护动物和土地能使我们的生活得以延续，因为其他生命也依赖我们成长和生存。我们天生就具有关爱其他生物的本能，而我们往往直到体验到照顾哪怕是最微小的生命所带来的乐趣时，才会意识到这一点。劳拉回忆起她童年在农场的经历，以及她如今如何在工作中努力为孩子们带来类似的体验。
“I learned the wisdom and comfort of nature from my childhood experiences on my grandparents’ farm in the rolling hills of western Virginia. To this day, I carry inside me the blessings of growing up with the freedom to jump into haystacks, climb oak trees, and play in our tree houses. We swam in a large pond fed by a bubbling stream, and napped on warm moss under weeping willow trees. We canned beans, peaches, and tomatoes and pickled cucumbers. We tended a two-acre vegetable garden and picked apples, pears, and peaches from our plentiful orchards. We nurtured baby chicks and ducklings and played with dozens of dogs and cats. Looking back, I realize I was very, very fortunate to have spent so many idyllic years learning about life on a farm.
“我在弗吉尼亚州西部连绵起伏的丘陵地带，祖父母的农场里度过的童年时光，让我领悟了大自然的智慧和慰藉。直到今天，我依然珍藏着那段自由自在的童年时光，我可以跳进干草堆，爬上橡树，在树屋里玩耍。我们在潺潺溪流汇入的大池塘里游泳，在垂柳下温暖的苔藓上小憩。我们腌制豆子、桃子和西红柿，腌黄瓜。我们照料着两英亩的菜园，从丰饶的果园里采摘苹果、梨和桃子。我们精心照料小鸡和小鸭，和几十只猫狗玩耍。回首往事，我意识到自己非常非常幸运，能够在那段田园诗般的农场生活中度过那么多美好的时光。”
“But further, this wisdom of nature was ultimately comforting for me. Children can better understand loss, even death, with nature, when they witness the life cycles, seasons, the frailty as well as resilience of living beings. Knowing that life goes on, no matter what, is comforting. Knowing that nature always has something to teach us, even in loss, is comforting.
“但更重要的是，大自然的这种智慧最终给了我安慰。孩子们通过观察生命的循环、四季更迭、生物的脆弱与韧性，能够更好地理解失去，甚至是死亡。知道生命无论如何都会继续，这令人感到安慰。知道即使在失去中，大自然也总能教会我们一些东西，这令人感到安慰。”
“Today, as a child care director, I have built educational programs inspired by the wisdom and comfort of the animals of my life and my years at my grandparents’ farm.”
“如今，作为一名儿童保育主管，我根据我生活中遇到的动物的智慧和带给我的慰藉，以及我在祖父母农场度过的岁月，创建了一系列教育项目。”
Laura’s Comforting Practices Teaching Comforting Skills with Nature at the Growing Tree
劳拉的舒缓疗法：在成长之树中运用自然教授舒缓技巧
At Laura’s Growing Tree program, the children each cared for their own animal. Inherent in the act of caregiving were ideal opportunities to practice comforting skills, to develop a strong sense of continuity, belonging, teamwork, and community over the years.
在劳拉的“成长之树”项目中，孩子们各自照料自己的动物。照料动物的过程本身就提供了绝佳的机会，让他们练习安抚动物的技巧，并在多年的成长过程中培养强烈的归属感、团队合作精神和社区意识。
HERE ARE THE MOST IMPORTANT COMFORTING QUALITIES CHILDREN HAVE LEARNED, BY BUILDING RELATIONSHIPS WITH THEIR PETS AND PLANTS:
以下是孩子们通过与宠物和植物建立关系而学到的最重要的几种令人感到安慰的品质：

Reliability 可靠性
If Swimmy the goldfish doesn’t get his meals on time, he gets into fights with the other fish and causes trouble in the tank. To keep harmony in the tank, feeding times have to be consistent, so we need to be dependable for feeding Swimmy.
如果金鱼斯威米没有按时吃到饭，它就会和其他鱼打架，给鱼缸带来麻烦。为了维持鱼缸的和谐，喂食时间必须规律，所以我们需要按时喂斯威米。
Empathy 共情
When Louie the cockatiel is upset and squawking, the children stop whatever they are doing and listen to him, to tune in to him so they can understand what is upsetting him.
当鹦鹉路易生气地叫唤时，孩子们会停下手中的一切，倾听它，以便了解是什么让它生气。
Gentleness, Patience, Calmness 温柔、耐心、冷静
If Louie is still squawking, the children quiet down, slow down, and gently step closer to him to see what he needs to calm down. They lower their voices and speak softly to him. If a child is putting her hands in his cage to add water when Louie is nervous, she needs to patiently, delicately pick up his little water bowl.
如果路易还在叫，孩子们就安静下来，放慢脚步，轻轻地靠近他，看看他需要什么才能平静下来。他们降低音量，轻声细语地和他说话。如果孩子在路易紧张的时候把手伸进笼子里加水，她需要耐心、轻柔地拿起他的小水碗。
Presence 在场
If Muffy the turtle is slowly inching her way through the room, we need to be very careful where we put our feet. If we hold Stewey and Petunia’s tiny baby rabbits, we must be attentive and focus closely, as they are fragile and need our utmost care.
如果小乌龟玛菲正慢慢地在房间里挪动，我们就得格外小心脚下。如果我们抱起斯图伊和佩图尼亚的小兔子，就必须全神贯注，因为它们很脆弱，需要我们格外呵护。
Respect and Appreciation 尊重与感激
If Petunia is tired and resting with her babies who are sleeping, we need to respect her needs and leave them alone for a while. We would not disturb Petunia by petting her or picking her up for a cuddle.
如果佩图尼亚累了，正和睡着的宝宝们一起休息，我们应该尊重她的需要，让它们安静一会儿。不要去抚摸佩图尼亚，也不要抱起她亲昵，打扰她。
Caring 关怀
When Muffy the turtle became very ill with a bacterial infection, Laura and the children decided to try to save Muffy by carefully giving her a series of injections into her tiny legs. A child was chosen to hold Muffy steadily while Laura administered the injections for several days. The children gathered every day to watch closely this delicate treatment. Though Muffy nearly died, she did come through finally and lived another seven years afterward.
小乌龟玛菲感染了细菌，病得很重。劳拉和孩子们决定尽力救治玛菲，他们小心翼翼地给玛菲的小腿注射了一系列药物。他们选了一个孩子稳稳地托住玛菲，劳拉则连续几天给她注射。孩子们每天都聚在一起，仔细观察这精细的治疗过程。玛菲虽然一度濒临死亡，但最终还是挺了过来，之后又活了七年。
Clarity and Boundaries 清晰度和界限
It would be confusing and stressful for Oreo the guinea pig to have the whole yard to run in for one day, and then be kept in his cage for another day. Oreo’s caregivers all need to uphold the same rules and behaviors and be unified in how and where they play with him.
对于豚鼠奥利奥来说，如果一天让它在整个院子里自由奔跑，另一天又被关在笼子里，这会让它感到困惑和压力。奥利奥的所有照料者都需要遵守相同的规则和行为规范，并且在与它玩耍的方式和地点上保持一致。
Comforting in Times of Loss: Louie’s Stones and Whitney’s Tree 抚慰失落之痛：路易的石头和惠特尼的树
In caring for animals, the children sometimes faced loss and death, and learned to comfort themselves and each other when providing memorial ceremonies for their pets.
在照顾动物的过程中，孩子们有时会面临失去和死亡，并学会了在为宠物举行追悼仪式时安慰自己和彼此。
When Louie the cockatiel died of old age, the children laid him in a shoe box, wrapped carefully in a doll’s blanket with his favorite things—his bell, his whistle, and some birdseed. He was buried at the end of the backyard, inside a circle of small stones by a bush. For his funeral, the children sang songs, read poems, and shared memories in his honor.
路易，这只玄凤鹦鹉，寿终正寝。孩子们把它放在鞋盒里，用娃娃毯子仔细包裹好，里面放着它最喜欢的东西——铃铛、哨子和一些鸟食。它被埋在后院尽头，灌木丛旁用小石头围成的圆圈里。葬礼上，孩子们唱歌、朗诵诗歌，分享与它相处的点点滴滴，以此缅怀它。
A year later, a girl named Whitney from the Growing Tree program suddenly and tragically died in a boating accident with her father the day after Valentine’s Day. Laura met with the children at the Growing Tree and talked about Whitney’s death in an honest, sensitive way. After remembering in great detail what they had done for Louie’s funeral, the children suggested planting a tree for Whitney and designed a ceremony.
一年后，来自“成长之树”项目的女孩惠特尼在情人节后的第二天，和父亲一起遭遇船难，不幸身亡。劳拉与“成长之树”项目的孩子们见面，以真诚而感人的方式谈论了惠特尼的离世。孩子们详细回忆了他们为路易的葬礼所做的一切，并提议为惠特尼种一棵树，还设计了一场纪念仪式。
A few weeks later, a cherry tree was planted in the front yard of the Growing Tree as a memorial ceremony for Whitney’s family members and her fellow students. The children, Laura, other staff, and Whitney’s family members all held hands and made a circle around Whitney’s cherry tree after it was planted and offered prayers and blessings. The children shared their poems, pictures, and Whitney’s favorite songs.
几周后，为了纪念惠特尼的家人和同学们，在“成长之树”学校的前院种下了一棵樱桃树。孩子们、劳拉、其他教职工以及惠特尼的家人手拉手，围成一个圈，为这棵樱桃树祈祷祝福。孩子们还分享了他们创作的诗歌、画作以及惠特尼生前最喜欢的歌曲。
Over the years, Whitney’s tree has grown strong and tall, and many former students of the Growing Tree, now adults, stop by to remember her.
多年来，惠特尼的树长得又高又壮，许多以前在这棵成长之树上学习的学生，现在都已长大成人，他们会时不时地来这里缅怀她。
Laura’s Comforting Suggestions for Families
劳拉给家庭的贴心建议
As a child care director, Laura observes that families need to gather together on a regular basis to keep the art of comforting alive. Essentially, we can create our own traditions, our own memory-makers.
作为一名托儿所主任，劳拉观察到，家庭成员需要定期团聚，才能维系彼此关怀的艺术。从本质上讲，我们可以创造属于我们自己的传统，创造属于我们自己的回忆。
• Great family traditions, rituals, memory-makers
Children tell Laura constantly what traditions they enjoy, especially events centered on nature, animals, or the seasons. They love it when adults make these events special, meaningful, memorable. The simplest activity can be turned into a rewarding ritual together.
• 美好的家庭传统、仪式和回忆：孩子们经常告诉劳拉他们喜欢哪些传统，尤其是那些与自然、动物或季节相关的活动。他们很喜欢大人把这些活动变得特别、有意义、令人难忘。最简单的活动也能变成一段美好的共同仪式。
HERE ARE SOME FAVORITE ACTIVITIES WITH ANIMALS AND NATURE THAT CHILDREN TALK ABOUT FOR YEARS AND YEARS:
• Getting out the plastic swimming (wading) pool, or turning on the sprinklers at the start of the summer to play in the water is a ritual in itself! Pool parties can be an annual tradition (often around Memorial Day). Getting out the lounge chairs, the hammock, or the deck chairs to sit outside or on the porch.
• Going on a picnic or a day trip to a favorite natural park or local sandy beach (by a lake, river, or ocean) in the warmer seasons. Take photos, too.
• Birthday parties for our pets, or parties for their special occasions, including playing games with their toys and watching them play.
• Playing Frisbee or other ball game with our dogs, family, and friends in the backyard or the park on the weekends.
• A show-and-tell event for sharing the stories and pictures of our pets or of other animals we have known or loved (dog stories, cat stories, horse stories, gerbil stories . . .). Also, we can create show-and-tell events after completing any special environmental projects, such as going to the park to clean up trash and debris, or doing other community service projects for our environment.
• Planting seeds in the spring for gardens, window boxes, or indoor plants. Tree-planting ceremonies.
• Making an annual video or movie of a favorite activity with our pets, to enjoy later as a follow-up event with popcorn.
以下是一些孩子们多年来津津乐道的与动物和大自然相关的精彩活动：• 夏天伊始，拿出塑料游泳池（或戏水池），或者打开洒水器玩水，本身就是一种仪式！泳池派对可以成为一项年度传统（通常在阵亡将士纪念日前后）。拿出躺椅、吊床或甲板椅，坐在户外或门廊上。• 在温暖的季节，去野餐或一日游，去最喜欢的自然公园或当地的沙滩（湖边、河边或海边）。别忘了拍照留念。 • 为宠物举办生日派对或其他特殊场合的聚会，包括和它们一起玩玩具游戏，以及观看它们玩耍。• 周末和家人朋友在后院或公园里与狗狗一起玩飞盘或其他球类游戏。• 举办“分享会”，分享我们宠物或其他我们认识或喜爱过的动物的故事和照片（狗狗的故事、猫咪的故事、马的故事、沙鼠的故事……）。此外，我们还可以在完成一些特别的环保项目后举办“分享会”，例如去公园清理垃圾，或参与其他社区环保服务项目。• 春天播种，种植花园、窗台花箱或室内植物。举行植树仪式。• 每年制作一段与宠物一起进行的精彩活动的视频或影片，以便日后一边享用爆米花一边观看。
OTHER TRADITIONS AND RITUALS
其他传统和仪式
• A regular sports event (seasonal) to attend together. Even the trip to the stadium can be a ritual in itself.
• 定期一起观看体育赛事（季节性赛事）。甚至去体育场的路程本身也可以成为一种仪式。
• A monthly Saturday or Sunday movie matinee, with an after-movie bite to eat, to talk about the movie or just visit.
• 每月一次周六或周日下午的电影放映，电影结束后提供小吃，供大家讨论电影或只是闲聊。
• A trip to a museum for a special exhibit.
• 去博物馆参观特别展览。
• Going to annual parades, participating in parades.
• 参加年度游行。
• A trip to a historic landmark.
• 参观历史古迹。
• Fashion shows with fun clothing or costumes, set to lively music so we can strut down the “catwalk.”
• 时装秀，穿着有趣的服装或戏服，配上欢快的音乐，我们可以昂首阔步地走上“T台”。
• Going to the library for story hour with a brown-bag lunch.
• 带着自带午餐去图书馆参加故事时间。
• Every fall, or for Thanksgiving, loading up cans of food to donate to the local food bank.
• 每年秋季或感恩节期间，都会收集罐头食品捐赠给当地食品银行。

THE RADIANCE OF STILLNESS

静谧的光辉

Jen Deraspe
珍·德拉斯佩
Director and Owner, Nurture Through Nature, an eco-retreat center in Denmark, Maine
缅因州丹麦镇生态静修中心“自然疗愈”的负责人兼所有者
We ask ourselves, “How can I connect with nature?” as if we’ve forgotten we already are a part of nature. We are nature—as much as any tree, flower, or bird. If we take a moment to be still and quiet, we can reconnect with the source of all life through sacred silence.
我们常常问自己：“我该如何与自然连接？”仿佛忘记了我们本身就是自然的一部分。我们就是自然——就像任何一棵树、一朵花、一只鸟一样。如果我们能静下心来，保持安静，就能通过神圣的静默重新与万物之源连接。
Core Comforting Qualities: Stillness and Presence
核心舒适特质：静谧与临在
On a mission to write my column, “Leaps of Faith,” for the Maine Women’s Journal two years ago, I drove to interview Jen at her retreat center in western Maine. I passed through mountains glowing in autumn foliage, flowing rapids, and deep blue lakes before reaching a cluster of cabins in the pines off a dirt road. I stepped out of my car in splendidly rugged wilderness, in scenery that guests like me hoped to find when they came from Boston, New York, or even Portland, Maine. Jen quickly and warmly greeted me and led me to her largest cabin, where she pointed out her dining and communal areas and showed me one of the guest rooms. I was struck by the elegant simplicity of the golden red pinewood floors, tables, and walls, and the radiant fresh-picked wildflowers and ferns. Her woodstove provided toasty heat by the table we chose for our interview. Jen poured me and herself a cup of peppermint tea from a blue teapot. Looking across the table, I spotted a striking photograph of a white owl.
两年前，为了给《缅因州女性杂志》撰写专栏“信仰的飞跃”，我驱车前往缅因州西部，采访珍在她静修中心的住处。沿途我经过秋色斑斓的群山、奔流的溪流和湛蓝的湖泊，最终抵达一条土路旁松林中的一簇小木屋。我下车后，眼前展现出壮丽而原始的自然风光，这正是像我这样的客人，即使从波士顿、纽约，甚至是缅因州波特兰远道而来，也渴望看到的景色。珍热情地迎接了我，并带我来到她最大的小木屋。她向我介绍了餐厅和公共区域，还带我参观了一间客房。金红色的松木地板、桌子和墙壁，以及那些鲜嫩的野花和蕨类植物，都让我眼前一亮，简洁而优雅。我们选择在一张桌子旁进行采访，柴火炉散发出温暖的气息。珍用一个蓝色的茶壶，给自己和我各倒了一杯薄荷茶。目光越过桌子，我看到一张引人注目的白色猫头鹰照片。
“That owl gives me a chill, a good kind of chill,” I told Jen. “I love the eyes, those soulful eyes, so much awareness in those eyes.”
“那只猫头鹰让我感到一阵寒意，一种美好的寒意，”我告诉珍。“我喜欢它的眼睛，那双充满灵性的眼睛，那双眼睛里充满了觉察。”
Jen sat back, paused, and smiled lovingly at the owl picture. “It is a beautiful shot, isn’t it?”
珍向后靠了靠，停顿了一下，满怀爱意地看着猫头鹰的照片。“拍得真漂亮，不是吗？”
“Really, really is . . . Who took the photo?” I asked eagerly.
“真的，真的是……谁拍的照片？”我急切地问道。
“Don’t know . . . I don’t think I’ve ever known.” She seemed perfectly content not knowing. We enjoyed a moment of stillness, in reverence of the owl’s eyes.
“不知道……我想我从来都不知道。”她似乎很满足于这种未知的状态。我们静静地欣赏着猫头鹰的眼睛，享受着片刻的宁静。
“We can hear owls not too far from here,” she added softly.
“我们能听到离这里不远的猫头鹰的叫声，”她轻声补充道。
Jen put me at ease as we shared other bird encounters with blue herons and hawks. We held our mugs of steaming tea, gazing through the window as the wind lifted and coaxed the orange and yellow leaves off their trees. Autumn demanded our attention and we welcomed its presence. Soon, looking back at Jen checking the logs piled beside her woodstove, my curiosity got me going again, and I asked her about her background.
珍让我感到很放松，我们一起分享了之前遇到的蓝鹭和鹰的经历。我们捧着热气腾腾的茶，望着窗外，只见微风拂过，吹落了树上橙黄相间的树叶。秋天的气息扑面而来，我们欣然接受。很快，我回头看到珍正在查看堆放在炉子旁的木柴，好奇心再次涌上心头，我便问起了她的背景。
Having a passion for health and wellness, Jen got her master’s degree in sports medicine and served on the faculty and as the head athletic trainer for the University of Southern Maine for ten years, taking care of the health care needs of the college athletes. Over time, she felt compelled to work with people in a more holistic way, including nature as a pathway toward stillness and healing. In that realization, she resigned from that line of work and began her own business, Nurture Through Nature, offering holistic canoe retreats for women, yoga instruction, and holistic personal training services. During that transition time, she earned her Maine guide’s license as well as her certification to be a yoga instructor. She found a mentor who worked with her to find stillness in her own busy mind and tendency to strive and drive hard and fast. In releasing her own distress, she got excited about sharing the possibilities found in peace. Along the journey, she found The Work of Byron Katie to be a direct path toward inner peace and freedom and became a facilitator of The Work of Byron Katie.
珍对健康和养生充满热情，她获得了运动医学硕士学位，并在南缅因大学担任了十年教职和首席运动训练师，负责大学运动员的健康护理。随着时间的推移，她感到自己应该以更全面的方式与人们合作，将自然视为通往平静和疗愈的途径。意识到这一点后，她辞去了原有的工作，创办了自己的公司“自然滋养”（Nurture Through Nature），为女性提供整体性的独木舟静修、瑜伽指导和整体性私人训练服务。在转型期间，她获得了缅因州向导执照和瑜伽教练资格认证。她找到了一位导师，帮助她在忙碌的思绪和追求卓越的倾向中找到内心的平静。在释放自身压力的过程中，她开始热衷于分享平和带来的种种可能性。在此过程中，她发现拜伦·凯蒂的“功课”（The Work of Byron Katie）是通往内心平静和自由的直接途径，并成为了“功课”的引导师。
With her versatile background, Jen could provide a holistic assortment of activities at her center through mindfulness eco-retreats. In the past year, she was focusing more on custom workshops “devoted to inner peace and presence,” facilitating retreats to “grow our own souls” and sharing The Work of Byron Katie as a means toward more clarity and less stress. She also accommodated custom retreats for those groups or couples who designed their own program, and hosted solo retreats for guests who simply wanted to spend private time in her woodland sanctuary.
凭借其多元化的背景，Jen能够通过正念生态静修，在她的中心提供丰富多彩的活动。过去一年，她更加专注于“致力于内心平静与觉察”的定制工作坊，组织“灵魂成长”的静修活动，并分享拜伦·凯蒂的“功课”，以此作为提升清晰度、减轻压力的途径。她也为那些自行设计行程的团体或情侣提供定制静修服务，并为那些只想在她林间静谧之地享受私人时光的客人举办个人静修。
Jen’s ability to invite moments of stillness and quietude, even during my first interview with her, inspired me to get to know her later as a colleague and as a master comforter. Clearly, Jen was a gentle teacher gifted at guiding us to enter our precious center, creating sacred pauses for our lives. She describes a powerful, profound experience in her life when facing the death of her brother as a child, and finding comfort in a moment of deep stillness—a moment that taught her the meaning of comfort.
珍在与我初次面谈时，就展现出营造静谧氛围的能力，这深深地感染了我，让我后来更愿意与她共事，并视她为一位抚慰大师。显然，珍是一位温柔的老师，她善于引导我们进入内心深处，为我们的生命创造神圣的停顿。她讲述了童年时面对哥哥去世的一段深刻而震撼的经历，以及在一段静谧的时光中找到慰藉——正是这段经历教会了她什么是真正的慰藉。
“I was eight years old when my older brother died. In the first days after his death, my father rocked me in his arms for a long time in the fading light of our family room, and we said nothing. The memory of this silent and deeply loving experience has stayed with me ever since, teaching me the power of what ‘being there’—being here, not ‘there’—really means for being human. I truly honor silence and stillness, how offering this for each other is essential for tapping our heart’s language, to be able to drop down into the embrace of our own hearts. Whether we give hugs or just sit softly with someone, our warmth is there when we allow sacred pause for our hearts to speak.”
“我八岁那年，哥哥去世了。在他去世后的最初几天，父亲在昏暗的客厅里，抱着我轻轻摇晃了很久，我们一句话也没说。这段无声却充满爱的记忆一直伴随着我，它教会了我‘身在其中’——活在当下，而非‘身在彼处’——对于人性的真正意义。我由衷地敬重沉默与宁静，因为我知道，彼此给予这种陪伴，对于我们聆听内心的语言至关重要，让我们能够敞开心扉，拥抱彼此。无论我们是拥抱，还是只是静静地陪伴，当我们允许内心静默片刻，让彼此的心诉说时，我们的温暖便会自然流露。”
More recently Jen has given me her time to explore more deeply the topic of comforting, especially the comfort of nature. I was keen on hearing what she thought about our societal disconnection from nature, and how this might interfere with our ability to be comforting.
最近，珍抽出时间与我深入探讨了“安慰”这个话题，尤其是大自然带来的安慰。我很想听听她对我们社会与自然脱节的看法，以及这种脱节会如何影响我们给予他人安慰的能力。
I was surprised by her answer. “We ask ourselves, ‘How can I connect with nature?’ as if we’ve forgotten we already are a part of nature. We are nature—as much as any tree, flower, or bird. We don’t always have to go outdoors. If we take a moment to be still and quiet, we can reconnect with the source of all life through sacred silence.”
她的回答让我很意外。“我们常常问自己，‘我该如何与自然连接？’，仿佛忘记了我们本身就是自然的一部分。我们就是自然——就像任何一棵树、一朵花、一只鸟一样。我们不必总是走到户外。如果我们能静下心来，享受片刻宁静，就能通过神圣的静默与万物之源重新连接。”
“So stillness and quiet give us a chance for nature to comfort us,” I echoed.
“所以，静谧让我们有机会感受大自然的慰藉，”我附和道。
“Stillness can be radiant. We pause and see how vibrant life is around us. How nature speaks to us.”
“静谧亦可闪耀光芒。我们停下脚步，便能感受到周围生命的蓬勃生机，感受到大自然的低语。”
I completely agreed with Jen. “Yes, though we know this is true, we shortchange ourselves most of the time by doing too much and missing out on savoring the gifts of the moment.”
我完全同意Jen的观点。“是的，虽然我们知道这是真的，但我们大多数时候都因为做得太多而错失了享受当下美好时光的机会。”
“Absolutely,” Jen continued. “This is why I’ve started a more radical practice to make myself stop and be quiet for at least one minute every hour, for most hours of the day. It’s really quite simple and deliberate with the aid of technology—my watch! My watch has a timer that I can set to go off every hour, and it has this sweet little chime that lets me know it’s time to stop whatever I am doing and pause. So, when my watch chimes, it’s time for my moment of silence. I allow a whole sixty seconds to be quiet and come back to the present. And this is not just for me anymore. It is downright comforting when that chime time comes! Talk about ‘saved by the bell!’ I get caught in the middle of doing things, and after a moment of silence, I realize how unpresent I have been in the moment.”
“当然，”珍继续说道，“所以我开始尝试一种更彻底的方法，让自己每小时至少停下来安静一分钟，一天中的大部分时间都是如此。借助科技——我的手表——这其实很简单，也很有意识！我的手表有个定时器，我可以设置每小时响一次，它会发出悦耳的提示音，提醒我该停下手中的事情，暂停一下。所以，当手表响起时，就到了我静默的时间。我会给自己整整六十秒的时间安静下来，回到当下。这不再只是我自己的习惯了。每次听到提示音，我都会感到无比安心！真是‘及时雨’！我经常忙得不可开交，但静默片刻后，我才意识到自己刚才有多么心不在焉。”
I listened closely as Jen spoke. She added, “Even though we yearn to be in the wilderness, to enjoy the beauty of a forest or a mountain, we quickly notice how our minds are distracted with nagging thoughts we have carried with us from home, keeping us from being comforted by the serenity of our surroundings. These inner distractions keep us from simply being present to ourselves and who or what is in front of us.”
我认真地听着珍说话。她补充道：“即使我们渴望置身荒野，欣赏森林或山脉的美景，我们很快就会发现，那些从家里带来的烦心事总是让我们心神不宁，使我们无法享受周围环境的宁静。这些内心的干扰让我们无法真正地活在当下，无法关注自己，也无法关注眼前的人或事。”
It struck me how important it is for us to be in a receptive mode in nature, to free our minds from the thicket of our busy thoughts. Walking, yoga, or canoeing certainly gave us the methods to wind our minds down, doing a concrete, physical activity, allowing us to ground our bodies, dropping into our bodies and hearts, away from those hyper-speeding zones of the mind. Even twenty minutes of a good walk on a path in the woods could shift our thinking into calmer awareness. The whole world could look different to us after a walk under the pines, and we might notice the brilliant goldfinches hopping on the branches right ahead of us. And if we had a loved one with us, stopping in the morning light to enjoy the gold glory of the finches, we shared a true moment of comfort.
我突然意识到，在大自然中保持开放的心态是多么重要，这能让我们的思绪从纷繁的思绪中解脱出来。散步、瑜伽或划独木舟无疑为我们提供了放松身心的方法，这些具体的、身体性的活动让我们能够扎根于大地，回归身体和内心，远离那些高速运转的思绪。即使只是在林间小径上漫步二十分钟，也能让我们的思绪变得更加平静。在松树林下散步之后，整个世界在我们眼中都会焕然一新，我们或许会注意到眼前枝头上跳跃的金翅雀。如果身边有爱人陪伴，在晨光中驻足欣赏金翅雀的金色光芒，我们便能共享一段真正温馨的时刻。
“So, Jen, your role in this process is to facilitate people learning to be quiet enough and grounded enough to receive the comfort of nature. You teach us how to open up and be present to what the earth has to teach us.”
“所以，珍，你在这个过程中的角色是帮助人们学会足够安静、足够沉稳，从而获得大自然的慰藉。你教我们如何敞开心扉，用心感受地球想要教给我们的一切。”
“Yes. And it works both ways—as we open ourselves to our natural surroundings, we learn the other-than-human languages of life around us—the language of animals, of seasons, of the wind, of the skies and waters, of mountains . . . of stillness. With more stillness, we begin to tap in to the wise voice within. And sacred silence.”
“是的。而且这种作用是双向的——当我们敞开心扉拥抱自然环境时，我们就能学习到周围生命中非人类的语言——动物的语言、季节的语言、风的语言、天空和水的语言、山脉的语言……以及静谧的语言。随着静谧的增多，我们开始聆听内心的智慧之声。以及神圣的寂静。”
I chimed in. “I see what you mean—we need to be willing to be still, to be present to these languages of creation around us, and step out of our own terms, beyond words.”
我插话道：“我明白你的意思——我们需要愿意静下心来，去感受我们周围这些造物语言的存在，并跳出我们自己的思维模式，超越语言的界限。”
Jen nodded and added, “Here’s an example of what we might call ‘tree language’: I love to watch how one of my favorite trees stays so rooted and strong while bending against the storms. The roots teach me how to stay grounded and rooted when a perceived storm arrives in myself or another. I remember my roots, all the things that keep me grounded—my home, my local community, my loved ones, my work. I can reflect on the tree’s roots before I offer comfort to someone in distress.”
珍点点头，补充道：“这里有个例子，我们可以称之为‘树语’：我喜欢观察我最喜欢的一棵树，它在暴风雨中依然根深蒂固、屹立不倒。它的根教会我，当自己或他人遭遇风暴时，如何保持内心的平静和稳定。我会想起我的根，想起所有让我感到踏实的事物——我的家、我的社区、我的亲人、我的工作。在安慰身处困境的人之前，我可以先想想树根的意义。”
With Jen, I didn’t need to rush to any clever comments to cheer up our pensive moment. I sat still in our silence, remembering my favorite trees in my life. Yes, sitting under a majestic two-hundred-year-old oak tree was more than just sitting. We could tap the strength of those roots with our quietude and stillness, taking a deep breath and beholding their steadfast power. And then we could carry this tree’s presence with us when we set out to comfort a person in pain.
和珍在一起，我无需急于说些俏皮话来打破我们沉思的氛围。我静静地坐着，回忆着我生命中最爱的几棵树。是的，坐在一棵雄伟的两百年橡树下，不仅仅是坐着那么简单。我们可以用我们的静默和沉稳去感受它根系的力量，深吸一口气，感受它坚韧不拔的力量。然后，当我们去安慰一个痛苦的人时，我们就可以带着这棵树的这份力量。

Jen’s Comforting Practices with Groups
Jen的团体安慰练习
Since 1999, Jen has consistently and successfully been providing retreats and gatherings, and facilitating workshops to help people slow down, soften, and quiet themselves. Highly skilled in helping her retreaters transition gently from their busier lives into a retreat’s simpler, more mindful ways, she lists suggestions here that can be widely applied in other group settings, including at home:
自 1999 年以来，Jen 一直成功地组织静修活动、聚会和工作坊，帮助人们放慢脚步、放松身心、获得内心的平静。她非常擅长帮助参与者从忙碌的生活中温和地过渡到静修中更简单、更专注的生活方式。她在此列出的一些建议可以广泛应用于其他团体活动，包括在家中进行：

A Welcoming Atmosphere: Music, Food, Drinks, and Flowers
温馨的氛围：音乐、美食、饮品和鲜花
Warm and relaxing music, easy-access food or potluck offerings, and even the simplest flower arrangements quickly contribute to a comforting environment. Basically, these are the welcoming signs that set the stage for gathering together, conveying the message, “Come join us. You are welcome here.” Jen describes her beautiful ritual for preparing for her guests:
“To prepare for an upcoming retreat, and to connect with my heart energy, I enjoy a simple ritual of placing flowers in vases for the tables and bedrooms of our center. I can’t help but smile and feel myself softening as the flowers beam back their beauty to me in the morning light. Next I put on some gentle music and light a circle of candles. I walk around the candles, in unison with footsteps and music. When my guests start arriving, I am ready to share my presence, coming from the sweetness of the flowers, music, and candles, and sincerely greet each retreat guest.”
温暖舒缓的音乐、方便取用的食物或自带的菜肴，甚至最简单的插花都能迅速营造出舒适的氛围。这些就像是欢迎的标志，为聚会拉开序幕，传递着“欢迎加入我们”的信息。珍妮描述了她为迎接客人而准备的美好仪式：“为了迎接即将到来的静修，并与我的内心能量连接，我喜欢一个简单的仪式：在中心的桌子和卧室里插上鲜花。当清晨的阳光照耀下，鲜花绽放出美丽的光芒时，我不禁微笑，感觉自己也变得温柔起来。接下来，我会播放一些轻柔的音乐，点燃一圈蜡烛。我会绕着蜡烛走动，脚步与音乐的节奏保持一致。当客人们陆续到来时，我已准备好与他们分享我的存在，我的存在源于鲜花、音乐和蜡烛的甜蜜，我会真诚地迎接每一位参加静修的客人。”
The Role as Facilitator or Host
担任协调员或主持人的角色
At the beginning of her retreats, Jen warmly greets her guests and welcomes them to the retreat space. She briefly shares with her group her background and what drew her to her work, and how she will facilitate the retreat’s activities.
在静修营开始时，珍会热情地迎接每位来宾，并欢迎他们来到静修场所。她会简要地向大家介绍自己的背景、是什么吸引她从事这项工作，以及她将如何组织静修营的各项活动。
She states it is very comforting for guests to understand the parameters of her role and how she is available. Essentially, this serves as an orientation to help participants “get their bearings” and feel at home.
她表示，让客人了解她的职责范围以及她如何提供帮助，会让他们感到非常安心。实际上，这相当于一个入场指导，帮助参与者“熟悉环境”，感到宾至如归。
In broader applications, the role of any host or facilitator is to graciously greet guests and assist in orienting them. This provides a sense of belonging, which is reassuring and inviting. Let guests know what is available, what is planned, who is available (the “go-to” people), and where things are. The role of a host (or hosts) is a vital comforting role, as people attending need to know what is going on and how they can get assistance if they need it.
在更广泛的应用场景中，任何接待人员或协调员的职责都是热情地迎接宾客并协助他们熟悉环境。这能营造一种归属感，令人感到安心和舒适。要让宾客了解有哪些设施可用、有哪些活动安排、哪些人可以提供帮助（“万事通”）以及物品的位置。接待人员的角色至关重要，因为与会者需要了解活动流程以及在需要帮助时如何获得支持。
Greeters and hosts (the warm and sometimes fuzzy “go-to” people) are essential for comforting experiences for groups, especially when there are newcomers. Team meetings at work start off better with a sincere welcome by an appointed host, expressing appreciation for people showing up. Even family and friends gatherings need at least one greeter as people wander through the doorway.
迎宾员和接待员（那些热情友善、有时甚至让人感到亲切的“万事通”）对于营造舒适的团体氛围至关重要，尤其是在有新成员加入的情况下。工作团队会议如果能由指定的接待员真诚地欢迎大家，表达对到场人员的感谢，将会更加顺利。即使是家庭和朋友聚会，也至少需要一位迎宾员在人们步入会场时迎接他们。

What We Are Grateful for Today
我们今天感恩的事
Jen believes talking about what we are grateful for is a great icebreaker for a gathering, especially before a meal, or at the start of an event. Retreat guests readily share their observations of what they are grateful for in the past day or week, and this naturally invites comfortable conversation.
Jen认为，谈论值得感恩的事情是打破聚会僵局的好方法，尤其是在餐前或活动开始时。参加静修的客人很乐意分享他们在过去一天或一周中感恩的事情，这自然而然地就能引发轻松愉快的对话。
Likewise, any participant at any kind of gathering, a meeting, a party, a book club, can share this warm-up topic.
同样，任何参与者，无论是在任何类型的聚会、会议、派对还是读书俱乐部，都可以分享这个热身话题。

Sharing Our Intentions
分享我们的意图
Retreat guests state what brought them to the event, and what they hope to gain from the experience. They are free to disclose as little or as much as they like about why they wanted to participate in the event.
参加静修活动的宾客会说明他们参加此次活动的原因，以及他们希望从这次体验中获得什么。他们可以根据自己的意愿，选择透露多少关于参与活动的原因。
For wider applications, at early stages of meetings and gatherings, it’s comforting for people to state what brought them together and what they hope to gain from the experience, though this information is offered voluntarily.
对于更广泛的应用而言，在会议和聚会的早期阶段，人们如果能说明是什么让他们聚集在一起，以及他们希望从这次经历中获得什么，会感到很欣慰，尽管这些信息是自愿提供的。

Reading Poems or Blessings, or Saying Prayers
诵读诗歌或祝福语，或祈祷
A short poem, a thoughtful blessing, or a centering prayer all focus people on the goal or the inspiration for an event. It helps get everyone “on the same page,” with beautiful, heartening words.
一首短诗、一句充满温情的祝福或一段令人心静的祈祷，都能帮助人们聚焦于活动的目标或初衷。这些优美动人的话语，能让所有人“步调一致”。

Outdoor Exercise
户外运动
Outdoors, Jen leads exercises to help guests find comfort in nature. She says to people, “Walk as if you are kissing the earth with your feet, stepping softly and lightly upon your mother’s back.” She encourages people to walk while allowing themselves to feel fully with their feet what they are walking through. She leads a walking meditation along a mountain brook path. She also leads yoga exercises outside, so guests can open up their bodies and spirits to the wide sky above them and the soft mossy earth below them.
在户外，珍带领大家进行一些练习，帮助客人在大自然中找到慰藉。她对大家说：“走路的时候，要像用脚亲吻大地一样，轻柔地踏在母亲的背上。”她鼓励大家边走边用脚感受脚下的一切。她带领大家沿着山涧小径进行行走冥想。她还会带领大家进行户外瑜伽练习，让客人敞开身心，拥抱头顶的广阔天空和脚下柔软的苔藓大地。
Her guests over the years have especially loved an exercise of finding a special spot in the woods, where they can sit by themselves and reflect on a particular question about their lives. Before locating this special spot, Jen facilitates their ability to follow their instincts in the wilderness:
“Let the space call you to it—you can sense the right spot for you and follow it. It might be a certain tree, or a shady glen or a clearing by a meadow. Sit with what has drawn you in to it—what was it about this spot that called you? How does this space feel to you? Quiet? Vibrant? Soft? Fierce? How does this space affect the way you are looking at your life situation now?”
多年来，她的客人们尤其喜欢在树林里寻找一处特别的地方，独自静坐，思考人生中的某个问题。在找到这处特别的地方之前，珍会引导他们跟随自己的直觉：“让这片空间召唤你——你可以感受到哪里才是最适合你的地方，然后跟随它。它可能是一棵特定的树，或是一个阴凉的山谷，或一片草地旁的空地。静静地感受是什么吸引了你——这个地方的什么特质召唤了你？你感觉如何？宁静？充满活力？柔和？还是强烈？这个地方如何影响你看待自己当下生活的方式？”
She asks her guests to describe their interaction with their special spot and their question. Many comment they didn’t feel so alone anymore with their burden or with their problem. Retreat-goers often noticed that the spaces beckoning them symbolically reflected a certain aspect of their lives that needed examining.
她请来宾描述他们与专属空间的互动以及他们提出的问题。许多人表示，他们不再感到孤单，不再独自面对重担或困境。参加静修的人常常注意到，那些吸引他们的空间象征性地反映了他们生活中需要审视的某个方面。
For example, someone drawn to a stream in a shady glen might have wanted to reflect on aspects of flow and opportunities in their lives, when they were feeling fearful of “going with the flow.”
例如，当一个人感到害怕“随波逐流”时，他可能会被阴凉山谷中的溪流所吸引，想要反思生活中的流动和机遇。
As individuals on our own, we can apply this exercise with walks in the natural world. We can allow ourselves to be “called” to a certain spot with which we feel a special affinity. Often the terrain and setting we choose for our resting spot might just speak to us, give us messages in sounds, smells, images, symbols, sensations. If we just sit and open ourselves to the present moment, something might beckon us to study it and learn from it.
作为个体，我们可以将这种练习运用到自然漫步中。我们可以让自己“被召唤”到某个让我们感到特别亲近的地方。通常，我们选择的休憩之地，其地形和环境本身就会与我们对话，通过声音、气味、图像、符号和感觉向我们传递信息。如果我们只是静静地坐着，敞开心扉拥抱当下，或许会有某种东西召唤我们去观察它，并从中学习。

Jen’s Invitations to Exploring Comforting Activities Together
珍邀请大家一起探索令人感到舒适的活动
Jen suggests, “Experiment with spending more time in nature and sensing how this feels. Try being unplugged from media and technology for a spell and notice the contrast.” I reflect on what Jen said as I watch children playing outside my window, on a large lawn next door, bordered by apple and pine trees and a little fountain. Four of them, under ten years of age, are having a blast, chasing each other and shrieking exuberantly. What a joy to behold! I smile, knowing these kids have found the great treasures of running wildly in the long golden light of evening. The chickadees are singing their mating songs while the children race along the stone fences, laughing. Spring is here. It just doesn’t get any better than this.
珍建议道：“不妨多花些时间亲近自然，感受一下这种感觉。试着暂时放下电子设备，远离媒体和科技，体会一下其中的差别。” 我一边想着珍的话，一边看着窗外隔壁草坪上的孩子们玩耍。草坪四周环绕着苹果树、松树和一个小喷泉。四个不到十岁的孩子玩得不亦乐乎，互相追逐嬉戏，欢声笑语不断。多么令人欣慰的景象！我微笑着，因为我知道这些孩子找到了在傍晚金色的余晖中尽情奔跑的乐趣。山雀在鸣唱求偶的歌声，孩子们则沿着石墙奔跑嬉戏，欢声笑语不断。春天来了。没有什么比这更美好的了。
Jen also suggests a few other activities:
“Make sacred pauses throughout the day. At least a few times during the day, take a minute or two just to stop, breathe, and come fully back into the present moment.
“Do exercises or yoga outside, even just walking. When we move our bodies outdoors, we may breathe better and sleep better at night.
“Play games outdoors, or on the porch, even card games are fun when sitting on a blanket on the grass. When we are outdoors, our sense of spaciousness and perspective is expanded. Stepping away from our ceilings and walls can open up our minds, and then our hearts.
“Have picnics and eat outdoors, or even on the porch. Find little spots where you can sit alone, in a garden, or the woods, or a park. Having alone time with nature quickly reminds us we are never really alone. There is life around us, and creation speaks to us.
“Go barefoot on the ground whenever you can. It can bring out the best of us as humans, just digging our feet in the warm sand or stepping into a cool spring. Happy feet can tell us it’s good to be alive!”
珍还建议了一些其他活动：“在一天中抽出一些神圣的停顿时间。每天至少抽出几次，花一两分钟停下来，深呼吸，完全回到当下。“在户外做运动或瑜伽，哪怕只是散步。当我们在户外活动身体时，呼吸可能会更顺畅，晚上睡得也更好。“在户外或门廊上玩游戏，即使是纸牌游戏，坐在草地上的毯子上也很有趣。当我们身处户外时，我们对空间和视野的感知会得到扩展。远离天花板和墙壁可以打开我们的思维，进而打开我们的心扉。“野餐，在户外或门廊上用餐。找一些可以独自坐下的小地方，比如花园、树林或公园。与大自然独处会让我们很快意识到，我们其实并不孤单。我们周围充满生机，造物主在与我们对话。” “尽可能光脚走在地上。这能激发我们人性中最美好的一面，哪怕只是把脚埋进温暖的沙子里，或是踏进清凉的泉水里。快乐的双脚会告诉我们，活着真好！”
# ↩

CHAPTER 9
第九章
Self-Comforting for Comforters
被子自慰
# ↩

Renewing Our Compassion

重拾我们的同情心

E VEN THE MOST EMPATHIC, GENEROUS, and kindhearted people among us experience compassion fatigue at times. In our yearning to be effective comforters, we often forget that we are only human beings, with human limitations. As much as we would love to keep going strong like the Energizer Bunny, we can simply run out of comfort to give.
即使我们当中最有同理心、最慷慨、最善良的人，有时也会感到同情疲劳。我们渴望成为有效的安慰者，却常常忘记自己只是普通人，有着人类的局限性。尽管我们很想像劲量兔子一样精力充沛，但我们终究会耗尽所有能给予的安慰。
Those of us in human services, health care, pastoral care, education, and other caregiver fields face compassion fatigue on a regular basis, and though we may vent privately that we are “sick of suffering fools,” or “fed up with ungrateful jerks,” many of us never let go of our drive to constantly “be there” for people who need us. In my work as a counselor in behavioral health and hospice settings, I certainly battled bouts of despair and pessimism about the state of the world, let alone how useless I felt to protect others from its harsh realities. And as much as I believed wholeheartedly in remaining compassionate toward others each and every day—maintaining my regimens for stress management, work/life balance, and good boundaries—my supply of comfort often come up short.
我们这些从事社会服务、医疗保健、牧灵关怀、教育和其他照护领域的人，经常会面临同情疲劳。虽然我们私下里可能会抱怨“受够了那些愚蠢的人”，或者“受够了那些忘恩负义的混蛋”，但我们中的许多人从未放弃过想要时刻陪伴在需要我们的人身边的动力。在我作为行为健康和临终关怀机构的咨询师工作中，我确实经历过对世界现状的绝望和悲观，更不用说那种觉得自己无力保护他人免受残酷现实伤害的无力感了。尽管我真心相信每天都应该对他人保持同情心——坚持我的压力管理、工作与生活平衡以及设定良好界限的习惯——但我的慰藉往往仍然不足。
In this chapter I will share some of the wisdom I’ve gained from my own experiences as well as from other comforters on how to take care of yourself even when you’re taking care of others.
在本章中，我将分享我从自身经历以及其他安慰者那里获得的一些智慧，这些智慧是关于如何在照顾他人的同时照顾好自己。
# ↩

FINDING STRENGTH IN COMMUNITY

在社区中寻找力量

Over the years I’ve been blessed with colleagues and friends who have heartened me when I’ve doubted my own capacity to be a comforter. These gifted individuals were able to sit down and give me the support I needed at crucial moments, working wonders with my compassion fatigue. But these comforting people didn’t just show up at my doorstep, my kitchen table, or my desk at work. I had to work to find them.
这些年来，我非常幸运地拥有一些同事和朋友，每当我怀疑自己是否有能力安慰他人时，他们都会给予我鼓励。这些才华横溢的人总能在关键时刻坐下来，给予我所需的支持，极大地缓解了我的同情疲劳。但这些给予我安慰的人并非凭空出现在我家门口、餐桌旁或办公桌前。我需要努力才能找到他们。
Sometimes our friends and family members are just too overwhelmed to lift us out of our own compassion fatigue. Though we may have relied on them for comfort in the past, in stressful and demanding times, we might need to reach out to our greater communities. It takes some courage and energy, but proactively venturing out to seek comforting bonds with new people actually helps build our communities as well as our confidence. Rest assured that there are other like-minded and like-hearted souls out there looking for meaningful connections, especially when their own family members or friends are in crisis or not available.
有时候，我们的亲朋好友可能已经不堪重负，无力帮助我们摆脱同情疲劳。虽然我们过去可能依赖他们获得安慰，但在压力巨大、疲惫不堪的时刻，我们或许更需要向更广泛的社群寻求帮助。这需要一些勇气和精力，但主动走出去，与新朋友建立慰藉和联系，实际上有助于我们构建社群，也能增强我们的自信心。请放心，还有很多志同道合、心地善良的人也在寻找有意义的联结，尤其是在他们的家人或朋友身处困境或无法提供帮助的时候。
Here are some ways we can find fellowship with other comforters in nurturing environments:
以下是一些我们可以在充满关爱的环境中与其他安慰者建立联系的方法：

Volunteering for compassionate or humanitarian programs
参与慈善或人道主义项目
Food banks, animal shelters, hospitals, nursing homes, cancer support campaigns, hospices, homeless shelters, elder care and child care services are just a few places we might meet nurturing, like-minded comforters.
食品银行、动物收容所、医院、疗养院、癌症支持活动、临终关怀中心、无家可归者收容所、老年护理和儿童保育服务机构只是我们可能遇到富有爱心、志同道合的安慰者的几个地方。

Support Groups
互助小组
Support groups are wonderful venues to meet people in similar situations, who have learned about comforting by going through their own hardship and loss. Caregiver support groups are full of comforters. Group facilitators can also be knowledgeable sources for referrals to programs that provide support and comfort. Further, another benefit for comforters is that caregiver support groups often focus on reinforcing our own self-care and self-comforting practices. It helps to have other comforters root for us to take good care of ourselves.
互助小组是结识处境相似的人的绝佳场所，这些人通过自身的苦难和失去，学会了如何安慰他人。照顾者互助小组里充满了乐于安慰他人的人。小组的组织者还可以提供相关信息，帮助你找到能够提供支持和安慰的项目。此外，对安慰者来说，另一个好处是，照顾者互助小组通常会着重强化我们自身的自我关爱和自我安慰的习惯。有其他安慰者鼓励我们好好照顾自己，这真的很有帮助。

Our Religious and Spiritual Communities
我们的宗教和精神团体
Finding fellowship through our spiritual interests gets us connected with comforting people on similar paths.
通过精神层面的兴趣爱好找到志同道合的人，可以让我们与走在相似道路上、互相安慰的人建立联系。

Classes, Study Groups, Clubs, or Events Related to Topics that Comfort Us
与让我们感到舒适的话题相关的课程、学习小组、俱乐部或活动
Topics may include spiritual healing, gardening, labyrinths, quilting, networking, massage, pottery, kayaking, bird-watching, and many other enriching activities. (When I moved to Maine nine years ago, I attended a local newcomers club and met a wonderful person who is still one of my best friends.)
主题可能包括灵性疗愈、园艺、迷宫漫步、拼布、人脉拓展、按摩、陶艺、皮划艇、观鸟以及许多其他有益身心的活动。（九年前我搬到缅因州时，参加了一个当地的新移民俱乐部，在那里我结识了一位很棒的人，她至今仍是我最好的朋友之一。）

Professional Associations and Conferences
专业协会和会议
A good way to meet comforting colleagues outside of their busy work settings is to attend regular association or networking meetings (often breakfast or luncheon events). The smiling, friendly person at your table who appears comforting might share with you the ways he or she prevents burnout and compassion fatigue.
在繁忙的工作环境之外，结识能给人带来安慰的同事的一个好方法是参加协会或人脉拓展活动的定期会议（通常是早餐或午餐会）。你桌上那位面带微笑、友善且看起来很和蔼的人，或许会与你分享他/她预防职业倦怠和同情疲劳的方法。
# ↩

Self-Comforting Wisdom from Our Guides

来自我们导师的自我安慰智慧

Many of the comforting professionals profiled in this book were eager to share the means by which they keep themselves grounded and nurtured. Each of them stressed to me that comfort is as much a vital life support as oxygen, water, or sunlight—it is something that we all , comforters and those who are comforted, need to survive. Also, many of them expressed to me a truth I have long observed: The greatest comforters learn by being comfort ed by others.
本书中介绍的许多抚慰者都渴望分享他们保持内心平静和获得滋养的方法。他们都向我强调，安慰如同氧气、水或阳光一样，是维持生命的重要保障——无论是安慰者还是被安慰者，都需要它才能生存。此外，他们中的许多人还向我表达了一个我长期以来观察到的真理：最优秀的安慰者也是从他人的安慰中学习而来的。
Most of them were regular participants in support groups, twelve-step groups, fitness clubs, or personal development groups. They told me it helped tremendously to have fellow group members rooting for them to take care of themselves. These caregivers and comforters enjoyed being cheered on as they reached their self-care goals.
他们中的大多数人经常参加互助小组、十二步互助小组、健身俱乐部或个人发展小组。他们告诉我，有其他组员鼓励他们照顾好自己，这对他们帮助极大。这些照顾者和安慰者在实现自我关爱目标的过程中，也乐于得到大家的鼓励和支持。
What grabbed my attention were the striking similarities of the other self-comforting activities practiced by all of our comfort guides. Here are their most popular self-comforting routines.
最吸引我的是，我们所有安抚指导员所使用的其他自我安抚活动都惊人地相似。以下是他们最常用的几种自我安抚方法。

Quiet Morning Routines
安静的晨间习惯
Morning routines involving quietude, reflection, and meditation are vital to all comforters profiled. They take their morning time seriously, as a way to prepare for their comforting work for the day.
对于所有受访者来说，晨间静思、反思和冥想都至关重要。他们非常重视晨间时光，以此为一天的慰藉工作做好准备。
Before she goes to work at the Mayo Clinic, Adrienne Dormody enjoys her mornings with her daily comforts.
在去梅奥诊所上班之前，艾德丽安·多莫迪喜欢享受她每天早晨的舒适时光。
“I start my day with a cup of hot tea, sitting in my dad’s old rocking chair. I begin by reading spiritually uplifting material, including Daily Word and Al-Anon literature and then I pray for those I care deeply about, and for others who are not close to me. Sitting in this chair, I feel held by my father. He died a year after surviving Hurricane Katrina, after barely making it out alive of the 7th Ward (Gentilly area) of New Orleans. In our last months together, when he moved to live with me in Rochester, he enjoyed rocking in this chair that he bought for ten dollars at a local flea market. He was very proud to have purchased it, as he had lost everything in Katrina. Every morning when I rock in his chair, I remember him and feel his spirit.”
我每天早上都以一杯热茶开始，坐在父亲的旧摇椅上。我会先读一些能提升精神境界的书籍，比如《每日箴言》和匿名戒酒互助会的资料，然后为我深爱的人祈祷，也为那些与我并不亲近的人祈祷。坐在这把椅子上，我感觉父亲就在我身边。他从卡特里娜飓风中死里逃生，在新奥尔良第七区（根蒂利地区）侥幸生还一年后去世。在我们相处的最后几个月里，他搬来和我一起住在罗切斯特，他很喜欢坐在这把他在当地跳蚤市场花十美元买的摇椅上。他为买到这把椅子感到非常自豪，因为他在卡特里娜飓风中失去了一切。每天早上，当我摇着他的椅子时，我都会想起他，感受到他的精神。
Patricia Ellen, before arriving at the Center for Grieving Children to direct outreach programs, practices a daily meditation in the morning:
“I start out the day with a meditation practice where I rub my hands together and see myself as a beloved child. I reflect on my need to pace myself and comfort myself. I need to remember to take time to comfort myself, and allow others to comfort me. I admit I have a habit of being more comforting to others than I am to myself. I just cannot take care of everybody. But I am blessed to know wonderful comforting people I can go to as loved ones and colleagues.”
帕特里夏·艾伦在到悲伤儿童中心负责外展项目之前，每天早上都会进行冥想：“我每天早上都会进行冥想练习，搓搓手，想象自己是一个被爱的孩子。我会反思自己需要放慢节奏，安抚自己。我需要记住要给自己留出时间，也要允许别人安慰我。我承认我习惯于更多地安慰别人而不是安慰自己。我不可能照顾到所有人。但我很幸运，认识一些很棒的、能安慰我的人，他们是我的亲人和同事。”
Hal Wallof and other comfort guides find comfort in sipping their coffee in the morning and talking intimately with their loved ones. Hal tells us:
“I love to wake up very early and enjoy a cup of coffee while sitting quietly with my wife, slowly transitioning into the day. Once we’ve had at least one cup of coffee, we talk about each other’s dreams—the ones we’ve had the night before or others. We like to know the details about the good dreams as well as the bad ones, because dreams reveal so much to us about our inner lives. It may seem simple, just drinking coffee and talking about our dreams, but these are some of the most comforting moments we share together.”
哈尔·沃洛夫和其他一些“舒适指南”的倡导者们发现，清晨啜饮咖啡、与爱人促膝长谈是慰藉心灵的方式。哈尔告诉我们：“我喜欢早起，和妻子静静地坐在一起，一边享用咖啡，一边慢慢地开启新的一天。至少喝完一杯咖啡后，我们会聊聊彼此的梦境——无论是前一晚的梦，还是其他的梦。我们喜欢了解梦境的细节，无论是美梦还是噩梦，因为梦境能揭示我们内心深处的许多秘密。喝咖啡、聊梦，看似简单，却是我们共同拥有的最温馨的时刻。”
# ↩

TAKING LITTLE PAUSES FOR CENTERING, MINDFULNESS, AND PRAYER

抽出一些时间进行静心、正念练习和祈祷

Jeff Lewis, a nurse-practitioner at a hectic veterans hospital, believes in the power of taking little pauses throughout his workday, often for only three minutes each. He uses his precious minutes to center himself with prayer.
杰夫·刘易斯是一家繁忙的退伍军人医院的执业护士，他深信在一天的工作中抽出短暂的停顿时间（通常只有三分钟）的力量。他利用这宝贵的几分钟时间，通过祈祷来平静身心。
“When I am in need of comfort, I must first be alone for a while to pray and reflect. I ask myself, ‘Is there a lessen I need to learn from this?’ Or ‘How can I comfort myself today?’ Then I take pause and think of my loved ones, alive and deceased.”
“当我需要安慰时，我必须先独自待一会儿，祈祷和反思。我会问自己：‘我能从中吸取什么教训？’或者‘今天我该如何安慰自己？’然后我会停下来，想起我所爱的人，无论他们是健在的还是已经去世的。”
Alicia Rasin, in her demanding work with the police and with victims of crime, prays frequently throughout the day.
艾丽西亚·拉辛在与警方和犯罪受害者打交道的繁重工作中，经常在一天中祈祷。
“I spend more time in prayer, and the more I pray, the more I believe God needs me to serve other people in pain. Prayer is a way for me to keep reminding myself what my true purpose is. It’s clear to me that I make my prayers real by serving others. Comforting others is my way of being true to God’s calling for me. I find comfort in believing God is using me this way, that I have a purpose.”
“我花更多时间祷告，祷告越多，我就越相信上帝需要我去服侍那些身处痛苦中的人。祷告让我不断提醒自己，我的真正使命是什么。我清楚地知道，服侍他人就是我实现祷告的方式。安慰他人是我回应上帝呼召的方式。我相信上帝正在以这种方式使用我，我相信我拥有使命，这让我感到安慰。”
Adrienne shares how she stays centered at her job at the Mayo Clinic:
“To strengthen myself as a comforter, I’ve needed to put into practice my centering skills to calm myself. I often need to stop myself when I am getting frustrated, to take a deep breath, step back, and see through the eyes of the patient and their caregivers. I also use centering prayers and the twelve-step Al-Anon teachings to slow myself down and regroup. I definitely have to keep aware of my ‘hot buttons,’ to honor my limitations and know when to back off and rest. Once again, if I don’t take care of myself in this way, the lines of communication are more likely to get crossed and blocked.”
艾德琳分享了她在梅奥诊所工作中保持专注的秘诀：“为了更好地安抚他人，我需要练习一些让自己平静下来的技巧。我经常会在感到沮丧时停下来，深呼吸，退后一步，从患者及其照护者的角度看待问题。我还会运用冥想祈祷和十二步戒酒互助会（Al-Anon）的教义来让自己慢下来，重新调整状态。我必须时刻留意自己的‘敏感点’，尊重自己的极限，知道何时应该退一步休息。再次强调，如果我不这样照顾好自己，沟通就更容易出现问题，甚至堵塞。”
# ↩

READING INSPIRATIONAL AND ENTERTAINING LITERATURE

阅读励志和娱乐性文学作品

All of our comfort guides have favorite books to inspire them, including uplifting memoirs, biographies, poems, short stories, and daily meditations. They frequently read books a second or third time, and study the words closely.
我们所有的心理辅导员都有自己喜爱的书籍来激励自己，包括励志回忆录、传记、诗歌、短篇小说和每日冥想。他们经常会反复阅读同一本书，仔细研读其中的文字。
Hal adores Thomas Moore’s Care of the Soul and other books that beckon him to listen to his soul, as well as gritty, inspirational memoirs. Patricia enjoys the life-affirming poems of Mary Oliver and collects beautiful children’s book that are comforting for families. Pam Blunt, an arts therapist, has read Saint-Exupéry’s The Little Prince many, many times, and finds joy in reciting Shakespeare’s sonnets.
哈尔酷爱托马斯·摩尔的《灵魂的照护》以及其他能引导他倾听内心声音的书籍，他还喜欢那些充满力量、鼓舞人心的回忆录。帕特里夏喜欢玛丽·奥利弗充满生命力的诗歌，并收藏了许多温馨感人的儿童读物。艺术治疗师帕姆·布朗特已经反复阅读过圣埃克苏佩里的《小王子》，她也乐于背诵莎士比亚的十四行诗。
Adrienne Dormody finds comfort in studying the biblical story of Job.
艾德琳·多莫迪从研读圣经中约伯的故事中找到了慰藉。
“One comforting thing I’ve discovered recently has surprised me. For the first time, I have been studying the biblical story of Job, and have found this ancient tale speaks to me about patience and faith. I had fallen into our societal habit for instant gratification, and had lost the art of waiting, the willingness to wait for things to unfold in their own time. I certainly have been prone to impatience in my lifetime, and mythic reminders to have patience are an important part of my daily rituals of self-comforting.”
最近我发现了一件令我感到安慰的事情，这让我很意外。我第一次开始研读圣经中约伯的故事，发现这个古老的故事让我意识到耐心和信仰的重要性。我曾经深受现代社会追求即时满足的习惯影响，失去了等待的艺术，失去了耐心等待事物顺其自然的能力。我一生中确实常常缺乏耐心，而神话故事中关于耐心的提醒，如今已成为我每日自我安慰的重要组成部分。
Amy Handy, a ceramic artist, loves escapist and light literature for comforting herself. Jennifer Crusie is a favorite author; Amy also happily loses herself listening to audio books of the Outlander series.
陶瓷艺术家艾米·汉迪喜欢阅读轻松愉快的文学作品来放松身心。她最喜欢的作家是詹妮弗·克鲁西；艾米也很喜欢听《异乡人》系列的有声书，完全沉浸其中。
“The ridiculous situations these characters find themselves in helps me deal with the real curve balls thrown at me every day. The strange thing is, the whacky stuff in my favorite books is not as bizarre as what I face every day in my business. But these stories get me laughing and looking at my life’s dramas in a similar perspective, which lifts me out of my funk.”
“这些角色所处的荒诞境地帮助我应对每天遇到的各种棘手问题。奇怪的是，我最喜欢的书里那些离奇古怪的事情，远不及我每天在工作中遇到的那些事那么离奇。但这些故事能让我开怀大笑，并以类似的视角看待我生活中的种种困境，这让我摆脱了低落的情绪。”
# ↩

LAUGHING, PLAYING, AND GOOFING OFF WITH LOVED ONES AND PETS

与爱人和宠物一起欢笑、玩耍、嬉闹

Jeff Lewis tells us how important it is to just kick back and play with our kids and our pets. He loves to pick up and hold his little loved ones.
杰夫·刘易斯告诉我们，放松下来，和孩子、宠物一起玩耍是多么重要。他喜欢抱起他心爱的孩子们。
“We’ve got to make time to play and just be silly. Otherwise, we get in the bad habit of taking ourselves too seriously. I display pictures of my kids and pets playing in my office, to keep me in a lighter mood.”
“我们必须抽出时间玩耍，放松一下。否则，我们就会养成过于严肃的坏习惯。我在办公室里挂着孩子和宠物玩耍的照片，让自己心情轻松一些。”
Comfort guides Don and Brenda Weeks, who work with therapy dogs, are in sync with what Jeff says:
“One of our greatest R&R activities is just watching the goofy stuff dogs do while they are playing. Never a dull moment—great entertainment, and it’s free!”
陪伴狗狗们的唐和布伦达·威克斯夫妇与杰夫的说法不谋而合：“我们最大的休闲活动之一就是观看狗狗们玩耍时那些滑稽的举动。永远不会感到无聊——既有趣又免费！”
Adrienne Dormody shares her favorite, simple moments of fun with her family:
• Hearing from my son, Allen, and seeing him smile
• Hearing from my brother and nephews
• Hearing my stepson Ryan’s laugh
• Laughing at my husband’s and my stepson Nathan’s jokes
艾德琳·多莫迪分享了她与家人最喜欢、最简单的快乐时光：• 听到儿子艾伦的声音，看到他的笑容• 听到哥哥和侄子们的声音• 听到继子瑞恩的笑声• 被丈夫和继子内森的笑话逗乐
# ↩

GOING TO BEAUTIFUL PLACES IN NATURE

去大自然中美丽的地方

All comfort guides are deeply appreciative of their time in nature. They all walk peacefully in their favorite places, with loved ones and sometimes by themselves. Alicia Rasin loves the James River near her home in Richmond, Virginia, where she goes to restore her spirit.
所有自然疗愈师都非常珍惜与大自然相处的时光。他们喜欢在自己喜爱的地方漫步，有时与亲人相伴，有时独自一人。艾丽西亚·拉辛（Alicia Rasin）尤其喜爱弗吉尼亚州里士满家附近的詹姆斯河，她经常去那里放松身心。
“About every other day, I go to the beautiful James River, right here in the busy city of Richmond. I bring my lawn chair, sit down, and watch the waves and the waterfalls along the rocks. Being by water is about as comforting as anything I know.”
“我几乎隔一天就会去美丽的詹姆斯河，它就在繁华的里士满市里。我会带上我的折叠椅，坐下来，欣赏波浪和岩石上的瀑布。对我来说，待在水边是最令人感到舒适的事情之一。”
Pam Blunt adds how she needs her walks:
“All I need to do is take a walk, even just a short, ten-minute stroll, and I feel better very quickly. The sky is always changing, and the ground is always reflecting back new colors, which reminds me how flowing and resourceful creation around us really is. There is so much supporting us, and when we feel fearful or stuck, we can restore ourselves with a moment of watching the sky or trees or the light on the grass.”
帕姆·布朗特补充道，她很需要散步：“我只需要散散步，哪怕只是短短的十分钟漫步，就能很快感觉好多了。天空总是变幻莫测，大地也总是映照出新的色彩，这让我意识到我们周围的造物是多么的丰富多彩、生机勃勃。有太多东西在支持着我们，当我们感到恐惧或迷茫时，只需片刻凝视天空、树木或草地上的光影，就能让我们重获新生。”

GRATITUDE PRACTICES

感恩练习

Simple practices of gratitude, such as keeping a gratitude journal, stopping to say grace before a meal, or posting grateful thoughts online, are commonly enjoyed by our comfort guides.
我们的安慰指导员通常喜欢一些简单的感恩行为，例如写感恩日记、饭前祷告或在网上发布感恩的想法。
Les Schaffer, a professional storyteller and former counselor, is a member of a gratitude circle, and shares his post from January 15, 2009. His list of things he appreciates is comforting to read:
Dear Friends:
For today, I am grateful for-
1. All the great posts over the past two days. 2. For your posts reminding me of the friend long ago who taught me that my anxiety attacks were a) not going to kill me, b) under my control, and c) alleviated by talking to people about them. 3. That my back continues to improve, and I’m going to try going to the YMCA for a light workout and some stretching this afternoon. 4. For the fun connections I’m making on Facebook, when it’s not crashing my computer. 5. That I did manage to connect with one new friend before my computer crashed today. 6. For the great salmon and squash and asparagus dinner I whipped up last night, despite my back giving me fits. 7. And for the fact that there still is some wild salmon out there, and for the power that created asparagus. 8. How, when I was vegetable gardening, that raising my own asparagus helped teach me patience, sort of like how zucchini teaches us to deal with abundance. 9. That, so far, I am not feeling super-anxious about the busy performing and teaching schedule this winter/spring, even though I do not feel in any way prepared. But things are in progress. 10. Speaking of that, I got invited back to perform at this spring’s Arts Festival at the Cultural Arts Center at Glen Allen. 11. For the long johns, flannel shirts, and fleece that enable me to work comfortably in our chilly house-without needing to jack up the thermostat too much. 12. I could not write down enough gratitude for my daughter, whose forty-third birthday is today. It seems like just yesterday she was born, a few ounces short of being a preemie, at the Medical College of Virginia, on a snowy afternoon. When she was born, she could fit in the palm of my hand. Now I fit like putty in her capable hands. 13. That I’ve survived to be a part of my daughter’s life and family.
Later,
专业故事讲述者、前心理咨询师莱斯·沙弗是感恩圈的成员，他分享了自己2009年1月15日的帖子。他列出的感恩清单读来令人感到安慰：亲爱的朋友们：今天，我感恩——1. 过去两天里所有精彩的帖子。2. 感谢你们的帖子让我想起很久以前的一位朋友，她教会我，我的焦虑症发作a) 不会要了我的命，b) 在我的掌控之中，c) 可以通过与人倾诉来缓解。3. 我的背痛持续好转，今天下午我打算去基督教青年会做一些轻松的锻炼和拉伸。4. 感谢我在Facebook上结识的那些有趣的朋友，虽然它总是让我的电脑崩溃。5. 感谢在今天电脑崩溃之前，我成功地结识了一位新朋友。6. 感谢昨晚我尽管背痛难忍，还是做出了美味的三文鱼、南瓜和芦笋晚餐。 7. 感谢大自然依然孕育着野生鲑鱼，也感谢造就芦笋的力量。8. 感谢我曾经种菜，自己种芦笋让我学会了耐心，就像西葫芦教会我们如何面对丰收一样。9. 感谢大自然，尽管我感觉自己完全没有做好准备，但到目前为止，我对这个冬春两季繁忙的演出和教学安排并没有感到特别焦虑。一切都在进行中。10. 说到演出，我受邀再次参加今年春天在格伦艾伦文化艺术中心举办的艺术节。11. 感谢保暖内衣、法兰绒衬衫和抓绒衫，让我可以在我们寒冷的房子里舒适地工作，而无需把恒温器调得太高。12. 我无法用言语表达我对女儿的感激之情，今天是她43岁的生日。仿佛就在昨天，她出生了，体重比早产儿轻了几盎司，出生在弗吉尼亚医学院，那是一个飘雪的午后。她刚出生时，可以放在我的手掌里。现在，我却像橡皮泥一样，被她灵巧的小手托着。13. 我活了下来，成为女儿生命和家庭的一部分。后来，
Les
