KEEPING COMFORTING REMINDERS AND SOUVENIRS AROUND US

在我们身边摆放令人感到慰藉的物品和纪念品

Keeping mementos around us of loved ones, both living and deceased, is a deeply comforting activity. With photos, artwork, cards, quilts, jewelry, and many other special objects, we can keep the loving spirit of our loved ones with us, especially at busy work settings.
保留亲人（包括在世的和已故的）的遗物，能给人带来深深的慰藉。照片、画作、卡片、被子、珠宝以及其他许多特别的物品，都能让我们感受到亲人的爱与关怀，尤其是在繁忙的工作环境中。
Adrienne tells us:
“I often wear my father’s watch to work on my left wrist, and my mother’s ring on my right hand (she survived Katrina, and continues to live north of New Orleans). With these little treasures, I am reminded of them, and comforted by their spirits. Other keepsakes and photos of my family comfort me both at home and at work.”
艾德琳告诉我们：“我经常戴着父亲的手表上班，戴在左手腕上，戴着母亲的戒指（她从卡特里娜飓风中幸存下来，现在仍然住在新奥尔良北部）。这些小小的纪念品让我想起他们，他们的精神也给了我慰藉。其他家人的纪念品和照片，无论在家还是在工作场所，都能给我带来安慰。”
# ↩

SHARING MEALS AND GATHERING WITH FRIENDS AND FAMILY

与亲朋好友共享美食和聚会

All of our comfort guides love to make food, share food, and eat food. Sitting down together for a meal with friends and family is certainly on the top ten list of comforting things for everyone.
我们所有的舒适指南都热爱烹饪、分享美食和享用美食。与亲朋好友围坐在一起用餐，绝对是每个人最能感到舒适的十大事情之一。
Alicia smiles to say:
“I love having my friends over to sit on the porch and sip iced tea with some homemade pies. But honestly, going out to dinner with friends is one of my favorite things to do.”
艾丽西亚笑着说：“我喜欢邀请朋友们来我家，坐在门廊上，一边喝着冰茶，一边吃着自制的馅饼。但说实话，和朋友们出去吃饭是我最喜欢的事情之一。”
Les beams when he talks about his cooking:
“Just putting the dinner I made on the table, and watching people dish it up and pass it around is about as comforting as anything I know.”
莱斯谈到自己的厨艺时笑容满面：“把我做的晚餐端上桌，看着人们把它盛出来，互相传递，这大概是我所知道的最令人感到安慰的事情了。”
# ↩

MUSIC

音乐

Music is a must-have for comforters. All the comfort guides told me they listen to music every day, and feel the difference it makes in their energy level and mood. Many of them are quite deliberate about what they listen to before going to see clients and patients as caregivers. Hal listens to Putumayo World Music and still enjoys Simon and Garfunkel. Adrienne never gets tired of hearing Toots and the Maytals and Willie Nelson. Pam Blunt plays Chopin on her piano to clear her mind when she comes home after working with her clients as a psychotherapist. Patricia has a passion for country-western music.
音乐是陪伴者不可或缺的。所有陪伴者都告诉我，他们每天都听音乐，并能感受到音乐对他们的精力和情绪带来的积极影响。许多人在去见客户和病人之前，都会精心挑选自己喜欢的音乐。哈尔喜欢听普图马约世界音乐，也依然很喜欢西蒙和加芬克尔的歌。艾德丽安百听不厌图茨和五月乐队以及威利·纳尔逊的歌。帕姆·布朗特在结束心理治疗工作回家后，会弹奏肖邦的钢琴曲来放松身心。帕特里夏则对乡村音乐情有独钟。
(I have noticed country-western music is full of songs about grief, loss, and abandonment, which can help us release negativity sometimes. When someone has left me high and dry and I feel dissed, I still love the 1977 hit by Kenny Loggins, You Picked a Fine Time to Leave Me, Lucille. )
（我注意到乡村音乐里有很多关于悲伤、失落和遗弃的歌曲，这有时可以帮助我们释放负面情绪。当有人让我孤立无援，让我感到被冷落时，我仍然很喜欢肯尼·罗根斯1977年的热门歌曲《露西尔，你离开我的时机真好》。）
# ↩

LEARNING ABOUT OTHER PEOPLE IN OTHER REGIONS, CULTURES, AND ERAS

了解其他地区、文化和时代的人们

All of the comfort guides also mentioned how important it was for them to learn about perspectives of people from other regions around the United States and from cultures around the world. Many of them enjoyed news and documentaries that shed light on situations in other countries. They said knowledge of what other people on the planet were going through helped them understand better the plight of people in their own communities. In short, a global perspective put local issues into perspective—economic changes, environmental changes, social changes.
所有参与“舒适指南”的受访者都提到，了解美国其他地区以及世界各地不同文化背景的人们的观点对他们来说非常重要。他们中的许多人喜欢观看新闻和纪录片，了解其他国家的情况。他们表示，了解地球上其他人正在经历的事情，有助于他们更好地理解自己社区居民的困境。简而言之，全球视野能够帮助他们更全面地看待本地问题——经济变化、环境变化和社会变化。
Hal says he likes meeting people from other cultures and “finding our commonalities.” He also loves to travel and explore.
哈尔说他喜欢结识来自其他文化背景的人，“寻找我们的共同点”。他也热爱旅行和探索。
Alicia adds:
“I really don’t see too many movies, and don’t watch that much TV, but I do read the news and watch the news on TV . This might sound strange to some people, but I find it comforting to get the news about what other people around the world are going through. When I hear about the people in China or in Africa, or somewhere else, I feel a sense of unity with the whole world, as a part of humanity. This lifts me out of my own little problems and puts things in a bigger perspective. So that’s why I think being aware of what’s going on around the world is actually very comforting. Sure, you can see a lot of bad stuff going on, but still, there is so much hope out there when you look at the faces of the children in other countries.”
艾丽西亚补充道：“我其实不太看电影，也不怎么看电视，但我会读新闻，也会看电视新闻。这听起来可能有点奇怪，但我发现了解世界各地人们的遭遇会让我感到安慰。当我听到中国、非洲或其他地方的人们的故事时，我感到自己与全世界同在，感受到我们都是人类的一份子。这让我从自己的小烦恼中解脱出来，以更宏观的视角看待事物。所以我觉得，了解世界各地正在发生的事情其实很令人欣慰。当然，你会看到很多糟糕的事情，但当你看到其他国家孩子们的脸庞时，仍然会感受到很多希望。”
Adrienne says she finds comfort in learning new things, as she is a curious person who is genuinely interested in how people live.
艾德琳说，她从学习新事物中获得慰藉，因为她是一个好奇心很强的人，对人们的生活方式非常感兴趣。
“It’s comforting for me to learn something stimulating and exciting—a new discovery or a medical cure, or some interesting and inspiring news about how a community is dealing with a problem.”
“对我来说，了解一些令人振奋和激动人心的事情——比如一项新发现、一种医学疗法，或者一些关于某个社区如何应对问题的有趣且鼓舞人心的消息——会让我感到欣慰。”
Jeff is a bit of a history buff, and enjoys seeing through the eyes of people from early in the last century, especially through movies. He works with elder veterans and tries to understand their perspective. He watches old movies from the ’30s and ’40s, including old newsreels. A favorite classic film of his is The Fighting Sullivans .
杰夫是个历史迷，喜欢从上世纪初人们的视角看待事物，尤其喜欢通过电影。他与一些老兵一起工作，努力理解他们的想法。他经常观看上世纪三四十年代的老电影，包括一些新闻短片。他最喜欢的经典电影之一是《沙利文一家》。
“The Fighting Sullivans tells us how to stick together. After all the poor father has lost, including his sons, he stills goes back to work. He finds brotherhood and fatherhood in his caring for his coworkers, his buddies.”
《战斗的苏利文一家》告诉我们如何团结一致。这位可怜的父亲失去了所有的一切，包括他的儿子们，但他仍然重返工作岗位。他在照顾同事和伙伴的过程中找到了兄弟情谊和父爱。
# ↩

GROUNDING, EXERCISE, BODY WORK, AND ENERGY WORK

接地、运动、身体疗法和能量疗法

Energy medicine, yoga, massage, and the martial arts are vital to comforters, especially for those of us prone to losing touch with our body’s messages and gut instincts when we push ourselves to serve others. Keeping a routine with these practices helps us read our bodies, know our limits, and honor our energy cycles. To be able to say no is crucial to comforters, but no doesn’t mean much if we don’t truly heed our body’s wisdom about what we can and cannot actually do.
能量医学、瑜伽、按摩和武术对照顾者来说至关重要，尤其对我们这些在竭力服务他人时容易忽略身体信号和直觉的人来说更是如此。坚持这些练习有助于我们了解自己的身体，认识自己的极限，并尊重自身的能量周期。学会说“不”对照顾者来说至关重要，但如果我们不真正倾听身体的智慧，不去了解自己能做什么、不能做什么，那么“不”就毫无意义。

Conclusion Comfort Is All Around Us

结论：舒适无处不在

ANGELS AT THE DOOR

门前的天使

In the mid-1990s, angels were all the rage. I collected angel cards, angel calendars, angel music, and angel stories, and in my job as a rehab counselor on the oncology unit at a hospital in Richmond, Virginia, angels were my role models for comforting. I also dreamed of the day I would have children to comfort.
上世纪九十年代中期，天使风靡一时。我收集天使卡片、天使日历、天使音乐和天使故事。在弗吉尼亚州里士满一家医院的肿瘤科担任康复咨询师期间，天使是我安慰病人的榜样。我也梦想着有一天能拥有孩子，去安慰他们。
Unfortunately, it was during this period that I learned I could never have my own children because of premature ovarian failure. And two months after the day I received this news, on a Friday afternoon in August, I was laid off from my job, along with three hundred others, when the hospital downsized. I felt barren, isolated, and different from other “normal” women I knew. And most of all, I grieved the life I thought I had been destined to live.
不幸的是，正是在这段时间里，我得知自己因卵巢早衰而永远无法生育。得知这一消息两个月后，八月的一个星期五下午，医院裁员，我和其他三百多人一起被解雇了。我感到自己失去了生育能力，孤立无援，与我认识的其他“正常”女性格格不入。最重要的是，我为自己原本以为命中注定的生活感到悲痛。
That following Saturday, while my husband was away on a long business trip, I cried all day. My angel books and angel music could no longer comfort me. I prayed to God to send me a real angel. I was ready for a bona fide spiritual visit from heaven.
接下来的那个星期六，我丈夫出差在外，我哭了一整天。天使书籍和天使音乐都无法再安慰我了。我向上帝祈祷，求他派一位真正的天使来见我。我渴望得到一次真正来自天堂的灵性探访。
The doorbell rang. Oh my God, who could that be? I wondered. It couldn’t be an angel, you silly fool, I chided myself. Before I ran downstairs to answer the door, I glanced at myself in the mirror. Pale, puffy, with tear-drenched cheeks, I quickly wiped my face with the bottom of my white polo shirt.
门铃响了。天哪，会是谁呢？我心想。不可能是天使，你这个傻瓜，我责备自己。在跑下楼去开门之前，我瞥了一眼镜子里的自己。脸色苍白，浮肿，泪水浸湿了双颊，我赶紧用白色polo衫的下摆擦了擦脸。
As I approached the door, I checked through the peep hole and saw a small, sweaty, man in a filthy T-shirt and muddy shoes. He must have been one of the laborers who worked on my neighbor’s lawn. What was he doing at my door? Annoyed, I almost didn’t open the door for him. But I did, and as I stepped onto the porch in the sweltering heat to speak with him, I noticed that a golden retriever was standing next to the man, staring at me, wagging his tail. The man smiled politely and asked, “Is this your dog?”
我走到门口，透过猫眼往里看，看到一个身材矮小、满头大汗的男人，穿着脏兮兮的T恤和沾满泥巴的鞋子。他应该是邻居家草坪上的工人。他怎么会出现在我家门口？我有点恼火，差点没给他开门。但我还是开了门，顶着酷热走上门廊，准备和他说话。这时我注意到，他旁边站着一只金毛犬，正盯着我看，摇着尾巴。男人礼貌地笑了笑，问道：“这是你的狗吗？”
“No . . .” I answered, drawn to the dog’s friendly eyes.
“不……”我回答道，被狗狗友善的眼神吸引住了。
The man struggled to speak in English. “I’m looking for his . . . for his person.”
那人努力用英语说道：“我在找他……找他本人。”
“I’m sorry, but I don’t know who he belongs to. I don’t have a dog.”
“对不起，我不知道他是谁的。我没有养狗。”
The dog panted in the heavy humidity. The man looked upon the dog tenderly and said, “Can he have some . . . some . . .”
潮湿闷热的空气中，狗喘着粗气。男人温柔地看着狗，说道：“它能吃点……吃点……”
“Water? Do you think the dog needs some water?”
“水？你觉得狗狗需要喝点水吗？”
“Yeah.” He nodded.
“是啊。”他点了点头。
“Would you like some water?” I asked the man.
“你想喝点水吗？”我问那人。
“Yeah. Thank you.”
“是啊，谢谢。”
“Hold on just a minute.” I brought the dog a bowl of water and the man a glass of water. They both stood on my front porch, drinking it down. I realized I was thirsty, too.
“等一下。”我给狗端来一碗水，给那人端来一杯水。他们俩站在我家前廊上，咕咚咕咚地喝了起来。这时我才意识到，我也渴了。
The man thanked me again. I asked if there was any more I could do. “Could I call someone about the dog? Would you like some more water?”
那人再次向我道谢。我问他是否还有什么我可以帮忙的。“我可以打电话叫人来处理一下那条狗的事吗？您需要再来点水吗？”
“No, that’s okay . . . I know somebody who can help me, who has a car and stuff.”
“不，没关系……我认识一个能帮我的人，他有车什么的。”
“Okay. By the way, you are really nice to be doing this. I hope you find the owner.”
“好的。对了，你真是太好了，愿意做这件事。希望你能找到失主。”
He nodded modestly, then left quickly, as the dog followed him eagerly, at ease with the man.
他谦逊地点了点头，然后迅速离开，那条狗热情地跟在他身后，对这个人很熟悉。
I closed the door and stood in the hallway, stunned. Just ten minutes earlier, desperate enough to go begging to God, I had prayed for a brilliant, glowing angel to come to me. But instead, this humble man and a lost dog had come to my door on this gruelingly hot day. Sure, I could have been suspicious and wary. He might have been using the dog as a cover for something. But no, I felt his good-heartedness and the dog’s sweetness and trust instantly. I sauntered to the kitchen, poured myself a glass of water, and drank the coolness down.
我关上门，呆立在走廊里，震惊不已。就在十分钟前，我绝望地向上帝祈祷，希望一位光芒四射的天使能降临到我身边。然而，在这酷热难耐的日子里，来到我家门口的却是一位谦逊的男子和一只迷路的狗。当然，我本可以心存疑虑，保持警惕。他或许是想借狗掩盖什么。但是，不，我立刻感受到了他的善良，也感受到了狗狗的可爱和信任。我踱步走到厨房，给自己倒了一杯水，痛快地喝下这清凉。
Was this stranger my angel? I don’t know. But I do know that in witnessing his beautiful kindness toward that dog I was reassured that comforting still existed here on earth even if it didn’t in heaven—and this hopeful reminder opened my heart up again. In the end, the art of comforting is nothing more than a language of the heart—someone we barely know or even a complete stranger reaching out to us at just the moment when all hope has left. But how will you know when it is your turn to answer the call? Listen with your heart. And always remember, comfort is all around us. We are never alone.
这位陌生人是我的天使吗？我不知道。但我知道，当他看到他对那只狗展现出的美好善意时，我确信，即使天堂不再有慰藉，人间依然存在——这份充满希望的提醒再次敞开了我的心扉。归根结底，安慰的艺术不过是一种心灵的语言——一个我们几乎不认识的人，甚至是一个完全陌生的人，在我们最绝望的时候向我们伸出援手。但你如何知道何时轮到你回应这份呼唤呢？用心聆听。永远记住，安慰就在我们身边。我们永远不会孤单。

Preface to Part Five

T HIS FINAL SECTION OF THE BOOK is a handy guide to ideas, suggestions, resources, and practical tips for comforting others. I have divided it into three sections.
本书的最后一部分是一份实用指南，提供了安慰他人的想法、建议、资源和实用技巧。我将其分为三个部分。
# ↩

SECTION A: COMFORTING FROM THE WORLD OF ENTERTAINMENT: A MEDIA GUIDE

A部分：来自娱乐界的慰藉：媒体指南

Here are movies, books, music, TV shows, and You Tube videos that people have told me have comforted them. These lists reflect hundreds of individual suggestions derived from sixteen years of facilitating support groups, speaking to audiences, and teaching classes in the art of comforting. I’ve categorized the media groups into accessible listings and lively genres to make choosing a movie, a book, or music a more enjoyable and comforting experience.
这里列出了一些电影、书籍、音乐、电视节目和YouTube视频，这些都是人们告诉我曾给予他们慰藉的。这些清单汇集了数百条个人建议，这些建议源自我十六年来组织互助小组、面向公众演讲以及教授安慰技巧课程的经验。我将这些媒体类别按易于查找的列表和生动有趣的类型进行分类，旨在让您在选择电影、书籍或音乐时获得更愉悦、更舒适的体验。
These selections of comforting media listings are only meant to get us started, as samples, not comprehensive, definitive lists. I would not want to have the last word on what comforts us about a movie, a memoir, or a song. I want to inspire comforters to use their imagination and wit in choosing media, and also to use their hearts and intuition in matching media choices to the people we are comforting. The Food Groups for the Soul are presented lightheartedly to help us percolate on ideas for offering comfort to meet the needs of the individual or group.
这些精选的抚慰心灵的媒体推荐仅供参考，并非全面详尽的最终清单。我并不想对一部电影、一本回忆录或一首歌如何抚慰人心拥有最终的评判权。我希望启发那些想要抚慰他人的人，让他们在选择媒体时运用想象力和智慧，同时也希望他们能够用心感受，并根据被抚慰者的具体情况选择合适的媒体。这些“心灵食粮”以轻松幽默的方式呈现，旨在帮助我们思考如何提供抚慰，以满足个人或群体的不同需求。
# ↩

SECTION B: COMFORTING FROM A TO Z , FROM ANGELS TO ZITHERS

第二部分：从A到Z的慰藉，从天使到齐特琴

Here’s where we can really have fun brainstorming on what’s out there in the world to comfort us. These comfort enhancers are listed for us to lighten, soften, and relax the tone of our environments and gatherings. (I admit, I had a blast putting these lists together. And I invite any reader to make their own lists of comforting things.) This exercise in simply writing down the comforting things around us reminds me of the wonderful song “My Favorite Things” from The Sound of Music .
在这里，我们可以尽情发挥创意，想想世界上有哪些东西能让我们感到舒适。这些提升舒适感的物品清单旨在帮助我们营造轻松、柔和、放松的氛围，改善我们周围的环境和聚会氛围。（说实话，我整理这些清单的过程非常愉快。我也邀请所有读者列出自己的舒适清单。）这种简单地写下身边舒适事物的方法，让我想起了《音乐之声》里那首动听的歌曲《我最喜欢的东西》。
Our favorite comforting things are listed in Section B in alphabetical order for easy reference.
为了方便查阅，我们最喜欢的令人感到舒适的事物已按字母顺序列在 B 部分。
# ↩

SECTION C: COMFORTING RESOURCES AND SUGGESTED READING

C 部分：慰藉资源和推荐阅读

This is also a start-up list of comforting websites and suggested reading selections. Once again, I wanted to inspire and stimulate ideas, not to present comprehensive lists. I’ve chosen in particular websites that have user-friendly, well-organized, pertinent, and updated links, so that these sites serve as clearinghouses and resource guides in their own ways.
这也是一份初步的实用网站和推荐阅读清单。再次强调，我的目的是激发灵感，启发思考，而不是提供一份详尽的清单。我特意挑选了一些用户友好、组织有序、内容相关且链接及时更新的网站，希望它们能以各自的方式发挥信息中心和资源指南的作用。
# ↩

A Guide to Comforting Things
安慰物品指南
# ↩

Section A. Comforting from the World of Entertainment: A Media Guide

A 部分：来自娱乐世界的慰藉：媒体指南

Comfort Movies, Comfort Books, Comfort Music
舒缓的电影、舒缓的书籍、舒缓的音乐

For the past five years, I’ve gathered lists of suggested comfort movies, books, TV shows, You Tube videos, and music. These reflect the vast input from members of support groups and seminars, dozens of colleagues, and hundreds of audience participants all voicing their most comforting influences from the arts and literature. In collecting this data and finding ways to organize the suggestions, I recognized recurring themes, genres, and styles being recommended, revealing universally comforting works of art. Adding to this, I studied the trends of bestselling books, popular movies, music, and TV shows on Amazon.com , IMDb, Billboard, and many other ratings sites.
过去五年，我收集了一系列令人感到慰藉的电影、书籍、电视剧、YouTube视频和音乐推荐清单。这些清单反映了来自互助小组和研讨会成员、数十位同事以及数百位听众的广泛意见，他们都分享了自己从艺术和文学中获得的慰藉。在收集这些数据并整理推荐的过程中，我发现了一些反复出现的主题、类型和风格，从中可以找到一些具有普遍慰藉作用的艺术作品。此外，我还研究了亚马逊、IMDb、Billboard以及其他众多评分网站上畅销书、热门电影、音乐和电视剧的趋势。
I discovered the most important common denominator of a comforting story or song is that it has a good landing with a positive message, giving us hope. Hope and hard work can float us through stormy times—proven in movies, books, and inspirational news clips. A pilot can land a plane on the Hudson, people of color can rise to high positions, slum kids can make it out of the slums, addicts can make it through their recovery. If we are getting jittery that humanity is fast going to hell in a handbasket (economically, environmentally, morally, and militarily), we need to witness a serious spunk in action. Stories and songs sustain us with solid assurance our beloved protagonists are going to succeed somehow, with resource fulness , not just resources, coming from inside as much as outside of themselves. This doesn’t mean we have to have a “feel good” ending, but at least a “feel better” ending, with characters who triumph over adversity, or muddle through it all pretty well.
我发现，一个能抚慰人心的故事或歌曲最重要的共同点在于，它总能以积极的信息圆满收尾，给予我们希望。希望和努力能帮助我们度过风雨飘摇的时期——电影、书籍和励志新闻片段都证明了这一点。飞行员能让飞机在哈德逊河上安全降落，有色人种可以晋升到高位，贫民窟的孩子可以摆脱贫民窟的困境，瘾君子可以成功戒毒。如果我们开始焦虑不安，担心人类正在迅速走向毁灭（经济、环境、道德和军事方面），我们就需要看到一些真正令人振奋的行动。故事和歌曲能让我们坚信，我们所喜爱的主人公最终会凭借智慧——而不仅仅是资源——取得成功，这种智慧和智慧既来自他们自身，也来自外部。这并不意味着我们必须要有一个“完美”的结局，但至少要有一个“令人欣慰”的结局，让主人公战胜逆境，或者至少能够很好地度过难关。
For art to be comforting, even if we went through a character’s anguish, or a song’s yearning, or a painting’s intense mood, our spirits are lifted at the end of our encounter. From whimsical to funny to cheery to high-grit inspirational, comfort comes in various nurturing ways for the soul, as long as the take-away vibe is upbeat, either energizing us, calming us, or amusing us. These nurturing variations, themes, and genres have beckoned me to organize them into “food groups” for the soul, because they feed the soul. Comforting art can also deal with dark themes, as long as we are reassured at the end that the bad stuff the character or artist went through is well worth the journey.
艺术之所以能带来慰藉，即便我们经历了人物的痛苦、歌曲的渴望或画作的强烈情绪，最终都能获得心灵的慰藉。从异想天开到幽默风趣，从欢快愉悦到振奋人心，慰藉以各种滋养灵魂的方式呈现，只要最终带给我们的是积极向上的感受，无论是激励我们、抚慰我们，还是让我们感到愉悦。这些滋养灵魂的变体、主题和类型促使我将它们归类为灵魂的“食物”，因为它们确实能够滋养灵魂。慰藉人心的艺术作品也可以探讨黑暗的主题，只要最终我们能够确信，人物或艺术家所经历的苦难都是值得的。
I have organized six basic “food groups” of comfort for the soul in the arts and media, all containing good landings and hefty doses of positive energy. We are left heartened, comforted, inspired, or at least a bit calmer after our encounter with these creations.
我总结了艺术和媒体领域六大抚慰心灵的“精神食粮”，它们都蕴含着美好的内容和满满的正能量。欣赏这些作品之后，我们会感到振奋、慰藉、受到启发，或者至少内心平静一些。
No tragedies are allowed on the following lists, though they are beautiful and important. I know many people say they are comforted by tragedies, but I have found that they are not quite as comforting for most of us, though tragedies are healing in their own ways. Sorry, Million Dollar Baby , Das Boot , Mystic River , The House of Mirth , American Beauty , No Country for Old Men , and so many great movies—not going here! And, of course, horror flicks and extremely violent thrillers are much too rough on the nerves to make the comfort movie lists below. Sorry, Kill Bill , The Exorcist , Halloween , The Texas Chainsaw Massacre , Clockwork Orange , not going here either.
以下片单中不允许出现悲剧，尽管它们美丽而重要。我知道很多人说悲剧能给他们带来慰藉，但我发现对大多数人来说，悲剧带来的慰藉并不那么强烈，尽管它们以自己的方式具有疗愈作用。抱歉，《百万美元宝贝》、《从海底出击》、《神秘河》、《欢乐之家》、《美国丽人》、《老无所依》等等许多优秀的电影——它们不在榜单之列！当然，恐怖片和极其暴力的惊悚片也太刺激神经了，所以它们也不在以下的“治愈系电影”榜单之列。抱歉，《杀死比尔》、《驱魔人》、《万圣节》、《德州电锯杀人狂》、《发条橙》，它们也不在榜单之列。

CLASSIC COMFORT: FROM HEARTENING TO HILARIOUS

经典舒适：从温馨到爆笑

This is comfort we might slip into a “snuggie” to enjoy. Sit back, sip a cup of hot chocolate, and “veg out” when there’s no energy left to function. The following classic comforts demand little from us, as no-brainer yet delightful entertainment. We can laugh, coo, sigh, and giggle when we haven’t even smiled all day long. When we have a cold or flu and feel yucky overall, this kind of remedy usually works.
这是一种我们可能会钻进“毛毯”里享受的舒适感。放松身心，啜饮一杯热巧克力，在精疲力竭、无力工作的时候彻底“放松”一下。以下这些经典的舒适方式无需我们费心，就能带来轻松愉悦的娱乐体验。即使我们一整天都没笑过，也能开怀大笑、发出轻柔的低语、叹息，甚至咯咯地笑。当我们感冒或流感，感觉浑身不舒服时，这类疗法通常很有效。
Comforting Qualities: Fun, funny, engaging, delightful, cheery, entertaining, reassuring, undemanding, uncomplicated

CLASSIC COMFORT LISTS FOR CHILDREN

儿童经典舒适清单

Comfort Movies for Children
适合儿童观看的温馨电影
For a helpful guide to choosing movies for children and families, I recommend the book The Best Old Movies for Families: A Guide to Watching Together by Ty Burr.
对于如何为孩子和家庭选择电影，我推荐泰·伯尔所著的《最适合家庭观看的老电影：一起观看指南》这本书。
Also, checking in with Movie Mom (Nell Minow) on the Belief Net website, parents are given good guidance to what’s comforting and appropriate (or not) with new releases for children and teens. Nell also compiles innovative theme lists of movie recommendations to help families pick the right flicks.
此外，家长们还可以参考 Belief Net 网站上的“电影妈妈”（Nell Minow）的建议，了解哪些新上映的电影适合儿童和青少年观看，哪些电影令人感到舒适和合适（或不适合）。Nell 还精心制作了各种主题电影推荐清单，帮助家庭挑选合适的影片。
According to hundreds of people I’ve asked, one of the most all-time comforting movies for families and children is Finding Nemo . More recently, dozens of people have told me the tender story of the movie Up has been comforting, too, dealing with loss issues. There is a great moment in the Up story, when a little boy says he misses a loved one, not because of the exciting things they did together, but because of the “boring” everyday things they shared together. I find this to be true about the comforting times in our lives, as we enjoy the ordinary routines and simple pastimes of daily life more than we might realize.
据我询问过的数百人说，《海底总动员》是史上最能抚慰家庭和孩子心灵的电影之一。最近，也有几十个人告诉我，电影《飞屋环游记》的温馨故事也让他们感到慰藉，因为它探讨了失去亲人的问题。《飞屋环游记》中有一个很棒的片段：一个小男孩说他想念亲人，不是因为他们一起做过的那些激动人心的事，而是因为他们一起经历过的那些“平凡”的日常琐事。我觉得这很贴切，因为我们生活中那些令人感到慰藉的时刻，往往是我们自己没有意识到的，其实都源于我们对平凡日常和简单消遣的享受。

GRITTY COMFORT: TRIUMPH OVER ADVERSITY

坚韧的慰藉：战胜逆境

Themes: true grit, underdogs, coming of age, recovery and healing, rags to riches, victory tales, the attainment of wisdom, stories of courage and moral strength, comeback stories, and bio pics. When we have plenty of energy but feel frustrated, wickedly cynical, or anxious, we might snap out of our funk with something from the more demanding, grittier menu of comforts. The endings in these movies may not be classically “feel-good,” but they are hopeful, “feel-better” endings, conveying the strength, resilience, and resourcefulness of the lead characters facing bleak situations. These tougher, riveting stories often can be ultimately comforting for us to boost our belief in the power of the human spirit.
主题：真正的勇气、弱者逆袭、成长、康复与治愈、白手起家、胜利故事、智慧的获得、勇气与道德力量的故事、东山再起的故事以及人物传记。当我们精力充沛却感到沮丧、愤世嫉俗或焦虑不安时，或许可以从这些更具挑战性、更接地气的慰藉之作中汲取力量，摆脱低落的情绪。这些电影的结局或许并非传统意义上的“皆大欢喜”，但它们充满希望，令人感到慰藉，展现了主人公在逆境中展现出的力量、韧性和智慧。这些扣人心弦、引人入胜的故事最终往往能抚慰我们的心灵，增强我们对人类精神力量的信念。
Comforting qualities: gutsy, hopeful, inspirational, life-affirming, spunky.
令人感到安慰的品质：勇敢、充满希望、鼓舞人心、积极向上、活泼好动。

QUIRKY COMFORT: SCREWED-UP BUT LOVABLE PEOPLE MUDDLING THROUGH

古怪的舒适：一群一团糟但可爱的人跌跌撞撞地摸索前行

Quirky, endearing indies we adore. Keeping the “fun” in dysfunctional families, communities, and love interests. Road trips, offbeat coming of age, funky problem-solving. Forget trying to be “normal.”
我们喜爱那些古怪又讨喜的独立电影。它们在问题重重的家庭、社区和爱情故事中保留着“乐趣”。公路旅行、另类的成长故事、奇特的解决问题方式。别再试图成为“正常人”了。
Comforting Qualities: Humility, accepting our imperfection, compassion, resourcefulness, wit, humor.
令人感到安慰的品质：谦逊、接受自己的不完美、同情心、足智多谋、机智、幽默。

SUBLIME COMFORT: HEAVEN ON EARTH

极致舒适：人间天堂

Comfort expressed spiritually, joyously, or gently, bringing a sense of grace into art, such as the angelic voice of someone singing “Ave Maria,” or the image of an eagle in flight. These moments give us chills, touching what is sacred inside our souls.
慰藉可以以精神层面、喜悦或温柔的方式表达，为艺术注入优雅之感，例如天使般吟唱《圣母颂》的歌声，或是雄鹰翱翔的画面。这些瞬间令人心潮澎湃，触动我们灵魂深处的神圣。
Comforting Qualities: Spiritual, soulful, awe-inspiring, serene, elegant.
令人感到舒适的特质：精神上的、深沉的、令人敬畏的、宁静的、优雅的。

Section B. Comforting from A to Z , from Angels to Zithers

B部分：从A到Z的慰藉，从天使到齐特琴

Activities and Enhancers for Creating a Comforting Atmosphere We can add the following ingredients to our homes for creating a comforting atmosphere with our families and friends.
营造舒适氛围的活动和增强因素 我们可以在家中添加以下元素，与家人和朋友一起营造舒适的氛围。
But first, before we go down the A to Z list, here are the top fifteen comforting essentials, the all-time favorite things most people need for comfort (not in any order).
但首先，在我们开始介绍 A 到 Z 的清单之前，这里列出了十五件最令人感到舒适的必需品，这些是大多数人获得舒适感所需要的永恒最爱之物（排名不分先后）。
THE TOP FIFTEEN COMFORTING ESSENTIALS
十五件最舒适的必备单品
The Arts for expressing ourselves, especially when words are hard to find
艺术是表达自我的途径，尤其是在难以找到合适的词语时。
Belief, a sense of meaning or purpose
信仰，一种意义感或目的感。
Comfort foods and drinks
令人感到舒适的食物和饮品
A comfortable place, home, or sanctuary, a sheltered, safe place to rest and restore oneself
一个舒适的地方，家，或者避难所，一个可以休息和恢复元气的庇护所。
Connection, a sense of belonging, community, being relational, having a support system
联系、归属感、社区、人际关系、拥有支持系统
Entertainment, media, games (including mindless distractions)
娱乐、媒体、游戏（包括无脑消遣）
Gratitude, recognizing what supports us
心怀感恩，认识到那些支持我们的人或事物。
Humor
幽默
Interests, passions, hobbies, outlets
兴趣爱好、热情所在、兴趣点、排解方式
Love, affection, warmth
爱、感情、温暖
Medication/treatment/therapy
药物/治疗/疗法
Nature, being connected with the Earth
自然，与地球相连
Pets, animals
宠物、动物
Sports
运动的
Touch, caresses, hugs, massages, footbaths, brushing hair, putting on lotion, putting on nail polish or makeup, sexual contact
触摸、爱抚、拥抱、按摩、足浴、梳头、涂抹润肤露、涂指甲油或化妆、性接触
And a little factoid: In times of economic hardship, people spend money on chocolate, lipstick, movies, and games more than most commodities. I hear sewing kits, craft-making kits, and Snuggie sales are going pretty well, too.
还有个小趣闻：经济困难时期，人们在巧克力、口红、电影和游戏上的花费比大多数其他商品都多。我听说缝纫套装、手工套装和毛毯的销量也相当不错。

AND HERE IS MY WHOLE LIST OF LIFE’S COMFORTS.
以下是我人生所有舒适享受的清单。

Section C. Comforting Resources and Suggested Reading RESOURCES: COMFORTING WEBSITES

C 部分：慰藉资源和推荐阅读 资源：慰藉网站

Comforting Gifts to Give and Share
赠送和分享的暖心礼物
• The Comfort Company
www.thecomfortcompany.net
• 舒适公司 www.thecomfortcompany.net
Comforting gifts for remembrance, such as memorial ornaments, sympathy cards and gifts, personalized objects and jewelry, keepsakes, art and prints, angels, all kinds of comforts for grieving people. Also a good resource list for other gifts, such as gift baskets. (Oprah has recognized and praised the company’s owner, Renee Wood, a former social worker.)
慰藉人心的纪念礼物，例如纪念饰品、慰问卡和礼品、个性化物品和珠宝、纪念品、艺术品和版画、天使摆件，以及各种能抚慰悲伤者的物品。此外，这里还提供其他礼物的实用清单，例如礼篮。（奥普拉曾公开表扬过这家公司的老板蕾妮·伍德，她曾是一名社工。）

Comforting Books, Games, Activities, and Media for Children
适合儿童的温馨书籍、游戏、活动和媒体
• Parents’ Choice Foundation, Parents’ Choice Awards www.Parents-choice.org
Diana Huss Green, founder of Parents’ Choice, gathers parents, educators, librarians, and other critics to review books, toys, games, and media for children. Diana has written articles about comfort books, such as “Finding Comfort in a Book,” on other sites such as www.education.com . Diana has created criteria for comfort books for children emphasizing stories with solid moral values and kindhearted characters. Her comfort book lists are wonderful and carefully selected.
• 家长之选基金会，家长之选奖 www.Parents-choice.org 家长之选基金会的创始人戴安娜·胡斯·格林召集家长、教育工作者、图书馆员和其他评论家，共同评选儿童书籍、玩具、游戏和媒体产品。戴安娜曾在www.education.com等网站上发表过关于“治愈系书籍”的文章，例如《在书中寻找慰藉》。她为儿童“治愈系书籍”制定了评判标准，强调故事中蕴含坚实的道德价值观和善良的角色。她精心挑选的“治愈系书籍”清单精彩纷呈。
• Children’s books on About.com childrensbooks.about.com
Plenty of guidance on books for children ages zero to twelve. I especially like the attention to little ones under six years of age, with great information on colorful picture books for reading aloud. Contains creative categories for selecting books, with a blog and helpful newsletter.
• About.com 上的儿童书籍专区 childrensbooks.about.com 为 0 至 12 岁的儿童提供了丰富的书籍选择指南。我尤其喜欢它对 6 岁以下幼儿的关注，其中包含许多适合朗读的彩色图画书信息。该网站还设有创意十足的图书分类，方便读者挑选书籍，并配有博客和实用的电子报。
• Education.com : Bringing Learning to Life
www.education.com
Aimed at parents, full of great ideas for activities, reading, games, and learning experiences with their children. This site helps families think of home-based activities.
• Education.com：让学习融入生活 www.education.com 该网站面向家长，提供丰富的亲子活动、阅读、游戏和学习体验创意。它能帮助家庭构思在家开展的活动。
Comforting Inspiration
令人慰藉的灵感
• Belief Net
www.beliefnet.com
For all kinds of spiritual seeker, this entertaining and informative site has something for everyone, for all religions and spiritual traditions. There are lists of comfort movies and books, and other comforts such as blessings, prayers, quotes, personal essays and stories, and plenty of inspirational news about what people around the world are doing to comfort others.
• Belief Net（www.beliefnet.com） 对于所有寻求精神慰藉的人来说，这个内容丰富、寓教于乐的网站都能满足他们的需求，涵盖所有宗教和灵修传统。网站提供抚慰人心的电影和书籍列表，以及其他慰藉资源，例如祝福语、祈祷文、名言警句、个人随笔和故事，还有大量关于世界各地人们如何抚慰他人的励志新闻。
• Simple Abundance
www.simpleabundance.com
Sarah Ban Breathnach’s wonderful book Simple Abundance: A Daybook of Comfort and Joy was the beginning of a series of highly comforting writings. Her website is loaded with current comforting news, articles, and resources for calming and quieting ourselves.
• Simple Abundance（www.simpleabundance.com）莎拉·班·布雷斯纳克（Sarah Ban Breathnach）的精彩著作《Simple Abundance: A Daybook of Comfort and Joy》（《简单富足：舒适与喜悦的日记》）开启了一系列抚慰人心的作品。她的网站汇集了大量抚慰人心的最新资讯、文章和资源，帮助我们平静下来，获得心灵的安宁。
Caregiver Support
照护者支持
• Family Caregiving 101
www.familycaregiving101.org
Helpful, basic, practical education and support for caregivers. A great primer.
• 家庭照护入门 www.familycaregiving101.org 为照护者提供实用、基础的教育和支持。一本很好的入门读物。
• National Family Caregivers Association
www.nfcacares.org
Now on Twitter and building e-communities and family caregiver forums, this site is highly useful for busy caregivers.
• 全国家庭护理员协会 www.nfcacares.org 现在已入驻 Twitter，并建立电子社区和家庭护理员论坛，该网站对忙碌的护理员来说非常有用。
• AARP, Family Caregiving
www.aarp.org/family/caregiving
AARP has excellent guidance and support for caregivers in their fifties and older.
• AARP，家庭照护www.aarp.org/family/caregiving AARP 为 50 岁及以上的照护者提供优秀的指导和支持。
Grief and Bereavement
悲伤与丧亲之痛
• HelpGuide.org
HelpGuide’s Helping a Grieving Person: www.helpguide.org/mental/helping_grieving.htm
Solid, well-rounded guidance on offering comfort and support for grieving people. Has special sections for supporting adults, as well as grieving teens and children. Links to superior articles and resources.
• HelpGuide.org 的“帮助悲伤的人”：www.helpguide.org/mental/helping_grieving.htm 提供全面、深入的指导，帮助人们安慰和支持悲伤的人。网站设有专门版块，分别针对成年人、青少年和儿童的悲伤关怀，并提供优质文章和资源的链接。
• MentalHelp.net
www.mentalhelp.net
A vast and comprehensive site for a wide range of mental health issues, and includes excellent pages for guidance on the grief process as well as for supporting grieving adults and children.
• MentalHelp.net www.mentalhelp.net 是一个内容丰富、涵盖广泛心理健康问题的网站，其中包含许多优秀的页面，为悲伤过程提供指导，并为悲伤的成人和儿童提供支持。
• The Center for Loss and Life Transition and Companion Press Bookstore
www.centerforloss.com
Psychiatrist Alan Wolfelt offers a comforting program of “companioning” with grieving people, and his helpful, accessible books are available at his Companion Press Bookstore online.
• 失落与生命过渡中心和伴侣出版社书店www.centerforloss.com 精神科医生艾伦·沃尔费尔特提供了一个令人感到安慰的“陪伴”悲伤者的计划，他那些实用易懂的书籍可以在他的伴侣出版社书店在线购买。
• Beyond Indigo
www.beyondindigo.com
Lots of online support for all kinds of grief, with great places for posting and connecting our thoughts, feelings, and remembrances.
• Beyond Indigowww.beyondindigo.com 为各种悲伤提供大量的在线支持，是发布和交流我们的想法、感受和回忆的好地方。
• AARP, Life After Loss
www.aarp.org/family/lifeafterloss
Full of helpful and practical articles for bereaved families, and also support for coping with issues related to aging.
• AARP，“失去亲人后的生活”www.aarp.org/family/lifeafterloss 网站上有很多对丧亲家庭有帮助的实用文章，也为应对与衰老相关的问题提供支持。
• GriefNet
www.griefnet.org
The virtual memorial program is comforting, with plenty of online support groups that can be joined for a small fee.
• GriefNetwww.griefnet.org 虚拟追思会项目令人感到安慰，只需支付少量费用即可加入许多在线支持小组。
• Hospice Foundation of America, Grief and Loss Support
www.hospicefoundation.org/griefandloss
Recommended reading: “Shattering the 8 Myths of Grieving” and “8 Myths About Children and Loss . ” Great articles and links for all kinds of bereavement issues, as well as caregiver and end-of-life issues. Also, the popular Journeys newsletter for bereaved families is available here.
• 美国临终关怀基金会，悲伤与失落支持 www.hospicefoundation.org/griefandloss 推荐阅读：《打破悲伤的八大迷思》和《关于儿童与失落的八大迷思》。其中包含大量关于丧亲之痛、照护者问题以及临终关怀的优质文章和链接。此外，广受欢迎的丧亲家庭通讯《旅程》也可在此处获取。
For Bereaved Families Who Have Lost Children
致失去孩子的悲痛家庭
• The Compassionate Friends
www.compassionatefriends.org
• 慈悲之友 (The Compassionate Friends) www.compassionatefriends.org
Grieving Children and Teens
悲伤的儿童和青少年
• The Dougy Center
www.dougy.org
One of the oldest and most highly respected centers for grieving children and teens. This inspirational program is a popular and successful model for many centers nationwide. They have a great online store for books to help grieving children and teens, as well as a search engine for finding grief support resources in your city or state.
• 道吉中心 (www.dougy.org) 是历史最悠久、最受尊敬的儿童和青少年悲伤辅导中心之一。这个鼓舞人心的项目已成为全国许多中心的热门成功典范。他们拥有一个很棒的在线书店，出售帮助悲伤儿童和青少年的书籍，还有一个搜索引擎，可以帮助你找到所在城市或州的悲伤支持资源。
Pet Loss
宠物离世
• HelpGuide’s Pet Loss Support
www.helpguide.org/mental/grieving_pets.htm#online
A good starting place for coping with the death of a pet.
• HelpGuide 的宠物丧失支持 www.helpguide.org/mental/grieving_pets.htm#online 应对宠物死亡的良好起点。
End-of-Life Issues
生命末期问题
• Growth House
www.growthhouse.org
For issues related to end-of-life matters, caring for a dying loved one, providing support and comfort, as well as facing grief and anticipatory grief.
• Growth Housewww.growthhouse.org 为临终关怀、照顾临终亲人、提供支持和安慰以及面对悲伤和预期悲伤等相关问题提供帮助。
• Hospice Foundation of America
www.hospicefoundation.org
Highly comprehensive, used by professionals in hospice and palliative care and by family caregivers alike.
• 美国临终关怀基金会 www.hospicefoundation.org 内容非常全面，临终关怀和姑息治疗的专业人员以及家庭护理人员都在使用。
For Endings of Relationships and Divorce
关于关系的结束和离婚
• Getting Past Your Past
www.gettingpastyourpast.wordpress.com
• 放下过去 www.gettingpastyourpast.wordpress.com
• Getting Past Your Breakup
www.gettingpastyourbreakup.com
Susan Elliott, a former grief counselor and lawyer, has created an inspirational and informative website and book of the same name to help us through breakups of all kinds.
• 如何走出分手阴影 www.gettingpastyourbreakup.com 前悲伤咨询师兼律师苏珊·艾略特创建了一个鼓舞人心、内容丰富的网站和同名书籍，以帮助我们度过各种类型的分手。
• Divorce Support
www.divorcesupport.com
A well-established, well-used site, very interactive with blogs and forums; full of topics dealing with divorce.
• 离婚支持网站 www.divorcesupport.com 一个成熟且广受欢迎的网站，拥有丰富的博客和论坛互动内容；涵盖了与离婚相关的各种主题。
• MentalHelp.net
www.mentalhelp.net
On this vast site, the topic of divorce is well covered, from getting through it to recovering from it. Good search program for locating local therapists, and recommendations for current books and articles.
• MentalHelp.net (www.mentalhelp.net) 这个内容丰富的网站全面涵盖了离婚话题，从如何度过离婚难关到如何从中恢复过来，应有尽有。网站还提供便捷的搜索功能，方便用户查找当地的心理咨询师，并推荐最新的书籍和文章。
Comforting for Loss of a Job
失业后的安慰
• Riley Guide, Coping with Job Loss
www.rileyguide.com/cope.html
The section of the Riley Guide offers both practical and emotional guidance and links to online support groups, resources, and networks.
• Riley 指南，应对失业 www.rileyguide.com/cope.html Riley 指南的这一部分提供了实用和情感上的指导，以及在线支持小组、资源和网络的链接。
• Career Planning at About.com and Job Searching at About.com
http://careerplanning.about.com
Dawn Rosenberg McKay addresses job loss, job transition, and unemployment issues on her extensive Career Change pages.
For more practical and detailed information on doing a job search, About.com guide Alison Doyle is helpful with her Job Search pages and has a busy blog ( http://jobsearch.about.com ). I have used these guides over the years in my social work tasks, helping clients coping with job loss and financial losses, and have found them to be highly reliable and consistently updated.
About.com 的职业规划和求职指南：http://careerplanning.about.com Dawn Rosenberg McKay 在其内容丰富的“职业转型”页面上探讨了失业、职业转型和失业问题。如需更实用、更详细的求职信息，About.com 的求职指南 Alison Doyle 在其“求职”页面和活跃的博客 (http://jobsearch.about.com) 中提供了许多有用的信息。多年来，我在社会工作中一直使用这些指南，帮助客户应对失业和经济损失，发现它们非常可靠且持续更新。
For Coping with Trauma and PTSD
应对创伤和创伤后应激障碍
• Gift from Within
www.giftfromwithin.org
This is an international organization to help survivors of trauma and victimization. It’s comprehensive and well organized, with informative and encouraging articles, guidance, and resources. It is also helpful for those who care for traumatized individuals. Excellent for locating support groups, Web casts, and many other online supports.
• Gift from Within（www.giftfromwithin.org）是一个国际组织，致力于帮助创伤和受害幸存者。它内容全面、组织有序，提供信息丰富且鼓舞人心的文章、指导和资源。对于照顾受创伤者的护理人员来说，它也大有裨益。该网站非常适合查找互助小组、网络直播和其他在线支持服务。
• MentalHelp.net
www.mentalhelp.net
Excellent guidance for trauma support, as well as for coping with disasters, violence, and abuse and dealing with other kinds of anxiety.
• MentalHelp.net www.mentalhelp.net 为创伤支持、应对灾难、暴力和虐待以及处理其他类型的焦虑提供优秀的指导。
Connecting to the Disability Community
与残障人士社群建立联系
Here are two essential websites for resources on disabilities:
• Wounded Warrior Project
www.woundedwarriorproject.org
• Disability.gov
www.disability.org
以下是两个提供残疾人资源的重要网站：• 伤残军人援助项目 (Wounded Warrior Project) www.woundedwarriorproject.org • Disability.gov www.disability.org
Comforting and Healing with the Arts
艺术带来的慰藉与疗愈
• Arts and Healing Network
www.artheals.org
This network has fantastic links to organizations and healing artists around the world. It’s very comprehensive, well organized, and inspirational. Go exploring on this site and your spirit will get a boost. Check out the Image Quilt—beautiful and comforting.
• 艺术与疗愈网络 (www.artheals.org) 这个网络汇集了世界各地众多机构和疗愈艺术家的精彩链接。它内容全面、条理清晰，而且充满启发性。不妨浏览一下这个网站，你的心灵会得到提升。看看“图像拼布”吧——美丽又抚慰人心。
• Paint Your Own Pottery
www.paintyourownpottery.net
A site to help your family find a place to paint pottery near you, anywhere in the United States.
• Paint Your Own Potterywww.paintyourownpottery.net 一个帮助您的家人在美国任何地方找到附近可以绘制陶器的地方的网站。
• The Foundation for Hospital Art
www.hospitalart.com
A program providing volunteers for painting artwork and murals and decorating hospitals to create a comforting atmosphere.
• 医院艺术基金会 www.hospitalart.com 该项目提供志愿者为医院绘制艺术作品和壁画，并装饰医院，以营造舒适的氛围。
• Now I Lay Me Down to Sleep
www.nowilaymedowntosleep.org
This is an organization that provides photographers (at no charge) to take pictures of families in hospitals, when an infant is very ill and not likely to live. The photographer will come to the hospital and take pictures of the infant in the arms of the parents and with the family.
• “现在我躺下睡觉”（Now I Lay Me Down to Sleep，www.nowilaymedowntosleep.org）是一个为医院里病情危重、生命垂危的婴儿及其家人提供免费摄影服务的组织。摄影师会前往医院，拍摄婴儿依偎在父母怀中以及与家人在一起的照片。
• Project Compassion
www.heropaintings.com/kzindex.aspx
This is an organization that helps grieving families dealing with the loss of a loved one who gave his or her life in service to the armed forces. An artist will paint a portrait of the deceased veteran to commemorate the service and comfort the family.
• “同情项目”（Project Compassion，网址：www.heropaintings.com/kzindex.aspx）是一个帮助因亲人牺牲而悲痛的家庭的组织。艺术家将为逝去的退伍军人绘制肖像，以纪念他们的奉献并慰藉家属。
• Playing for Change
www.playingforchange.com
They produced and organized the highly popular Stand By Me on YouTube, as musicians around the world gather in the name of peace.
• Playing for Change（www.playingforchange.com）他们在 YouTube 上制作并组织了广受欢迎的《Stand By Me》，世界各地的音乐家们为了和平聚集在一起。
Comforting with Nature and Connecting with the Earth
亲近自然，与地球建立联系
• Roots and Shoots
www.rootsandshoots.org
This international program developed by Jane Goodall teaches children and families about taking care of our earth, in our own communities and around the world. Many schools and nature centers have adopted this highly popular program throughout the United States.
• “根与芽”（Roots and Shoots，www.rootsandshoots.org）是由珍·古道尔创立的国际项目，旨在教导儿童和家庭如何在社区乃至世界各地保护地球。美国许多学校和自然中心都采用了这项广受欢迎的项目。
Three Great Books about Comforting Others The Etiquette of Illness: What to Say When You Can’t Find the Words by Susan P. Halpern
三本关于安慰他人的好书：《疾病礼仪：当你找不到合适的词语时该说什么》（作者：苏珊·P·哈尔彭）
This is highly recommended reading for supporting people who are dealing with severe and life-threatening illness.
强烈推荐本书给那些正在与重病和危及生命的疾病作斗争的人们阅读。
Healing Conversations: What to Say When You Don’t Know What to Say by Nance Guilmartin
疗愈对话：当你不知该说什么时该说什么（作者：南希·吉尔马丁）
Not just for bereavement, this book covers many difficult and challenging times in our lives (loss of job, divorce, illness, crisis), and offers guidance for what to say to those in the midst of these times.
这本书不仅适用于丧亲之痛，还涵盖了我们生活中许多艰难和充满挑战的时刻（失业、离婚、疾病、危机），并为我们提供了在这种时期应该如何与他人交谈的指导。

Turning to One Another: Simple Conversations to Restore Hope to the Future by Margaret J. Wheatley
《彼此依靠：用简单的对话重燃对未来的希望》（Turning to One Another: Simple Conversations to Restore Hope to the Future）作者：玛格丽特·J·惠特利
This book is gently written yet deeply inspiring for restoring the art of fostering good conversation, in both home and work settings.
这本书文笔温和，却又极具启发性，它能帮助我们重拾在家庭和工作环境中培养良好沟通能力的艺术。

Acknowledgments: The Return of the Blue Herons
致谢：《蓝鹭归来》
Finally the Maine landscape, once white, then gray, then muddy, has turned a brilliant green this spring. Lilacs, irises, and apple blossoms burst forth along the sidewalks of the town of Yarmouth. It has been a rougher than usual winter, even for Mainers, and now people glow in their relief and pleasure. Everyone moves with a spring in their step, young fathers and mothers pushing baby strollers, older couples with dogs, packs of teens running in track clothes, and kids charging ahead on their bicycles.
缅因州的大地，曾经的白色、灰色、泥泞，终于在今年春天披上了绚丽的绿色。丁香花、鸢尾花和苹果花在雅茅斯镇的人行道上竞相绽放。即使对缅因州人来说，今年的冬天也比往年更加严酷，如今人们脸上都洋溢着如释重负的喜悦。每个人都步履轻快，年轻的父母推着婴儿车，老年夫妇牵着狗，一群群穿着运动服的青少年奔跑着，孩子们骑着自行车飞驰而过。
But, as tranquil as my little town of Yarmouth is this afternoon, the promise of a beautiful evening beckons me to return to Wolfe’s Neck Woods for a walk in the long light through the pines. This evening I yearn especially to see the great blue herons. I have not seen a single heron since November, for six cold months. I know they love Wolfe’s Neck Woods, where the Harraseeket River meets the wide Casco Bay, beside Googins Island. A heron colony thrives nearby, on another tiny island, one of the largest refuges for herons in New England, protected by the state of Maine and the Nature Conservancy.
虽然今天下午雅茅斯小镇宁静祥和，但傍晚的美好景象却召唤着我重返沃尔夫颈森林，在松林间漫步，沐浴着悠长的夕阳。今晚我尤其渴望见到苍鹭。自从去年十一月以来，整整六个月的寒冬，我都没见过一只苍鹭。我知道它们喜欢沃尔夫颈森林，那里是哈拉西基特河汇入宽阔的卡斯科湾的地方，毗邻古金斯岛。附近另一个小岛上，也栖息着一群苍鹭，那是新英格兰地区最大的苍鹭保护区之一，受到缅因州政府和自然保护协会的共同保护。
I arrive at the rocks near Googins Island, where the ospreys are busy as usual. I step easily along the large flat rocks of the shoreline to a small sandy beach and sit on a patch of moss. Though the tide is low and the glistening, spongy bottom of the sea is exposed and bustling with birdlife, I see no herons. Odd, I think. Herons are usually here, standing in clusters, very still, like sentinels, watching quietly for fish.
我来到古金斯岛附近的岩石边，那里的鱼鹰像往常一样忙碌着。我轻松地沿着海岸线上平坦的大岩石走到一小片沙滩上，坐在一片苔藓上。虽然正值退潮，波光粼粼、松软的海底裸露出来，鸟儿们熙熙攘攘，但我却没看到一只苍鹭。真奇怪，我想。苍鹭通常都在这里，成群结队地站着，一动不动，像哨兵一样，静静地守候着鱼群。
This is a time to be still. I decide to stop watching for the herons to arrive, and lie down on the warm sand, gazing upon the tall grasses swaying in the moist sea breezes, breathing in the clean, sweet scents of bayberry and pine. Lulled by the slow-lapping waves, I rest my eyes on the silver blue light of the rising crescent moon. I settle into a glowing sense of gratitude, remembering the immense generosity of all my comforting colleagues who have offered me their insights as well as their stories. One by one, I picture their kind faces and hear echoes of their voices. I adore each one of them and marvel at their wisdom.
这是静谧的时刻。我决定不再等待苍鹭的到来，而是躺在温暖的沙滩上，凝望着在潮湿海风中摇曳的高草，呼吸着月桂和松树清新甜美的香气。伴着轻柔的海浪声，我将目光投向冉冉升起的银蓝色新月。我沉浸在感恩的氛围中，想起所有给予我安慰的同事们，他们慷慨地分享了他们的见解和故事。我一个个地想起他们和蔼的面容，耳边仿佛回荡着他们的声音。我爱他们每一个人，并惊叹于他们的智慧。
A gust of wind grabs my attention and sprays a few tiny drops of the sea on my face. I sit up. I take off my shoes and step slowly into the cool, frothy water at the edge of the bay. So moved, and bursting with joy and gratitude, I begin to speak out loud my thanks to my comforting colleagues, friends, family, animals, and more. I speak in reverence for the providence of all my comforters.
一阵风吹来，卷起几滴海水，扑面而来。我坐起身，脱下鞋子，缓缓踏入海湾边缘清凉的泡沫海水中。我感动不已，心中充满喜悦和感激，开始大声感谢那些安慰我的同事、朋友、家人、动物们等等。我满怀敬畏地感谢所有给予我安慰的人。
First, I thank my comfort guides for what they have taught me, and for the distinct comforting qualities of their true natures:
首先，我要感谢我的良师益友们教会我的一切，以及他们真实本性中那些令人感到慰藉的独特品质：
Jeff, for his gift of deeply appreciating and respecting his patients as a nurse.
杰夫，因为他作为一名护士，对病人充满深深的感激和尊重。
Adrienne, for her integrity, humility, and wisdom in helping us communicate difficult things with our providers as well as our loved ones.
感谢艾德琳的正直、谦逊和智慧，她帮助我们与医护人员以及我们所爱的人沟通困难的事情。
Alicia, for teaching us to be real, to be ourselves with distressed families, and even with police departments.
感谢艾丽西亚教会我们真诚待人，在困境中的家庭面前，甚至在与警察部门相处时，都要保持真我。
Patricia, for showing us the healing power of our presence when grieving people need to be heard.
帕特里夏，感谢你向我们展示了在悲伤的人需要倾诉时，我们的陪伴所具有的治愈力量。
Hal, for his generosity, kindness, and genius for heart-to-heart conversation.
哈尔，因为他慷慨、善良，而且非常擅长进行深入的交谈。
Les, for finding common ground between all ages, cultures, and faiths with our stories.
莱斯，感谢你用我们的故事在不同年龄、文化和信仰之间找到共同点。
Amy, for her amazing grace under pressure, showing us how art helps us to go with the flow, even in hectic times.
艾米在压力下表现出的惊人优雅，向我们展示了艺术如何帮助我们顺其自然，即使在忙碌的时期也是如此。
Pam, for her validation of our journeys, and for shining a light on the gifts of our journeys.
感谢 Pam 对我们旅程的肯定，并让我们看到了旅程中的馈赠。
Don and Brenda and their dogs, for their unconditional love and acceptance.
感谢唐和布伦达以及他们的狗狗们给予的无条件的爱和接纳。
Nancy and her horses, for their clarity, honesty, and firmness.
南希和她的马，因为他们的清晰、诚实和坚定。
Laura and Whitney’s Cherry Tree, for showing us the comfort of continuity, keeping rituals, and our reliability in showing up for each other’s life passages.
劳拉和惠特尼的樱桃树，向我们展示了延续的慰藉、保持仪式感，以及在彼此人生阶段中互相扶持的可靠性。
Jen, for teaching us to take pause, to appreciate the radiance of stillness.
Jen，谢谢你教会我们停下来，欣赏静谧的光辉。
I thank more comforters of my life. My old friend Morna in Scotland across the ocean. My dear friends and family members in Virginia who have warmly and generously supported me. My newer friends in Maine, especially my friend Susan Neale, former publisher of the Maine Women’s Journal , who first provided an opportunity for me to write profiles of comforting and courageous women. And all the readers and reviewers of my book in its many, many versions and stages.
我还要感谢生命中给予我慰藉的人们。感谢远在苏格兰的老朋友莫娜；感谢我在弗吉尼亚的亲朋好友，他们给予了我热情慷慨的支持；感谢我在缅因州的新朋友们，特别是《缅因州妇女杂志》的前出版人苏珊·尼尔，她给了我机会去撰写那些令人感到慰藉和勇敢的女性的人物特写；还要感谢所有阅读和评论我这本书的读者和评论家，感谢你们见证了这本书的无数个版本和阶段。
The two wonderful people who guided, grounded, and encouraged me in bringing this book into the world: My editor at Tarcher/Penguin, Sara Carder, and my agent, Diane Freed.
两位出色的人指导、帮助和鼓励我完成了这本书：我在 Tarcher/Penguin 的编辑 Sara Carder 和我的经纪人 Diane Freed。
My favorite writers and artists who have created the books, movies, music, and paintings that kept my spirit alive through the harsh winter and give me faith in the genius of all our hearts.
我最喜欢的作家和艺术家们创作了书籍、电影、音乐和绘画，这些作品在严酷的寒冬中滋养了我的精神，并让我相信我们每个人心中都蕴藏着天才。
My beloved comforters in heaven, my cat Ivan, and my grandmother Viv.
我在天堂里最亲爱的安慰者，我的猫伊万，还有我的祖母薇薇。
And lunar moths, chickadees, and herons.
还有月蛾、山雀和苍鹭。
Comfort is all around me. I am never alone.
舒适感环绕着我。我从不孤单。
I step away from the water and turn toward the other side of the beach. There, glistening in the twilight on a rock, stands a magnificent blue heron, watching me closely. We behold each other for one moment, one that lives forever.
我离开水边，转身面向沙滩的另一边。只见一只美丽的蓝鹭栖息在岩石上，在暮色中闪闪发光，它正专注地注视着我。我们彼此凝视了片刻，那一瞬间却永恒难忘。
